author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: याऽइषवो यातुधानानां ये वा वनस्पतीँ१ऽरनु। ये वावटेषु शेरते तेभ्यः सर्पेभ्यो नमः ॥७ ॥
translation: To those that are the demons’ darts, to those that live upon the trees, To all the Serpents that lie low in holes be adoration paid.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ये वामी रोचने दिवो ये वा सूर्यस्य रश्मिषु। येषामप्सु सदस्कृतं तेभ्यः सर्पेभ्यो नमः ॥८ ॥
translation: Or those that are in heaven’s bright sphere, or those that dwell in the Sun’s beams: Serpents, whose home has been prepared in waters, homage unto them!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: कृणुष्व पाजः प्रसितिं न पृथ्वीं याहि राजेवामवाँ२ऽ इभेन। तृष्वीमनु प्रसितिं द्रूणानोऽस्तासि विध्य रक्षसस्तपिष्ठैः ॥९ ॥
translation: Put forth like a wide-spreading net thy vigour: go like a mighty King with his attendants. Thou, following thy swift net, shootest arrows: transfix the fiends with darts that burn most fiercely.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तव भ्रमासऽ आशुया पतन्त्यनु स्पृश धृषता शोशुचानः। तपूष्यग्ने जुह्वा पतङ्गानसन्दितो विसृज विष्वगुल्काः ॥१० ॥
translation: Forth go in rapid flight thy whirling weapons: follow them closely glowing in thy fury. Spread with thy tongue the wingèd flames, O Agni: unfettered cast thy firebrands all around thee.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: प्रति स्पशो विसृज तूर्णितमो भवा पायुर्विशोऽ अस्या अदब्धः। यो नो दूरेऽ अघशꣳसो योऽ अन्त्यग्ने माकिष्टे व्यथिरादधर्षीत् ॥११ ॥
translation: Send thy spies forward, fleetest in thy motion: be, ne’er deceived, the guardian of this people From him who, near or far, is bent on evil, and let no trouble sent from thee o’ercome us.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उदग्ने तिष्ठ प्रत्यातनुष्व न्यमित्राँ२ऽ ओषतात् तिग्महेते। यो नोऽ अरातिꣳ समिधान चक्रे नीचा तं धक्ष्यतसं न शुष्कम् ॥१२ ॥
translation: Rise up, O Agni, spread thee out before us, burn down our foes, thou who hast sharpened arrows. Him, blazing Agni! who hath worked us mischief, consume thou utterly like dried-up stubble.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वो भव प्रतिविध्याध्यस्मदाविष्कृणुष्व दैव्यान्यग्ने। अव स्थिरा तनुहि यातुजूनां जामिमजामिं प्रमृणीहि शत्रून्। अग्नेष्ट्वा तेजसा सादयामि ॥१३ ॥
translation: Rise, Agni, drive off those who fight against us: make manifest thine own celestial vigour. Slacken the strong bows of the demon-driven: destroy our foemen whether kin or stranger. I settle thee with Agni’s fiery ardour.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्निर्मूर्द्धा दिवः ककुत्पतिः पृथिव्याऽ अयम्। अपा रेतासि जिन्वति। इन्द्रस्य त्वौजसा सादयामि ॥१४ ॥
translation: Agni is head and height of heaven, the Master of the earth is he: He quickeneth the waters’ seed. I settle thee with the great strength of Indra.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: भुवो यज्ञस्य रजसश्च नेता यत्रा नियुद्भिः सचसे शिवाभिः। दिवि मूर्द्धानं दधिषे स्वर्षां जिह्वामग्ने चकृषे हव्यवाहम् ॥१५ ॥
translation: Thou art the leader of the rite and region to which with thine auspicious teams thou tendest. Thy light-bestowing head to heaven thou liftest, making thy tongue the oblation- bearer, Agni! 50
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ध्रुवासि धरुणास्तृता विश्वकर्मणा। मा त्वा समुद्रऽ उद्वधीन्मा सुपर्णोऽअव्यथमाना पृथिवीं दृꣳह ॥१६ ॥
translation: Steady art thou, sustainer, laid by Visvakarman in thy place. Let not the ocean nor the bird harm thee: unshaking, steady earth.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: प्रजापतिष्ट्वा सादयत्वपां पृष्ठे समुद्रस्येमन्। व्यचस्वतीं प्रथस्वतीं प्रथस्व पृथिव्यसि ॥१७ ॥
translation: Thee let Prajâpati settle on the waters’ back, in Ocean’s course, Thee the capacious, widely spread. Thou art the Wide One: spread thee wide
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: भूरसि भूमिरस्यदितिरसि विश्वधाया विश्वस्य भुवनस्य धर्त्री। पृथिवीं यच्छ पृथिवीं दृꣳह पृथिवीं मा हिꣳसीः ॥१८ ॥
translation: Thou art the earth, the ground, thou art the all-sustaining Aditi, she who supporteth all the world. Control the earth, steady the earth, do thou the earth no injury.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: विश्वस्मै प्राणायापानाय व्यानायोदानाय प्रतिष्ठायै चरित्राय। अग्निष्ट्वाभिपातु मह्या स्वस्त्या छर्दिषा शन्तमेन तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद् ध्रुवा सीद ॥१९ ॥
translation: For all breath, out-breath; through-breath, upward-breathing, for high position, for prescribed observance, May Agni keep thee safe with great well-being, with the securest shelter. As aforetime with Angiras, with that Deity lie steady.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: काण्डात्काण्डात्प्ररोहन्ती परुषःपरुषस्परि। एवा नो दूर्वे प्रतनु सहस्रेण शतेन च ॥२० ॥
translation: Upspringing from thine every joint, upspringing from each knot of thine, Thus with a thousand, Dûrvâ! with a hundred do thou stretch us out.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: या शतेन प्रतनोषि सहस्रेण विरोहसि। तस्यास्ते देवीष्टके विधेम हविषा वयम् ॥२१ ॥
translation: Thou spreading with a hundred, thou that branched with a thousand shoots, Thee, such, with our oblation will we worship, O celestial Brick.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यास्तेऽ अग्ने सूर्य्ये रुचो दिवमातन्वन्ति रश्मिभिः। ताभिर्नोऽ अद्य सर्वाभी रुचे जनाय नस्कृधि ॥२२ ॥
translation: Thy lights, O Agni, in the Sun that with their beams o’erspread the sky,— With all of those assist thou us to-day to light and progeny.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: या वो देवाः सूर्य्ये रुचो गोष्वश्वेषु या रुचः। इन्द्राग्नी ताभिः सर्वाभी रुचं नो धत्त बृहस्पते ॥२३ ॥
translation: Lights of yours in the Sun, O Gods, or lights that are in kine and steeds, O Indra-Agni, with all those vouchsafe us light, Brihaspati!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: विराड् ज्योतिरधारयत् स्वराड् ज्योतिरधारयत्। प्रजापतिष्ट्वा सादयतु पृष्ठे पृथिव्या ज्योतिष्मतीम्। विश्वस्मै प्राणायापानाय व्यानाय विश्वं ज्योतिर्यच्छ। अग्निष्टेऽधिपतिस्तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद् ध्रुवा सीद ॥२४ ॥
translation: The Far.-Refulgent held the light. The Self-Refulgent held the light. Thee, luminous, may Prajâpati settle upon the back of Earth. Give, to all breathing, all the light, to out-breath, to diffusive breath. Thy Sovran Lord is Agni. With that Deity, as with Angiras, lie firmly settled in thy place.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मधुश्च माधवश्च वासन्तिकावृतूऽ अग्नेरन्तः श्लेषोऽसि कल्पेतां द्यावापृथिवी कल्पन्तामापऽ ओषधयः कल्पन्तामग्नयः पृथङ् मम ज्यैष्ठ्याय सव्रताः। येऽ अग्नयः समनसोऽन्तरा द्यावापृथिवीऽ इमे। वासन्तिकावृतूऽ अभिकल्पमानाऽ इन्द्रमिव देवाऽ अभिसंविशन्तु तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद् ध्रुवे सीदतम् ॥२५ ॥
translation: Madhu and Mâdhava, the two Spring seasons—thou art the innermost cement of Agni. May Heaven and Earth, may Waters, Plants and Agnis help, separate, accordant, my precedence. May all the Fires ‘twixt heaven and earth, one-minded, well-fitted, gather round these two Spring seasons, As the Gods gathering encompass Indra: firm with that Deity, Angiras-like, be seated.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अषाढासि सहमाना सहस्वारातीः सहस्व पृतनायतः। सहस्रवीर्य्यासि सा मा जिन्व ॥२६ ॥
translation: Thou art Ashâdhâ, Conquering One. Conquer our foemen, conquer thou the men who fain would-fight with us. A thousand manly powers hast thou: so do thou aid and quicken me.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मधु वाताऽ ऋतायते मधु क्षरन्ति सिन्धवः। माध्वीर्नः सन्त्वोषधीः ॥२७ ॥
translation: The winds waft sweets, the rivers pour sweets for the man who keeps the Law: So may the plants be sweet for us.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मधु नक्तमुतोषसो मधुमत् पार्थिवꣳ रजः। मधु द्यौरस्तु नः पिता ॥२८ ॥
translation: Sweet be the night and sweet the dawns, sweet the terrestrial atmosphere: Sweet be our Father Heaven to us.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मधुमान्नो वनस्पतिर्मधुमाँ२ऽ अस्तु सूर्य्यः। माध्वीर्गावो भवन्तु नः ॥२९ ॥
translation: May the tall tree be full of sweets for us and, and full of sweets the Sun: May our milch- kine be sweet for us.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अपां गम्भन्त्सीद मा त्वा सूर्य्योऽभिताप्सीन्माग्निर्वैश्वानरः। अच्छिन्नपत्राः प्रजाऽ अनुवीक्षस्वानु त्वा दिव्या वृष्टिः सचताम् ॥३० ॥
translation: Seat thyself in the deepness of the waters, lest Sûrya, lest Vaisvânara Agni scorch thee. With wing unclipped, survey created beings: may rain that cometh down from heaven attend thee.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: त्रीन्त्समुद्रान्त्समसृपत् स्वर्गानपां पतिर्वृषभऽ इष्टकानाम्। पुरीषं वसानः सुकृतस्य लोके तत्र गच्छ यत्र पूर्वे परेताः ॥३१ ॥
translation: He crept across the three heaven-reaching oceans, the Bull of Bricks, the Master of the Waters. Clad in the world with his, the Well-Made’s, vesture, go whither those before thee have departed.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मही द्यौः पृथिवी च नऽ इमं यज्ञं मिमिक्षताम्। पिपृतां नो भरीमभिः ॥३२ ॥
translation: May Heaven and Earth, the Mighty Pair, besprinkle this our sacrifice, And feed us full with nourishments. 51
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: विष्णोः कर्माणि पश्यत यतो व्रतानि पस्पशे। इन्द्रस्य युज्यः सखा ॥३३ ॥
translation: Look ye on Vishnu’s works whereby the Friend of Indra, close allied, Hath let his holy ways be seen.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ध्रुवासि धरुणेतो जज्ञे प्रथममेभ्यो योनिभ्योऽअधि जातवेदाः। स गायत्र्या त्रिष्टुभाऽनुष्टुभा च देवेभ्यो हव्यं वहतु प्रजानन् ॥३४ ॥
translation: Firm art thou, a sustainer. Hence engendered, forth from these wombs at first came Jâtavedas. By Gâyatrî, by Trishtup, by Anushtup, may he who knows bear to the Gods oblation.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इषे राये रमस्व सहसे द्युम्नऽ ऊर्जेऽ अपत्याय। सम्राडसि स्वराडसि सारस्वतौ त्वोत्सौ प्रावताम् ॥३५ ॥
translation: Take thou thine ease for food, for store of riches, for might in splendour, and for strength and offspring. Thou art all-ruling, independent Ruler: both fountains of Sarasvatî protect thee!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्ने युक्ष्वा हि ये तवाश्वासो देव साधवः। अरं वहन्ति मन्यवे ॥३६ ॥
translation: O radiant Agni, harness thou thy steeds which are most excellent! They bear thee as thy spirit wills.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: युक्ष्वा हि देवहूतमाँ२ऽ अश्वाँ२ऽ अग्ने रथीरिव। नि होता पूर्व्यः सदः ॥३७ ॥
translation: Yoke, Agni, as a charioteer, thy steeds who best invoke the Gods: As ancient Hotar take thy seat.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सम्यक् स्रवन्ति सरितो न धेनाऽ अन्तर्हृदा मनसा पूयमानाः। घृतस्य धाराऽ अभिचाकशीमि हिरण्ययो वेतसो मध्येऽ अग्नेः ॥३८ ॥
translation: Like rivers our libations flow together, cleansing themselves in inmost heart and spirit. I look upon the flowing streams of butter: the golden reed is in the midst of Agni.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ऋचे त्वा रुचे त्वा भासे त्वा ज्योतिषे त्वा। अभूदिदं विश्वस्य भुवनस्य वाजिनमग्नेर्वैश्वानरस्य च ॥३९ ॥
translation: Thee for the praise-verse, thee for sheen, thee for bright splendour, thee for light. This hath become the energetic spirit of all the world and of Vaisvânara Agni.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्निर्ज्योतिषा ज्योतिष्मान् रुक्मो वर्चसा वर्चस्वान्। सहस्रदाऽ असि सहस्राय त्वा ॥४० ॥
translation: Agni, all-luminous with light, splendid with splendour, golden One. Giver of thousands art thou: for a thousand thee.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आदित्यं गर्भं पयसा समङ्धि सहस्रस्य प्रतिमां विश्वरूपम्। परिवृङ्धि हरसा माभि मꣳस्थाः शतायुषं कृणुहि चीयमानः ॥४१ ॥
translation: Balm thou with milk the unborn babe Âditya, wearing all forms, creator of a thousand. Spare, him with heat, nor plot against him: give him a hundred years of life while thou art building.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वातस्य जूतिं वरुणस्य नाभिमश्वं जज्ञानꣳ सरिरस्य मध्ये। शिशुं नदीना हरिमद्रिबुध्नमग्ने मा हिꣳसीः परमे व्योमन् ॥४२ ॥
translation: The wind’s impetuous rush, Varuna’s navel! the horse that springs to life amid the waters! The rivers’ tawny child, based on the mountain, harm not, O Agni, in the loftiest region.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अजस्रमिन्दुमरुषं भुरण्युमग्निमीडे पूर्वचित्तिं नमोभिः। स पर्वभिर्ऋतुशः कल्पमानो गां मा हिꣳसीरदितिं विराजम् ॥४३ ॥
translation: Unwasting Drop, red, eager, pressing forward, Agni I worship with repeated homage. Forming thyself with joints in proper order, harm not the Cow, Aditi widely ruling!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वरूत्रीं त्वष्टुर्वरुणस्य नाभिमविं जज्ञाना रजसः परस्मात्। मही साहस्रीमसुरस्य मायामग्ने मा हिसीः परमे व्योमन् ॥४४ ॥
translation: Her who is Tvashtar’s guardian, Varuna’s navel, the Ewe brought forth from out the loftiest region, The Asura’s mighty thousandfold contrivance, injure not in the highest sphere, O Agni.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: योऽ अग्निरग्नेरध्यजायत शोकात् पृथिव्याऽ उत वा दिवस्परि। येन प्रजा विश्वकर्मा जजान तमग्ने हेडः परि ते वृणक्तु ॥४५ ॥
translation: The Agni who from Agni had his being, from heat of Earth or also heat of Heaven, Whereby the Omnific One engendered creatures, him may thy fierce displeasure spare, O Agni.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: चित्रं देवानामुदगादनीकं चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याग्नेः। आ प्रा द्यावापृथिवीऽ अन्तरिक्षꣳ सूर्य्यऽ आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च ॥४६ ॥
translation: The brilliant presence of the Gods hath risen, the eye of Mitra, Varuna, and Agni. The soul of all that moveth not or moveth, the Sun hath filled the air, and earth and heaven.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इमं मा हिꣳसीर्द्विपादं पशुꣳ सहस्राक्षो मेधाय चीयमानः। मयुं पशुं मेधमग्ने जुषस्व तेन चिन्वानस्तन्वो निषीद। मयुं ते शुगृच्छतु यं द्विष्मस्तं ते शुगृच्छतु ॥४७ ॥
translation: Injure not, thousand-eyed, while thou art building for sacrifice, this animal, the biped. Accept as pith man’s counterfeit the victim, Agni: therewith building thy forms, be settled. Let thy flame reach man’s counterfeit: let thy flame reach the man we hate.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इमं मा हिꣳसीरेकशफं पशुं कनिक्रदं वाजिनं वाजिनेषु। गौरमारण्यमनु ते दिशामि तेन चिन्वानस्तन्वो निषीद। गौरं ते शुगृच्छतु यं द्विष्मस्तं ते शुगृच्छतु ॥४८ ॥
translation: Harm not this animal whose hooves are solid, the courser neighing in the midst of coursers. I dedicate to thee the forest Gaura: building thy bodies up with him be settled. Let thy flame reach the Gaura, let thy flame reach him whom we detest.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इमꣳ साहस्रꣳ शतधारमुत्सं व्यच्यमानꣳ सरिरस्य मध्ये। घृतं दुहानामदितिं जनायाग्ने मा हिꣳसीः परमे व्योमन्। गवयमारण्यमनु ते दिशामि तेन चिन्वानस्तन्वो निषीद। गवयं ते शुगृच्छतु यं द्विष्मस्तं ते शुगृच्छतु ॥४९ ॥
translation: Thousandfold, with a hundred streams, this fountain, expanded in the middle of the waters, Infinite, yielding butter for the people, harm not, O Agni, in the highest region. This wild bull of the forest I assign thee: building thy bodies up therewith be settled. Let thy flame reach the wild hull, etc. (as in 48). 52
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इममूर्णायुं वरुणस्य नाभिं त्वचं पशूनां द्विपदां चतुष्पदाम्। त्वष्टुः प्रजानां प्रथमं जनित्रमग्ने मा हिꣳसीः परमे व्योमन्। उष्ट्रमारण्यमनु ते दिशामि तेन चिन्वानस्तन्वो निषीद। उष्ट्रं ते शुगृच्छतु यं द्विष्मस्तं ते शुगृच्छतु ॥५० ॥
translation: This creature clothed in wool, Varuna’s navel, the skin of animals quadruped and biped, The first that was produced of Tvashtar’s creatures, O Agni, harm not in the highest region. The forest buffalo do I assign thee: building, etc., as above mutato mutando.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अजो ह्यग्नेरजनिष्ट शोकात् सोऽ अपश्यज्जनितारमग्रे। तेन देवा देवतामग्रमायँस्तेन रोहमायन्नुप मेध्यासः। शरभमारण्यमनु ते दिशामि तेन चिन्वानस्तन्वो निषीद। शरभं ते शुगृच्छतु यं द्विष्मस्तं ते शुगृच्छतु ॥५१ ॥
translation: From Agni’s warmth the he-goat had his being: he looked at first upon his generator. Thereby the Gods at first attained to Godhead: those meet for worship to the height ascended. The forest Sarabha do I assign thee: building, etc. 52 Do thou, Most Youthful God, protect the men who offer, hear their songs, Protect his offspring and himself.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अपां त्वेमन्त्सादयाम्यपां त्वोद्मन्सादयाम्यपां त्वा भस्मन्त्सादयाम्यपां त्वा ज्योतिषि सादयाम्यपां त्वायने सादयाम्यर्णवे त्वा सदने सादयामि समुद्रे त्वा सदने सादयामि। सरिरे त्वा सदने सादयाम्यपां त्वा क्षये सादयाम्यपां त्वा सधिषि सादयाम्यपां त्वा सदने सादयाम्यपां त्वा सधस्थे सादयाम्यपां त्वा योनौ सादयाम्यपां त्वा पुरीषे सादयाम्यपां त्वा पाथसि सादयामि। गायत्रेण त्वा छन्दसा सादयामि त्रैष्टुभेन त्वा छन्दसा सादयामि जागतेन त्वा छन्दसा सादयाम्यानुष्टुभेन त्वा छन्दसा सादयामि पाङ्क्तेन त्वा छन्दसा सादयामि ॥५३ ॥
translation: I set thee in the passage of the waters. I set thee in the swelling of the waters. I set thee in the ashes of the waters. I set thee in the lustre of the waters. I set thee in the way which waters travel. I set thee in the flood, the place to test in. I set thee in the sea, the place to rest in. I set thee in the stream, the place to rest in. I set thee in the water’s habitation. I set thee in the resting-place of waters. I set thee in the station of the waters. I set thee in the meeting- place of waters. I set thee in the birthplace of the waters. I set thee in the refuse of the waters. I set thee in the residence of waters. I settle thee with the Gâyatrî metre. I settle thee with the Trishtup metre. I settle thee with the Jagatî metre. I settle thee with the Anushtup metre. I settle thee with the Pankti metre.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अयं पुरो भुवस्तस्य प्राणो भौवायनो वसन्तः प्राणायनो गायत्री वासन्ती गायत्र्यै गायत्रं गायत्रादुपाशुरुपाशोस्त्रिवृत् त्रिवृतो रथन्तरं वसिष्ठऽ ऋषिः। प्रजापतिगृहीतया त्वया प्राणं गृह्णामि प्रजाभ्यः ॥५४ ॥
translation: This, in front, is Bhuva. His offspring, Breath, is Bhauvâyana. Spring is Prânâyana. The Gâyatrî is the daughter of Spring. From the Gâyatrî comes the Gâyatra tune. From the Gâyatra the Upâmsu. From the Upâmsu the Trivrit. From the Trivrit the Rathantara. The Rishi Vasishtha. By thee, taken by Prajâpati, I take vital breath for creatures.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अयं दक्षिणा विश्वकर्मा तस्य मनो वैश्वकर्मणं ग्रीष्मो मानसस्त्रिष्टुब् ग्रैष्मी त्रिष्टुभः स्वारꣳ स्वारादन्तर्य्यामोऽन्तर्यामात् पञ्चदशः पञ्चदशाद् बृहद् भरद्वाजऽ ऋषिः प्रजापतिगृहीतया त्वया मनो गृह्णामि प्रजाभ्यः ॥५५ ॥
translation: This on the right, the Omnific. His, the Omnific’s offspring, Mind. Summer sprang from Mind. The Trishtup is the daughter of Summer. From the Trishtup came the Svâra song. From the Svâra the Antaryâma. From the Antaryâma the Pañchadasa. From the Pañchadasa the Brihat. The Rishi Bharadvâja. By thee, taken by Prajâpati, I take Mind for creatures.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अयं पश्चाद् विश्वव्यचास्तस्य चक्षुर्वैश्वव्यचसं वर्षाश्चाक्षुष्यो जगती वार्षी जगत्याऽ ऋक्सममृक्समाच्छुक्रः शुक्रात् सप्तदशः सप्तदशाद् वैरूपं जमदग्निर्ऋषिः प्रजापतिगृहीतया त्वया चक्षुर्गृह्णामि प्रजाभ्यः ॥५६ ॥
translation: This on the western side, the All-Embracer. His, the All-Embracer’s offspring, the Eye. The Rains sprang from the Eye. The Jagatî is the daughter of the Rains. From the Jagatî came the Riksama. From the Riksama the Sukra. From the Sukra the Saptadasa. From the Saptadasa the Vairûpa. The Rishi Jamadagni. By thee, taken by Prajâpati, I take the Eye for creatures.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इदमुत्तरात् स्वस्तस्य श्रोत्रꣳ सौवꣳ शरछ्रौत्र्यनुष्टुप् शारद्यनुष्टुभऽ ऐडमैडान् मन्थी मन्थिनऽ एकविꣳशऽ एकविꣳशाद् वैराजं विश्वामित्रऽ ऋषिः प्रजापतिगृहीतया त्वया श्रोत्रं गृह्णामि प्रजाभ्यः ॥५७ ॥
translation: This on the north side, heaven. This, heaven’s offspring, the Ear. Autumn, the daughter of the Ear. The Anushtup sprang from Autumn. From the Anushtup came the Aida. From the Aida the Manthin. From the Manthin the Ekavimsa. From the Ekavimsa the Vairâja. The Rishi Visvâmitra. By thee, taken by Prajâpati, I take the Ear for creatures.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इयमुपरि मतिस्तस्यै वाङ्मात्या हेमन्तो वाच्यः पङ्क्तिर्हैमन्ती पङ्क्त्यै निधनवन्निधनवतऽ आग्रयणऽ आग्रयणात् त्रिणवत्रयस्त्रिꣳशौ त्रिणवत्रयस्त्रिꣳशाभ्या शाक्वररैवते विश्वकर्मऽ ऋषिः प्रजापतिगृहीतया त्वया वाचं गृह्णामि प्रजाभ्यः ॥५८ ॥
translation: This above, Intellect. Its, Intellect’s offspring, Speech. Winter the offspring of Speech. Pankti sprang from Winter. From Pankti the Nidhanavat. From the Nidhanavat came the Âgrayana. From the Âgrayana the Trinava and the Trayastrimsa. From the Trinava and the Trayastrimsa the Sâkvara and the Raivata. The Rishi Visvakarman. By thee, taken by Visvakarman, I take Speech for people. Fill up the room, etc. The dappled kine, etc. All sacred songs, etc., three texts repeated from XII. 54-56. 53
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ध्रुवक्षितिर्ध्रुवयोनिर्ध्रुवासि ध्रुवं योनिमासीद साधुया। उख्यस्य केतुं प्रथमं जुषाणाऽ अश्विनाऽध्वर्यू सादयतामिह त्वा ॥१ ॥
translation: WITH stedfast site and birthplace thou art stedfast: settle thou duly in thy stedfast birthplace, rejoicing in the Ukhya’s first appearance. Here let the Asvins, the Adhvaryus, seat thee.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: कुलायिनी घृतवती पुरन्धिः स्योने सीद सदने पृथिव्याः। अभि त्वा रुद्रा वसवो गृणन्त्विमा ब्रह्म पीपिहि सौभगायाश्विनाध्वर्यू सादयतामिह त्वा ॥२ ॥
translation: Nesting, intelligent, dripping with butter, in the auspicious seat of earth be seated. Let Rudras, Vasus welcome thee with praises: fill full these prayers for our propitious fortune. Here let the Asvins, the Adhvaryus, seat thee.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: स्वैर्दक्षैर्दक्षपितेह सीद देवानासुम्ने बृहते रणाय। पितेवैधि सूनवऽआ सुशेवा स्वावेशा तन्वा संविशस्वाश्विनाध्वर्यू सादयतामिह त्वा ॥३ ॥
translation: Here, Guard of Strength, with thine own powers be seated for the Gods’ happiness and great enjoyment. Even as a father to his son, be friendly: with easy entrance enter with thy body. Here let the Asvins, the Adhvaryus seat thee:
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: पृथिव्याः पुरीषमस्यप्सो नाम तां त्वा विश्वेऽअभिगृणन्तु देवाः। स्तोमपृष्ठा घृतवतीह सीद प्रजावदस्मे द्रविणा यजस्वाश्विनाध्वर्यू सादयतामिह त्वा ॥४ ॥
translation: Thou art the filling-stuff of earth called Apsas. May all the Gods celebrate thee with praises. Enriched with songs of praise, Prishthas and butter, sit here and give us wealth with store of children. Here let the Asvins, etc.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अदित्यास्त्वा पृष्ठे सादयाम्यन्तरिक्षस्य धर्त्रीं विष्टम्भनीं दिशामधिपत्नीं भुवनानाम्। ऊर्मिर्द्रप्सोऽअपामसि विश्वकर्मा तऽऋषिरश्विनाध्वर्यू सादयतामिह त्वा ॥५ ॥
translation: Upon the back of Aditi I lay thee the sky’s supporter, pillar of the Quarters, Queen over creatures. Wave and drop of waters art thou; and Visvakarman is thy Rishi.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: शुक्रश्च शुचिश्च ग्रैष्मावृतूऽ अग्नेरन्तःश्लेषोऽसि कल्पेतां द्यावापृथिवी कल्पन्तामापऽ ओषधयः कल्पन्तामग्नयः पृथङ् मम ज्यैष्ठ्याय सव्रताः। येऽअग्नयः समनसोऽन्तरा द्यावापृथिवीऽइमे। ग्रैष्मावृतूऽ अभिकल्पमानाऽइन्द्रमिव देवाऽअभिसंविशन्तु तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद् ध्रुवे सीदतम् ॥६ ॥
translation: Sukra and Suchi, seasons, both, of summer—thou art the innermost cement of Agni. May Heaven and Earth, may Waters, Plants and Agnis help, separate, accordant, my precedence. Let all the Agnis ‘twixt the earth and heaven gather together round these summer seasons, as the Gods gather in their hosts round Indra, Firm, with that Deity, Angiras-like, be seated.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सजूर्ऋतुभिः सजूर्विधाभिः सजूर्देवैः सजूर्देवैर्वयोनाधैरग्नये त्वा वैश्वानरायाश्विनाध्वर्यू सादयतामिह त्वा सजूर्ऋतुभिः सजूर्विधाभिः सजूर्वसुभिः सजूर्देवैर्वयोनाधैरग्नये त्वा वैश्वानरायाश्विनाऽध्वर्यू सादयतामिह त्वा सजूर्ऋतुभिः सजूर्विधाभिः सजू रुद्रैः सजूर्देवैर्वयोनाधैरग्नये त्वा वैश्वानरायाश्विनाध्वर्यू सादयतामिह त्वा सजूर्ऋतुभिः सजूर्विधाभिः सजूरादित्यैः सजूर्देवैर्वयोनाधैरग्नये त्वा वैश्वानरायाश्विनाध्वर्यू सादयतामिह त्वा सजूर्ऋतुभिः सजूर्विधाभिः सजूर्विश्वैर्देवैः सजूर्देवैर्वयोनाधैरग्नये त्वा वैश्वानरायाश्विनाध्वर्यू सादयतामिह त्वा ॥७ ॥
translation: Associate with the Seasons, with the Modes with the Gods, with the health-establishing Gods—may the Asvins the Adhvaryus settle thee here for Agni Vaisvânara. Associate.............with the Vasus, etc. Associate.............with the Rudras, etc. Associate.............with the Âdityas, etc. Associate.............with the Visvedevas, etc.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: प्राणम्मे पाह्यपानम्मे पाहि व्यानम्मे पाहि चक्षुर्मऽउर्व्या विभाहि श्रोत्रम्मे श्लोकय। अपः पिन्वौषधीर्जिन्व द्विपादव चतुष्पात् पाहि दिवो वृष्टिमेरय ॥८ ॥
translation: Guard thou my breath. Guard my out-breathing. Guard my through-breathing. Illume mine eye with far-reaching vision. Give power of hearing to mine ear. Pour forth waters. Quicken plants. Protect bipeds. Protect quadrupeds. Send rain from heaven.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मूर्धा वयः प्रजापतिश्छन्दः क्षत्रं वयो मयन्दं छन्दो विष्टम्भो वयोऽधिपतिश्छन्दो विश्वकर्मा वयः परमेष्ठी छन्दो बस्तो वयो विबलं छन्दो वृष्णिर्वयो विशालं छन्दः पुरुषो वयस्तन्द्रं छन्दो व्याघ्रो वयोऽनाधृष्टं छन्दः सिꣳहो वयश्छदिश्छन्दः पष्ठवाड् वयो बृहती छन्दऽ उक्षा वयः ककुप् छन्दऽ ऋषभो वयः सतोबृहती छन्दः ॥९ ॥
translation: The head is vital vigour. Prajâpati became the metre. Royalty is vital vigour, health-giving metre. The Supporter is vital vigour, the Sovran Lord the metre. Visvakarman is vital vigour, Parameshthin the metre. The he-goat is vital vigour, excellent the metre. The bull is vital vigour, extensive the metre. Man is vital vigour, languid the metre. The tiger is vital vigour, invincible the metre. The lion is vital vigour, covering the metre. The four-year bull is vital vigour, Brihatî the metre. The ox is vital vigour, Kakup the metre. The steer is vital vigour, Satobrihatî the metre.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अनड्वान् वयः पङ्क्तिश्छन्दो धेनुर्वयो जगती छन्दस्त्र्यविर्वयस्त्रिष्टुप् छन्दो दित्यवाड् वयो विराट् छन्दः पञ्चाविर्वयो गायत्री छन्दस्त्रिवत्सो वयऽउष्णिक् छन्दस्तुर्य्यवाड् वयोऽनुष्टुप् छन्दः ॥१० ॥
translation: The bullock is vital vigour, Pankti the metre. The milch-cow is vital vigour, Jagatî the metre. The eighteen-month calf is vital vigour, Trishtup the metre. The two year old steer is vital vigour, Virâj the metre. The thirty-month old ewe is vital vigour, Gâyatrî the metre. The three year old steer is vital vigour, Ushnih the metre. The four year old ox is vital vigour, Anushtup the metre. Fill up the room, etc. The dappled kine, etc. All sacred songs, etc. are three texts repeated from XII. 54-56. See also XIII. 58.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इन्द्राग्नीऽ अव्यथमानामिष्टकां दृꣳहतं युवम्। पृष्ठेन द्यावापृथिवीऽ अन्तरिक्षं च विबाधसे ॥११ ॥
translation: Indra and Agni, in its place securely set the unshaking brick. Thou with thy back sunderest heaven and the broad earth and firmament.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: विश्वकर्मा त्वा सादयत्वन्तरिक्षस्य पृष्ठे व्यचस्वतीं प्रथस्वतीमन्तरिक्षं यच्छान्तरिक्षं दृꣳहान्तरिक्षं मा हिꣳसीः। विश्वस्मै प्राणायाऽपानाय व्यानायोदानाय प्रतिष्ठायै चरित्राय। वायुष्ट्वाभिपातु मह्या स्वस्त्या छर्दिषा शन्तमेन तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद् ध्रुवा सीद ॥१२ ॥
translation: On the air’s back let Visvakarman set thee, thee the capacious, thee the far-extended. Control the air, fix firm the air, do thou the air no injury. For all breath, out-breath, through- 54 breath, upward breathing, for high position, for prescribed observance, May Vâyu keep thee safe with great well-being, with securest shelter. In the manner of Angiras, with that Deity lie steady.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: राज्ञ्यसि प्राची दिग्विराडसि दक्षिणा दिक् सम्राडसि प्रतीची दिक् स्वराडस्युदीची दिगधिपत्न्यसि बृहती दिक् ॥१३ ॥
translation: Queen art thou, Quarter of the East. Wide-ruler, Quarter of the South. West Quarter, thou art Sovran. Thou Autocrat, Quarter of the North. Queen Paramount art thou, the Lofty Point.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: विश्वकर्मा त्वा सादयत्वन्तरिक्षस्य पृष्ठे ज्योतिष्मतीम्। विश्वस्मै प्राणायाऽपानाय व्यानाय विश्वं ज्योतिर्यच्छ। वायुष्टेऽधिपतिस्तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद् ध्रुवा सीद ॥१४ ॥
translation: On the air’s back may Visvakarman set thee luminous. Control all light for all breath, for out-breath, up-breath, through-breath. Thy Lord is Vâyu, with that Deity, Angiras-like, lie firm.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नभश्च नभस्यश्च वार्षिकावृतूऽ अग्नेरन्तःश्लेषोऽसि कल्पेतां द्यावापृथिवी कल्पन्तामापऽ ओषधयः कल्पन्तामग्नयः पृथङ् मम ज्यैष्ठ्याय सव्रताः। येऽअग्नयः समनसोऽन्तरा द्यावापृथिवीऽ इमे। वार्षिकावृतूऽ अभिकल्पमानाऽ इन्द्रमिव देवाऽ अभिसंविशन्तु तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद् ध्रुवे सीदतम् ॥१५ ॥
translation: Two Rainy Seasons, Nabhas and Nabhasya—thou art the innermost cement of Agni, etc. (as in XIII. 25).
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इषश्चोर्जश्च शारदावृतूऽ अग्नेरन्तःश्लेषोऽसि कल्पेतां द्यावापृथिवी कल्पन्तामापऽ ओषधयः कल्पन्तामग्नयः पृथङ् मम ज्यैष्ठ्याय सव्रताः। येऽ अग्नयः समनसोऽन्तरा द्यावापृथिवीऽ इमे। शारदावृतूऽ अभिकल्पमानाऽ इन्द्रमिव देवाऽ अभिसंविशन्तु तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद् ध्रुवे सीदतम् ॥१६ ॥
translation: Isha and Ûrja, two Autumnal Seasons—thou art the innermost cement of Agni, etc.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आयुर्मे पाहि प्राणं मे पाह्यपानं मे पाहि व्यानं मे पाहि चक्षुर्मे पाहि श्रोत्रं मे पाहि वाचं मे पिन्व मनो मे जिन्वात्मानं मे पाहि ज्योतिर्मे यच्छ ॥१७ ॥
translation: Preserve my life. Preserve my breath. Guard mine out-breath. Preserve mine eyes. Preserve mine ears. Strengthen my voice. Quicken my mind. Preserve my self. Vouchsafe me light.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मा छन्दः प्रमा छन्दः प्रतिमा छन्दोऽ अस्रीवयश्छन्दः पङ्क्तिश्छन्दऽ उष्णिक् छन्दो बृहती छन्दोऽनुष्टुप् छन्दो विराट् छन्दो गायत्री छन्दस्त्रिष्टुप् छन्दो जगती छन्दः ॥१८ ॥
translation: Mâ metre. Pramâ metre. Pratimâ metre. Âsrivayas metre. Pankti metre. Ushnih metre. Brihatî metre. Anushtup metre. Virâj metre. Gâyatrî metre, Trishtup metre. Jagatî metre.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: पृथिवी छन्दोऽन्तरिक्षं छन्दो द्यौश्छन्दः समाश्छन्दो नक्षत्राणि छन्दो वाक् छन्दो मनश्छन्दः कृषिश्छन्दो हिरण्यं छन्दो गौश्छन्दोऽजाच्छन्दोऽश्वश्छन्दः ॥१९ ॥
translation: Earth metre. Sky metre. Heaven metre. Years metre. Nakshatras metre. Vâk metre. Mind metre. Husbandry metre. Gold metre. Cow metre. She-goat metre. Horse metre.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्निर्देवता वातो देवता सूर्यो देवता चन्द्रमा देवता वसवो देवता रुद्रा देवताऽऽदित्या देवता मरुतो देवता विश्वे देवा देवता बृहस्पतिर्देवतेन्द्रो देवता वरुणो देवता ॥२० ॥
translation: The Deity Agni. The Deity Vita. The Deity Sûrya. The Deity Moon. The Deity Vasus. The Deity Rudras. The Deity Âdityas The Deity Maruts. The Deity Visvedevas. The Deity Brihaspati. The Deity Indra. The Deity Varuna.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मूर्द्धासि राड् ध्रुवासि धरुणा धर्त्र्यसि धरणी। आयुषे त्वा वर्चसे त्वा कृष्यै त्वा क्षेमाय त्वा ॥२१ ॥
translation: Chief art thou, bright, supporting, firm, thou art the great sustainer, Earth. Thee for life, thee for lustre, thee for tillage, thee for peace and rest.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यन्त्री राड् यन्त्र्यसि यमनी ध्रुवासि धरित्री। इषे त्वोर्जे त्वा रय्यै त्वा पोषाय त्वा ॥२२ ॥
translation: Controller, brilliant art thou, managing controller, firm sustainer. For strength, for energy thee, for riches thee, for prosperity thee. Fill up the room, etc. The dappled kine, etc. All sacred songs, etc. (as in 10).
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आशुस्त्रिवृद्भान्तः पञ्चदशो व्योमा सप्तदशो धरुणऽ एकविꣳशः प्रतूर्त्तिरष्टादशस्तपो नवदशोऽभीवर्त्तः सविꣳशो वर्चो द्वाविꣳशः सम्भरणस्त्रयोविꣳशो योनिश्चतुर्विꣳशो गर्भाः पञ्चविꣳशऽ ओजस्त्रिणवः क्रतुरेकत्रिꣳशः प्रतिष्ठा त्रयस्त्रिꣳशो ब्रध्नस्य विष्टपं चतुस्त्रिꣳशो नाकः षट्त्रिꣳशो विवर्तोऽष्टाचत्वारिꣳशो धर्त्रं चतुष्टोमः ॥२३ ॥
translation: This Swift, the triple praise-song. The Shining, the Pañchadasa hymn. Heaven, the Saptadasa. The Supporter, the Ekavimsa. Speed, the Ashtâdasa. Ardour, the Navadasa. Triumphant Onset, Savimsa, Vigour, Dvâvimsa. Maintenance, Trayovimsa. Womb, Chaturvimsa. Embryos, Pañchavimsa. Energy, the Trinava. Intention, the Ekatrimsa. The Basis, the Trayastrimsa. The Bright One’s Station, the Chatustrimsa. The Vault of Heaven, the Shattrimsa. The Revolving One, the Ashtâchatvârimsa. The Support, the Four-divisioned praise-song.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्नेर्भागोऽसि दीक्षायाऽ आधिपत्यं ब्रह्म स्पृतं त्रिवृत्स्तोमऽ इन्द्रस्य भागोऽसि विष्णोराधिपत्यं क्षत्रꣳ स्पृतं पञ्चदश स्तोमो नृचक्षसां भागोऽसि धातुराधिपत्यं जनित्रꣳ स्पृतꣳ सप्तदश स्तोमो मित्रस्य भागोऽसि वरुणस्याधिपत्यं दिवो वृष्टिर्वात स्पृतऽ एकविꣳश स्तोमः ॥२४ ॥
translation: Thou art the portion of Agni, chief control of Consecration. The Priesthood is saved; the Trivrit Stoma. Thou art the portion of Indra, the sovranty of Vishnu. The Nobility is saved; the Pañchadasa Stoma. Thou art the share of the Man-beholders; the supremacy of the Creator; the birthplace is saved; the Saptadasa Stoma. Thou art the share of Mitra, the sovranty of Varuna. Rain of heaven and wind are saved; the Ekavimsa Stoma.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वसूनां भागोऽसि रुद्राणामाधिपत्यं चतुष्पात् स्पृतं चतुर्विꣳश स्तोमऽ आदित्यानां भागोऽसि मरुतामाधिपत्यं गर्भा स्पृताः पंचविꣳश स्तोमोऽदित्यै भागोऽसि पूष्णऽ आधिपत्यमोज स्पृतं त्रिणव स्तोमो देवस्य सवितुर्भागोऽसि बृहस्पतेराधिपत्यꣳ समीचीर्दिश स्पृताश्चतुष्टोम स्तोमः ॥२५ ॥
translation: Thou art the share of the Vasus, the sovranty of the Rudras. Quadrupeds are saved; the Chaturvimsa Stoma. Thou art the share of the Âdityas; the sovranty of the Maruts. The Embryos are saved; the Pañchavimsa Stoma. Thou art the share of Aditi; the sovranty of Pûshan. Strength is saved; the Trinava Stoma. Thou art the share of God Savitar; the sovranty of Brihaspati. The universal Quarters are saved; the Chatushtoma Stoma. 55
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यवानां भागोऽस्ययवानामाधिपत्यं प्रजा स्पृताश्चतुश्चत्वारिꣳश स्तोमऽ ऋभूणां भागोऽसि विश्वेषां देवानामाधिपत्यं भूतꣳ स्पृतं त्रयस्त्रिꣳश स्तोमः ॥२६ ॥
translation: Thou art the share of the Yavas; the sovranty of the Ayavas. Creatures are saved; the Chatuschatvârimsa Stoma. Thou art the share of the Ribhus; the sovranty of the Visvedevas. The Being is saved; the Trayastrimsa Stoma.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सहश्च सहस्यश्च हैमन्तिकावृतूऽ अग्नेरन्तःश्लेषोऽसि कल्पेतां द्यावापृथिवी कल्पन्तामापऽ ओषधयः कल्पन्तामग्नयः पृथङ् मम ज्यैष्ठ्याय सव्रताः। येऽ अग्नयः समनसोऽन्तरा द्यावापृथिवीऽ इमे। हैमन्तिकावृतूऽ अभिकल्पमानाऽ इन्द्रमिव देवाऽ अभिसंविशन्तु तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद् ध्रुवे सीदतम् ॥२७ ॥
translation: Sahas, Sahasya, the two Winter Seasons—thou art the innermost cement of Agni, etc. (as in XIII. 25).
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: एकयास्तुवत प्रजाऽ अधीयन्त प्रजापतिरधिपतिरासीत्। तिसृभिरस्तुवत ब्रह्मासृज्यत ब्रह्मणस्पतिरधिपतिरासीत्। पञ्चभिरस्तुवत भूतान्यसृज्यन्त भूतानां पतिरधिपतिरासीत्। सप्तभिरस्तुवत सप्तऽ ऋषयोऽसृज्यन्त धाताधिपतिरासीत् ॥२८ ॥
translation: With one they praised; creatures were produced. Prajâpati was over-lord. With three they praised; the Priesthood was created. Brihaspati was over-lord. With five they praised; beings were created. The Lord of Beings was over-lord. With seven they praised; the Seven Rishis were created. Dhâtar was over-lord.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नवभिरस्तुवत पितरोऽसृज्यन्तादितिरधिपत्न्यासीत्। एकादशभिरस्तुवतऽ ऋतवोऽसृज्यन्तार्त्तवाऽ अधिपतयऽआसन्। त्रयोदशभिरस्तुवत मासाऽ असृज्यन्त संवत्सरोऽधिपतिरासीत्। पञ्चदशभिरस्तुवत क्षत्रमसृज्यतेन्द्रोऽधिपतिरासीत्। सप्तदशभिरस्तुवत ग्राम्याः पशवोऽसृज्यन्त बृहस्पतिरधिपतिरासीत् ॥२९ ॥
translation: With nine they praised; the Fathers were created. Aditi was Sovran Lady. With eleven they praised; the Seasons were created. The Season-Lords were over-lords. With thirteen they praised; the Months were created. The Year was over-lord. With fifteen they praised; the Nobility was created. Indra was over-lord. With seventeen they praised; domestic animals were created. Brihaspati was over-lord.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नवदशभिरस्तुवत शूद्रार्य्यावसृज्येतामहोरात्रेऽ अधिपत्नीऽ आस्ताम्। एकविꣳशत्यास्तुवतैकशफाः पशवोऽसृज्यन्त वरुणोऽधिपतिरासीत्। त्रयोविꣳशत्यास्तुवत क्षुद्राः पशवोऽसृज्यन्त पूषाधिपतिरासीत्। पञ्चविꣳशत्यास्तुवताऽऽरण्याः पशवोऽसृज्यन्त वायुरधिपतिरासीत्। सप्तविꣳशत्यास्तुवत द्यावापृथिवी व्यैतां वसवो रुद्रोऽ आदित्याऽ अनुव्यायँस्तऽ एवाधिपतयऽ आसन् ॥३० ॥
translation: With nineteen they praised; Sûdra and Arya were created. Day and Night were Sovran Ladies. With twenty-one they praised; solid-hoofed animals were created. Varuna was over- lord. With twenty-three they praised; small animals were created. Pûshan was over-lord. With twenty-five they praised; forest animals were created. Vâyu was over-lord. With twenty- seven they praised; earth and heaven came apart. Vasus, Rudras, Âdityas followed separately, so they were over-lords.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नवविꣳशत्याऽस्तुवत वनस्पतयोऽसृज्यन्त सोमोऽधिपतिरासीत्। एकत्रिꣳशताऽस्तुवत प्रजाऽ असृज्यन्त यवाश्चायवाश्चाधिपतयऽआसन्। त्रयस्त्रिꣳशताऽस्तुवत भूतान्यशाम्यन् प्रजापतिः परमेष्ठ्यधिपतिरासीत् ॥३१ ॥
translation: With twenty-nine they praised; Trees were created. Soma was over-lord. With thirty-one they praised; creatures were created. The Yavas and the Ayavas were over-lords. With thirty- three they praised; living beings. were happy. Prajâpati, the Supreme in Place, was over-lord. Fill up the room, etc. The dappled kine, etc. All sacred songs, etc. Repeated from XII. 14-16. 56
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्ने जातान् प्र णुदा नः सपत्नान् प्रत्यजातान् नुद जातवेदः। अधि नो ब्रूहि सुमनाऽअहेडँस्तव स्याम शर्मꣳस्त्रिवरूथऽउद्भौ ॥१ ॥
translation: DRIVE our born enemies away, O Agni; drive from us foes unborn, O Jâtavedas. Graciously- minded, free from anger, bless us: may we enjoy my firm thrice-guarding shelter. Drive off with might our foemen born and living: keep off these yet unborn, O Jâtavedas. Benevolent in thought and spirit bless us. May we remain alive: drive off our foemen.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: षोडशी स्तोमऽओजो द्रविणं चतुश्चत्वारिꣳश स्तोमो वर्चो द्रविणम्। अग्नेः पुरीषमस्यप्सो नाम तां त्वा विश्वेऽअभिगृणन्तु देवाः। स्तोमपृष्ठा घृतवतीह सीद प्रजावदस्मे द्रविणा यजस्व ॥३ ॥
translation: The Sixteenfold Stoma, strength and wealth. The Forty- fourth Stoma, splendour and wealth. Apsas art thou, the complement of Agni. As such may all the Gods greet thee with praises. Enriched with songs of praise, Prishthas, and butter, sit here and give us wealth with store of children.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: एवश्छन्दो वरिवश्छन्दः शम्भूश्छन्दः परिभूश्छन्दऽआच्छच्छन्दो मनश्छन्दो व्यचश्छन्दः सिन्धुश्छन्दः समुद्रश्छन्दः सरिरं छन्दः ककुप् छन्दस्त्रिककुप् छन्दः काव्यं छन्दोऽअङ्कुपं छन्दोऽक्षरपङ्क्तिश्छन्दः पदपङ्क्तिश्छन्दो विष्टारपङ्क्तिश्छन्दः क्षुरश्छन्दो भ्रजश्छन्दः ॥४ ॥
translation: Course metre. Space metre. Happy metre, Encompassing metre. Covering metre. Mind metre. Expanse metre. River metre. Sea metre. Water metre. Kakup metre. Trikakup metre. Kâvya metre. Ankupa metre Aksharapankti metre. Padapankti metre. Vishtârapankti metre. Kshurabhrâja metre.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आच्छच्छन्दः प्रच्छच्छन्दः संयच्छन्दो वियच्छन्दो बृहच्छन्दो रथन्तरञ्छन्दो निकायश्छन्दो विवधश्छन्दो गिरश्छन्दो भ्रजश्छन्दः सꣳस्तुप् छन्दोऽनुष्टुप् छन्दऽएवश्छन्दो वरिवश्छन्दो वयश्छन्दो वयस्कृच्छन्दो विष्पर्द्धाश्छन्दो विशालं छन्दश्छदिश्छन्दो दूरोहणं छन्दस्तन्द्रं छन्दोऽअङ्काङ्कं छन्दः ॥५ ॥
translation: Covering metre. Clothing metre. Collecting metre. Parting metre. Brihat metre. Rathantara metre, Group metre. Vivadhra metre. Swallower metre. Bright metre. Samstup metre. Anushtup metre. Course metre. Space metre. Vigour metre. Vigour-giving metre. Emulating metre. Spacious metre, Inaccessible metre. Slow metre. Ankânka metre.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: रश्मिना सत्याय सत्यं जिन्व प्रेतिना धर्मणा धर्मं जिन्वान्वित्या दिवा दिवं जिन्व सन्धिनान्तरिक्षेणान्तरिक्षं जिन्व प्रतिधिना पृथिव्या पृथिवीं जिन्व विष्टम्भेन वृष्ट्या वृष्टिं जिन्व प्रवयाऽह्नाहर्जिन्वानुया रात्र्या रात्रीं जिन्वोशिजा वसुभ्यो वसूञ्जिन्व प्रकेतेनादित्येभ्यऽआदित्याञ्जिन्व ॥६ ॥
translation: With the ray for truth quicken thou truth. With advance by duty quicken duty. With following by heaven quicken heaven. With union by middle air quicken middle air. With Pratidhi by Earth quicken Earth. With support by rain quicken rain. With blowing away by day quicken day. With following by eight quicken night. With clarified butter by the Vasus quicken the Vasus. With perception by the Âdityas quicken the Âdityas.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तन्तुना रायस्पोषेण रायस्पोषं जिन्व सꣳसर्पेण श्रुताय श्रुतं जिन्वैडेनौषधीभिरोषधीर्जिन्वोत्तमेन तनूभिस्तनूर्जिन्व वयोधसाधीतेनाधीतं जिन्वाभिजिता तेजसा तेजो जिन्व ॥७ ॥
translation: With the thread by prosperity quicken prosperity. With the creeper by revelation quicken revelation. With refreshment by plants quicken plants. With the best by bodies quicken bodies. With the invigorating by religious study quicken religious study. With the victorious by brilliance quicken brilliance.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: प्रतिपदसि प्रतिपदे त्वानुपदस्यनुपदे त्वा सम्पदसि सम्पदे त्वा तेजोऽसि तेजसे त्वा ॥८ ॥
translation: Thou art Pratipad, for Pratipad thee. Thou art Anupad, for Anupad thee. Thou art Sampad, for Sampad thee. Thou art brilliance, for brilliance thee.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: त्रिवृदसि त्रिवृते त्वा प्रवृदसि प्रवृते त्वा विवृदसि विवृते त्वा सवृदसि सवृते त्वाक्रमोऽस्याक्रमाय त्वा संक्रमोऽसि संक्रमाय त्वोत्क्रमोऽस्युत्क्रमाय त्वोत्क्रान्तिरस्युत्क्रान्त्यै त्वाऽधिपतिनोर्जोर्जं जिन्व ॥९ ॥
translation: Trivrit (triple) art thou, thee for Trivrit. Pravrit art thou, thee for Pravrit. Vivrit art thou, thee for Vivrit. Savrit art thou, thee for Savrit. Thou art attack, thee for attack. Thou art concurrence, thee for concurrence. Thou art ascent, thee for ascent. Thou art upstriding, thee for upstriding. With Energy as over-lord quicken food-essence.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: राज्ञ्यसि प्राची दिग्वसवस्ते देवाऽअधिपतयोऽग्निर्हेतीनां प्रतिधर्त्ता त्रिवृत् त्वा स्तोमः पृथिव्याश्रयत्वाज्यमुक्थमव्यथायै स्तभ्नातु रथन्तरꣳसाम प्रतिष्ठित्याऽअन्तरिक्षऽऋषयस्त्वा प्रथमजा देवेषु दिवो मात्रया वरिम्णा प्रथन्तु विधर्त्ता चायमधिपतिश्च ते त्वा सर्वे संविदाना नाकस्य पृष्ठे स्वर्गे लोके यजमानं च सादयन्तु ॥१० ॥
translation: Thou art the Queen, the Eastern region. The bright Vasus are thine overlords. Agni is thy warder-off of hostile weapons. May the Trivrit Stoma assist thee on earth. The Âjya Uktha fix thee firmly against slipping. The Rathantara Sâman establish thee in the sky for secure station. May the first-born Rishis extend thee among the Gods by the measure and amplitude of heaven. May this Disposer and the Over-Lord extend thee. May all, concordant, settle thee on the ridge of heaven in the world of Svarga.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: विराडसि दक्षिणा दिग्रुद्रास्ते देवाऽअधिपतयऽइन्द्रो हेतीनां प्रतिधर्त्ता पञ्चदशस्त्वा स्तोमः पृथिव्या श्रयतु प्रऽउगमुक्थमव्यथायै स्तभ्नातु बृहत्साम प्रतिष्ठित्याऽअन्तरिक्षऽऋषयस्त्वा प्रथमजा देवेषु दिवो मात्रया वरिम्णा प्रथन्तु विधर्त्ता चायमधिपतिश्च ते त्वा सर्वे संविदाना नाकस्य पृष्ठे स्वर्गे लोके यजमानं च सादयन्तु ॥११ ॥
translation: Thou art Far-ruling, the Southern region. The bright Rudras are thine over-lords. Indra is thy warder-off of arrows. May the Pañchadasa Stoma support thee on earth. The Praüga Uktha fix thee firmly against slipping. The Brihat Sâman establish thee in the sky, etc. (the rest as in 10). 57
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सम्राडसि प्रतीची दिगादित्यास्ते देवाऽअधिपतयो वरुणो हेतीनां प्रतिधर्त्ता सप्तदशस्त्वा स्तोमः पृथिव्याश्रयतु मरुत्वतीयमुक्थमव्यथायै स्तभ्नातु वैरूपꣳ साम प्रतिष्ठित्याऽअन्तरिक्षऽऋषयस्त्वा प्रथमजा देवेषु दिवो मात्रया वरिम्णा प्रथन्तु विधर्त्ता चायमधिपतिश्च ते त्वा सर्वे संविदाना नाकस्य पृष्ठे स्वर्गे लोके यजमानं च सादयन्तु ॥१२ ॥
translation: Thou art Universal Ruler, the Western region. The Âdityas are thine over-lords. Varuna is thy warder-off of missiles. The Saptadasa Stoma support thee on earth. The Marutvatîya Uktha fix thee firmly against slipping. The Vairûpa Sâman establish thee, etc. (as above).
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: स्वराडस्युदीची दिङ्मरुतस्ते देवाऽअधिपतयः सोमो हेतीनां प्रतिधर्त्तैकविꣳशस्त्वा स्तोमः पृथिव्या श्रयतु निष्केवल्यमुक्थमव्यथायै स्तभ्नातु वैराजꣳसाम प्रतिष्ठित्याऽअन्तरिक्षऽऋषयस्त्वा प्रथमजा देवेषु दिवो मात्रया वरिम्णा प्रथन्तु विधर्त्ता चायमधिपतिश्च ते त्वा सर्वे संविदाना नाकस्य पृष्ठे स्वर्गे लोके यजमानं च सादयन्तु ॥१३ ॥
translation: Thou art Independent Ruler, the Northern region. (The rest is identical with 12, with the substitution of Maruts . . . Soma . . . .Vimsa Stoma . . . Nishkevalya Uktha. . . . Vairâja Sâman for the corresponding names).
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अधिपत्न्यसि बृहती दिग्विश्वे ते देवाऽअधिपतयो बृहस्पतिर्हेतीनां प्रतिधर्त्ता त्रिणवत्रयस्त्रिꣳशौ त्वा स्तोमौ पृथिव्या श्रयतां वैश्वदेवाग्निमारुतेऽउक्थेऽअव्यथायै स्तभ्नीता शाक्वररैवते सामनी प्रतिष्ठित्याऽअन्तरिक्षऽऋषयस्त्वा प्रथमजा देवेषु दिवो मात्रया वरिम्णा प्रथन्तु विधर्त्ता चायमधिपतिश्च ते त्वा सर्वे संविदाना नाकस्य पृष्ठे स्वर्गे लोके यजमानञ्च सादयन्तु ॥१४ ॥
translation: Thou art Lady-Paramount, the Lofty region. (The rest as above, Visvedevas. . . Brihaspati . . .Trinava and Trayastrimsa Stomas . . .Vaisvadeva and Mâruta Ukthas . . . Sâkvara and Raivata Sâmans being substituted for the corresponding names.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अयं पुरो हरिकेशः सूर्यरश्मिस्तस्य रथगृत्सश्च रथौजाश्च सेनानीग्रामण्यौ। पुञ्जिकस्थला च क्रतुस्थला चाप्सरसौ दङ्क्ष्णवः पशवो हेतिः पौरुषेयो वधः प्रहेतिस्तेभ्यो नमोऽअस्तु ते नोऽवन्तु ते नो मृडयन्तु ते यं द्विष्मो यश्च नो द्वेष्टि तमेषां जम्भे दध्मः ॥१५ ॥
translation: This one in front, golden-tressed, with sunbeams; the leader of his host and his chieftain are Rathagritsa and Rathaujas, and Puñjikasthalâ: and Kratusthalâ his Apsarases. Biting animals are his weapon, homicide his missile weapon; to them be homage: may they protect us, may they have mercy upon us. In their jaws we place the man whom we hate and who hates us.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अयं दक्षिणा विश्वकर्मा तस्य रथस्वनश्च रथेचित्रश्च सेनानीग्रामण्यौ। मेनका च सहजन्या चाप्सरसौ यातुधाना हेती रक्षासि प्रहेतिस्तेभ्यो नमोऽअस्तु ते नोऽवन्तु ते नो मृडयन्तु ते यं द्विष्मो यश्च नो द्वेष्टि तमेषां जम्भे दध्मः ॥१६
translation: This one on the right, the Omnific; the leader of his host and his chieftain are Rathasvana and Rathechitra, and Menakâ and Sahajanyâ his Apsarases. Yâtudhânas are his weapon, Râkshasas his missile weapon; to them be homage, etc. (as in 15).
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अयं पश्चाद् विश्वव्यचास्तस्य रथप्रोतश्चासमरथश्च सेनानीग्रामण्यौ। प्रम्लोचन्ती चानुम्लोचन्ती चाप्सरसौ व्याघ्रा हेतिः सर्पाः प्रहेतिस्तेभ्यो नमोऽअस्तु ते नोऽवन्तु ते नो मृडयन्तु ते यं द्विष्मो यश्च नो द्वेष्टि तमेषां जम्भे दध्मः ॥१७ ॥
translation: This one behind, the All-comprising; the leader of his host and his chieftain are Rathaprota and Asamaratha, and Pramlochantî and Anumochlantî are his Apsarases. Tigers are his weapon, Serpents his missile weapon; to them be homage, etc.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अयमुत्तरात् संयद्वसुस्तस्य तार्क्ष्यश्चारिष्टनेमिश्च सेनानीग्रामण्यौ। विश्वाची च घृताची चाप्सरसावापो हेतिर्वातः प्रहेतिस्तेभ्यो नमोऽअस्तु ते नोऽवन्तु ते नो मृडयन्तु ते यं द्विष्मो यश्च नो द्वेष्टि तमेषां जम्भे दध्मः ॥१८ ॥
translation: This one on the left, Lord of uninterrupted riches; the leader of his host and his chieftain are Târkshya and Arishtanemi, and Visvâchî and Ghritâchi his Apsarases. Water is his weapon, wind his missile weapon; to them be homage, etc.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अयमुपर्यर्वाग्वसुस्तस्य सेनजिच्च सुषेणश्च सेनानीग्रामण्यौ। उर्वशी च पूर्वचित्तिश्चाप्सरसाववस्फूर्जन् हेतिर्विद्युत्प्रहेतिस्तेभ्यो नमोऽअस्तु ते नोऽवन्तु ते नो मृडयन्तु ते यं द्विष्मो यश्च नो द्वेष्टि तमेषां जम्भे दध्मः ॥१९ ॥
translation: This one above, Wealth-giver; the leader of his host and his chieftain are Senajit and Sushena, and Urvasi and Pûrvachitti his Apsarases. Thundering is his weapon and lightning his missile weapon; to them be homage, etc.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्निर्मूर्द्धा दिवः ककुत्पतिः पृथिव्याऽअयम्। अपा रेतासि जिन्वति ॥२० ॥
translation: Agni is head and height of heaven, the Master of the earth is he. He quickeneth the waters’ seed.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अयमग्निः सहस्रिणो वाजस्य शतिनस्पतिः। मूर्धा कवी रयीणाम् ॥२१ ॥
translation: This Agni is the Master of spoil thousandfold and hundredfold, the sapient one, the head of wealth.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: त्वामग्ने पुष्करादध्यथर्वा निरमन्थत। मूर्ध्नो विश्वस्य वाघतः ॥२२ ॥
translation: Agni, Atharvan brought thee forth by rubbing from the lotus-leaf, the head of Visva, of the Priest.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: भुवो यज्ञस्य रजसश्च नेता यत्रा नियुद्भिः सचसे शिवाभिः। दिवि मूर्धानं दधिषे स्वर्षां जिह्वामग्ने चकृषे हव्यवाहम् ॥२३ ॥
translation: Guide of the rite art thou and of the region to which with thine auspicious teams thou tendest. Thy light-bestowing head to heaven thou liftest, making thy tongue oblation-bearer, Agni.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अबोध्यग्निः समिधा जनानां प्रति धेनुमिवायतीमुषासम्। यह्वाऽइव प्र वयामुज्जिहानाः प्र भानवः सिस्रते नाकमच्छ ॥२४ ॥
translation: Agni is wakened by the people’s fuel to meet the Dawn who cometh like a milch-cow. Like young trees shooting up on high their branches his flames are rising to the vault of heaven.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अवोचाम कवये मेध्याय वचो वन्दारु वृषभाय वृष्णे। गविष्ठिरो नमसा स्तोममग्नौ दिवीव रुक्ममुरुव्यञ्चमश्रेत् ॥२५ ॥
translation: To him adorable, sage, strong and mighty we have sung forth our song of praise and homage. Gavishthira hath raised with prayer to Agni this laud far-reaching as the gold in heaven.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अयमिह प्रथमो धायि धातृभिर्होता यजिष्ठोऽअध्वरेष्वीड्यः। यमप्नवानो भृगवो विरुरुचुर्वनेषु चित्रं विभ्वं विशेविशे ॥२६ ॥
translation: Here by ordainers was this God appointed first Invoker, best at worship, to be praised at rites; Whom Apnavâna and the Bhrigus caused to shine bright-coloured in the wood, spreading to every house. 58
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: जनस्य गोपाऽअजनिष्ट जागृविरग्निः सुदक्षः सुविताय नव्यसे। घृतप्रतीको बृहता दिविस्पृशा द्युमद्विभाति भरतेभ्यः शुचिः ॥२७ ॥
translation: The watchful Guardian of the people hath been born, Agni the very strong, for fresh prosperity. With oil upon his face, with high heaven-touching flame, he shineth splendidly, pure for the Bharatas.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: त्वामग्नेऽअङ्गिरसो गुहा हितमन्वविन्दञ्छिश्रियाणं वनेवने। स जायसे मथ्यमानः सहो महत् त्वामाहुः सहसस्पुत्रमङ्गिरः ॥२८ ॥
translation: Agni, Angirases discovered thee what time thou layest hidden, fleeing back from wood to wood. Thou by attrition art produced as conquering, might, and men, O Angiras, call thee the Son of Strength.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सखायः सं वः सम्यञ्चमिषꣳस्तोमं चाग्नये। वर्षिष्ठाय क्षितीनामूर्जो नप्त्रे सहस्वते ॥२९ ॥
translation: Offer to Agni, O my friends, your seemly food, your seemly praise; To him supremest o’er the folk, the Son of Strength, the Mighty Lord.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सꣳसमिद्युवसे वृषन्नग्ने विश्वान्यर्य्यऽआ। इडस्पदे समिध्यसे स नो वसून्याभर ॥३० ॥
translation: Thou, mighty Agni, gatherest up all that is precious for thy friend: Bring us all treasure as thou art enkindled in libation’s place.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: त्वां चित्रश्रवस्तम हवन्ते विक्षु जन्तवः। शोचिष्केशं पुरुप्रियाग्ने हव्याय वोढवे ॥३१ ॥
translation: O Agni, loved of many, thou of fame most wondrous, in their homes Men call on thee whose hair is flame to be the bearer of their gifts.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: एना वोऽअग्निं नमसोर्जो नपातमाहुवे। प्रियं चेतिष्ठमरतिꣳस्वध्वरं विश्वस्य दूतममृतम् ॥३२ ॥
translation: With this my reverent hymn I call Agni for you, the Son. of Strength, Dear, wisest envoy, served with noble sacrifice, immortal messenger of all.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: विश्वस्य दूतममृतं विश्वस्य दूतममृतम्। स योजतेऽअरुषा विश्वभोजसा स दुद्रवत् स्वाहुतः ॥३३ ॥
translation: Immortal messenger of all, immortal messenger of all, His two red steeds, all-cherishing; he harnesseth: let him, well-worshipped, urge them fast.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: स दुद्रवत् स्वाहुतः स दुद्रवत् स्वाहुतः। सुब्रह्मा यज्ञः सुशमी वसूनां देवꣳराधो जनानाम् ॥३४ ॥
translation: Let him well-worshipped urge them fast, let him well-worshipped urge them fast. Then hath the sacrifice good prayer and happy end, and heavenly gift of wealth to men.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्ने वाजस्य गोमतऽईशानः सहसो यहो। अस्मे धेहि जातवेदो महि श्रवः ॥३५ ॥
translation: O Agni, thou who art the Lord of wealth in kine, the Son of Strength, Vouchsafe to us, O Jâtavedas, high renown.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सऽइधानो वसुष्कविरग्निरीडेन्यो गिरा। रेवदस्मभ्यं पुर्वणीक दीदिहि ॥३६ ॥
translation: He, Agni, kindled, good and wise, must be exalted in our song: Shine, thou of many forms, shine radiantly on us.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: क्षपो राजन्नुत त्मनाग्ने वस्तोरुतोषसः। स तिग्मजम्भ रक्षसो दह प्रति ॥३७ ॥
translation: O Agni, shining of thyself by night and when the morning breaks, Burn, thou whose teeth are sharp, against the Râkshasas.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: भद्रो नोऽअग्निराहुतो भद्रा रातिः सुभग भद्रो अध्वरः। भद्राऽउत प्रशस्तयः ॥३८ ॥
translation: May Agni, worshipped, bring us bliss, may the gift, Blessed One! and sacrifice bring bliss, Yea, may our praises bring us bliss.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: भद्राऽउत प्रशस्तयो भद्रं मनः कृणुष्व वृत्रतूर्य्ये। येना समत्सु सासहः ॥३९ ॥
translation: Yea, may our praises bring us bliss. Show forth the mind that brings success in war with fiends, wherewith thou conquerest in fights:
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: येना समत्सु सासहोऽव स्थिरा तनुहि भूरि शर्धताम्। वनेमा तेऽअभिष्टिभिः ॥४० ॥
translation: Wherewith thou conquerest in fights. Bring down the many firm hopes of our enemies, and let us vanquish with thine aid.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्निं तं मन्ये यो वसुरस्तं यं यन्ति धेनवः। अस्तमर्वन्तऽआशवोऽस्तं नित्यासो वाजिनऽइषꣳस्तोतृभ्यऽआ भर ॥४१ ॥
translation: I value Agni, that good Lord, the home to which the kind return; Whom fleet-foot coursers seek as home, and strong enduring steeds as home. Bring food to those who sing thy praise.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सोऽअग्निर्यो वसुर्गृणे सं यमायन्ति धेनवः। समर्वन्तो रघुद्रुवः सꣳसुजातासः सूरयऽइषꣳ स्तोतृभ्यऽआ भर ॥४२ ॥
translation: ‘Tis Agni whom we laud as good, to whom the milch-kine come in herds, To whom the coursers swift of foot, to whom our well-born princes come. Bring food to those who sing thy praise.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उभे सुश्चन्द्र सर्पिषो दर्वी श्रीणीषऽआसनि। उतो नऽउत्पुपूर्या उक्थेषु शवसस्पतऽइष स्तोतृभ्यऽआ भर ॥४३ ॥
translation: Thou, brilliant God, within thy mouth warmest both ladles of the oil. So fill us also in our hymns abundantly, O Lord of Strength. Bring food to those who sing thy praise.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्ने तमद्याश्वं न स्तोमैः क्रतुं न भद्रꣳ हृदिस्पृशम्। ऋध्यामा तऽओहैः ॥४४ ॥
translation: Agni, with lauds this day may we bring thee that which thou lovest, Right judgment, like a horse, with our devotions.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अधा ह्यग्ने क्रतोर्भद्रस्य दक्षस्य साधोः। रथीर्ऋतस्य बृहतो बभूथ ॥४५ ॥
translation: For thou hast ever been the car-driver, Agni, of noble Strength, lofty sacrifice, and rightful judgment. 59
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: एभिर्नोऽअर्कैर्भवा नोऽअर्वाङ् स्वर्ण ज्योतिः। अग्ने विश्वेभिः सुमनाऽअनीकैः ॥४६ ॥
translation: Through these our praises come thou to meet us, bright as the sunlight, O Agni, well- disposed, with all thine aspects.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्नि होतारं मन्ये दास्वन्तं वसुꣳ सूनुꣳ सहसो जातवेदसं विप्रं न जातवेदसम्। यऽऊर्ध्वया स्वध्वरो देवो देवाच्या कृपा। घृतस्य विभ्राष्टिमनु वष्टि शोचिषाऽऽजुह्वानस्य सर्पिषः ॥४७ ॥
translation: Agni I hold as Herald, the munificent, the gracious Son of Strength who knoweth all that live, as holy singer knowing all; Lord of fair rites, a God with form erected, turning to the Gods, He, when the flame hath sprung forth from the sacred oil, the offered fatness, longeth for it with his glow.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्ने त्वं नो अन्तमऽउत त्राता शिवो भवा वरूथ्यः। वसुरग्निर्वसुश्रवाऽअच्छा नक्षि द्युमत्तमꣳ रयिं दाः। तं त्वा शोचिष्ठ दीदिवः सुम्नाय नूनमीमहे सखिभ्यः ॥४८ ॥
translation: O Agni, be our nearest Friend, be thou a kind deliverer and a gracious Friend. Come as good Agni, come as excellent and give us wealth most splendidly renowned. To thee then, O most bright, O radiant God, we come with prayer for happiness for our friends.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: येनऽऋषयस्तपसा सत्रमायन्निन्धानाऽअग्नि स्वराभरन्तः। तस्मिन्नहं नि दधे नाकेऽअग्निं यमाहुर्मनव स्तीर्णबर्हिषम् ॥४९ ॥
translation: With what devotion, winning light, the Rishis came, kindling Agni, to the Holy session, Even with that in heaven I stablish Agni whom men call him whose sacred grass is scattered.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तं पत्नीभिरनु गच्छेम देवाः पुत्रैर्भ्रातृभिरुत वा हिरण्यैः। नाकं गृभ्णानाः सुकृतस्य लोके तृतीये पृष्ठेऽअधि रोचने दिवः ॥५० ॥
translation: Gods, let us follow him with wives beside us, with sons, with brothers, with our gold adornments, Grasping the sky up in the world of virtue, on the third height, the luminous realm of heaven.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आ वाचो मध्यमरुहद् भुरण्युरयमग्निः सत्पतिश्चेकितानः। पृष्ठे पृथिव्या निहितो दविद्युतदधस्पदं कृणुतां ये पृतन्यवः ॥५१ ॥
translation: This Agni mounted up to Speech’s Centre, Lord of the Brave, observant, ever-active. Laid on the back of Earth, may he, resplendent, cast under foot those who would fight against us.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अयमग्निर्वीरतमो वयोधाः सहस्रियो द्योततामप्रयुच्छन्। विभ्राजमानः सरिरस्य मध्यऽउप प्र याहि दिव्यानि धाम ॥५२ ॥
translation: May this most manly Agni, strength-bestower, giver of thousands, shine with care that fails not. Resplendent in the middle of the water, make thine approach to the celestial mansions.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सम्प्रच्यवध्वमुप संप्रयाताग्ने पथो देवयानान् कृणुध्वम्। पुनः कृण्वाना पितरा युवानान्वातासीत् त्वयि तन्तुमेतम् ॥५३ ॥
translation: Make him go forth from all sides: meet, Approach ye. O Agni, make the paths for Godward travel. Making the Parents young with life’s renewal, the out spun thread in thee have they extended.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उद् बुध्यस्वाग्ने प्रति जागृहि त्वमिष्टापूर्त्ते सꣳसृजेथामयं च। अस्मिन्त्सधस्थेऽअध्युत्तरस्मिन् विश्वे देवा यजमानश्च सीदत ॥५४ ॥
translation: Wake up, O Agni, thou, and keep him watchful. Wish and fruition, meet, and he, together. In this and in the loftier habitation be seated, All-Gods! and the Sacrificer.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: येन वहसि सहस्रं येनाग्ने सर्ववेदसम्। तेनेमं यज्ञं नो नय स्वर्देवेषु गन्तवे ॥५५ ॥
translation: Convey our sacrifice to heaven that it may reach the God with that Whereby thou, Agni, bearest wealth in thousands and all precious things.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अयं ते योनिर्ऋत्वियो यतो जातोऽअरोचथाः। तं जानन्नग्नऽआ रोहाथा नो वर्धया रयिम् ॥५६ ॥
translation: This is thine ordered place of birth whence sprung to life thou shonest forth. Knowing this, Agni, rise thou up and cause our riches to increase.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तपश्च तपस्यश्च शैशिरावृतूऽअग्नेरन्तःश्लेषोऽसि कल्पेतां द्यावापृथिवी कल्पन्तामापऽओषधयः कल्पन्तामग्नयः पृथङ् मम ज्यैष्ठ्याय सव्रताः। येऽअग्नयः समनसोऽन्तरा द्यावापृथिवीऽइमे। शैशिरावृतूऽअभिकल्पमानाऽइन्द्रमिव देवाऽअभिसंविशन्तु तया देवतयाऽङ्गिरस्वद् ध्रुवे सीदतम् ॥५७ ॥
translation: Tapa, Tapasya, pair of Dewy Seasons: thou art, etc. (as in XIII. 25).
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: परमेष्ठी त्वा सादयतु दिवस्पृष्ठे ज्योतिष्मतीम्। विश्वस्मै प्राणायापानाय व्यानाय विश्वं ज्योतिर्यच्छ। सूर्यस्तेऽधिपतिस्तया देवतयाऽङ्गिरस्वद् ध्रुवा सीद ॥५८ ॥
translation: On the sky’s back may Parameshthin lay thee, etc. (as in XIV. 14). Thy Lord is Sûrya, etc. (as in XIV. 14).
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: लोकं पृण छिद्रं पृणाथो सीद ध्रुवा त्वम्। इन्द्राग्नी त्वा बृहस्पतिरस्मिन् योनावसीषदन् ॥५९ ॥
translation: Repeated from XII. 54.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ताऽअस्य सूददोहसः सोमꣳ श्रीणन्ति पृश्नयः। जन्मन्देवानां विशस्त्रिष्वारोचने दिवः ॥६० ॥
translation: Repeated from XII. 55.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इन्द्रं विश्वाऽअवीवृधन्त्समुद्रव्यचसं गिरः। रथीतमꣳ रथीनां वाजाना सत्पतिं पतिम् ॥६१ ॥
translation: Repeated from XII. 56.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: प्रोथदश्वो न यवसेऽविष्यन्यदा महः संवरणाद्व्यस्थात्। आदस्य वातोऽअनु वाति शोचिरध स्म ते व्रजनं कृष्णमस्ति ॥६२ ॥
translation: Like a horse neighing, eager for the pasture, when he hath stepped forth from the great enclosure: Then the wind following blows upon his splendour, and, straight, the path is black which thou hast travelled.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आयोष्ट्वा सदने सादयाम्यवतश्छायाया समुद्रस्य हृदये। रश्मीवतीं भास्वतीमा या द्यां भास्या पृथिवीमोर्वन्तरिक्षम् ॥६३ ॥
translation: In Âyu’s seat I set thee, in the shadow of the protector in the heart of Ocean, Thee luminous, bright with eyes, thee who illumest the sky, the earth, and air’s broad realm between them.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: परमेष्ठी त्वा सादयतु दिवस्पृष्ठे व्यचस्वतीं प्रथस्वतीं दिवं यच्छ दिवं दृꣳह दिवं मा हिꣳसीः। विश्वस्मै प्राणायापानाय व्यानायोदानाय प्रतिष्ठायै चरित्राय। सूर्यस्त्वाभिपातु मह्या स्वस्त्या छर्दिषा शन्तमेन तया देवतयाऽङ्गिरस्वद् ध्रुवे सीदतम् ॥६४ ॥
translation: On the sky’s back may Parameshthin set thee, etc. (as in XIV. 12, substituting sky for air and Sûrya for Vâyu). 60
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सहस्रस्य प्रमासि सहस्रस्य प्रतिमासि सहस्रस्योन्मासि साहस्रोऽसि सहस्राय त्वा ॥६५ ॥
translation: Thou art the measure of a thousand. Thou art the representative of a thousand. Thou art the equivalent of a thousand. Thou art worth a thousand. Thee for a thousand. 61
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमस्ते रुद्र मन्यवऽउतो तऽइषवे नमः। बाहुभ्यामुत ते नमः ॥१ ॥
translation: HOMAGE be paid unto thy wrath, O Rudra, homage to thy shaft: to thy two arms be homage paid.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: या ते रुद्र शिवा तनूरघोराऽपापकाशिनी। तया नस्तन्वा शन्तमया गिरिशन्ताभि चाकशीहि ॥२ ॥
translation: With that auspicious form of thine, mild, Rudra! pleasant to behold, Even with that most blessèd form, look, Mountain-haunter! here on us.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यामिषुं गिरिशन्त हस्ते बिभर्ष्यस्तवे। शिवां गिरित्र तां कुरु मा हिꣳसीः पुरुषं जगत् ॥३ ॥
translation: The shaft which, Mountain-haunter, thou art holding in thy hand to shoot, Make that auspicious, Mountain-Lord! Injure not man nor moving thing.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: शिवेन वचसा त्वा गिरिशाच्छा वदामसि। यथा नः सर्वमिज्जगदयक्ष्म सुमनाऽअसत् ॥४ ॥
translation: O Dweller on the Mountain, we salute thee with auspicious hymn; That all, yea, all our people may be healthy and well-satisfied.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अध्यवोचदधिवक्ता प्रथमो दैव्यो भिषक्। अहीश्चँ सर्वाञ्जम्भयन्त्सर्वाश्च यातुधान्योऽधराचीः परा सुव ॥५ ॥
translation: The Advocate, the first divine Physician, hath defended us. Crushing all serpents, drive away all Yâtudhânis down below.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: असौ यस्ताम्रोऽअरुणऽउत बभ्रुः सुमङ्गलः। ये चैनꣳ रुद्राऽअभितो दिक्षु श्रिताः सहस्रशोऽवैषा हेडऽईमहे ॥६ ॥
translation: That most auspicious One whose hue is coppery and red and brown, And those, the Rudras who maintain their station in the regions, who surround him in a thousand bands, of these we deprecate the wrath.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: असौ योऽवसर्पति नीलग्रीवो विलोहितः। उतैनं गोपाऽअदृश्रन्नदृश्रन्नुदहार्य्यः स दृष्टो मृडयाति नः ॥७ ॥
translation: May he who glides away, whose neck is azure, and whose hue is red, He whom the herdsmen, whom the girls who carry water have beheld, may he when seen be kind to us.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमोऽस्तु नीलग्रीवाय सहस्राक्षाय मीढुषे। अथो येऽअस्य सत्वानोऽहं तेभ्योऽकरं नमः ॥८ ॥
translation: Homage to him the Azure-nested, the thousand-eyed, the bountiful, Yea, and his spirit ministers—to them I offer reverence.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: प्रमुञ्च धन्वनस्त्वमुभयोरार्त्न्योर्ज्याम्। याश्च ते हस्तऽइषवः परा ता भगवो वप ॥९ ॥
translation: Loosen thy bowstring, loosen it from thy bow’s two extremities, And cast away, O Lord Divine, the arrows that are in thy hand.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: विज्यं धनुः कपर्दिनो विशल्यो बाणवाँ२ऽउत। अनेशन्नस्य याऽइषवऽआभुरस्य निषङ्गधिः ॥१० ॥
translation: Now stringless be Kapardin’s bow, his quiver hold no pointed shaft. The shafts he had have perished and the sheath that held his sword is bare.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: या ते हेतिर्मीढुष्टम हस्ते बभूव ते धनुः। तयास्मान् विश्वतस्त्वमयक्ष्मया परि भुज ॥११ ॥
translation: Thy weapon, O Most Bountiful, the bow that resteth in thy hand,— With that, deprived of power to harm, protect thou us on every side.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: परि ते धन्वनो हेतिरस्मान् वृणक्तु विश्वतः। अथो यऽइषुधिस्तवारेऽअस्मन्निधेहि तम् ॥१२ ॥
translation: So may the arrow of thy bow, in all directions, pass us by, And in a place remote from us lay thou the quiver that thou hast.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अवतत्य धनुष्ट्व सहस्राक्ष शतेषुधे। निशीर्य शल्यानां मुखा शिवो नः सुमना भव ॥१३ ॥
translation: Having unbent thy how O thou hundred-eyed, hundred-quivered One! And dulled thy pointed arrows’ heads, be kind and gracious unto us.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमस्तऽआयुधायानातताय धृष्णवे। उभाभ्यामुत ते नमो बाहुभ्यां तव धन्वने ॥१४ ॥
translation: To thy fierce weapon, now unstrung, be reverent obeisance paid. Homage be paid to both thine arms, and to thy bow be reverence!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मा नो महान्तमुत मा नोऽअर्भकं मा नऽउक्षन्तमुत मा नऽउक्षितम्। मा नो वधीः पितरं मोत मातरं मा नः प्रियास्तन्वो रुद्र रीरिषः ॥१५ ॥
translation: Do thou no injury to great or small of us, harm not the growing boy, harm not the full grown man. Slay not a sire among us, slay no mother here, and to our own dear bodies, Rudra! do no harm.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मा नस्तोके तनये मा नऽआयुषि मा नो गोषु मा नोऽअश्वेषु रीरिषः। मा नो वीरान् रुद्र भामिनो वधीर्हविष्मन्तः सदमित् त्वा हवामहे ॥१६ ॥
translation: Harm us not in our seed or in our progeny, harm us not in our life or in our cows or steeds. Slay not our heroes in the fury of their wrath. We with oblations ever call on only thee.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमो हिरण्यबाहवे सेनान्ये दिशां च पतये नमो नमो वृक्षेभ्यो हरिकेशेभ्यः पशूनां पतये नमो नमः शष्पिञ्जराय त्विषीमते पथीनां पतये नमो नमो हरिकेशायोपवीतिने पुष्टानां पतये नमः ॥१७ ॥
translation: Homage to the golden-armed leader of hosts, lord of the 1 regions, to the trees with their green tresses, to the Lord of beasts be homage; homage to him whose sheen is like green grass, homage to the radiant Lord of paths, homage to the golden-haired wearer of the sacrificial cord, homage to the Lord of the well-endowed. 62
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमो बभ्लुशाय व्याधिनेऽन्नानां पतये नमो नमो भवस्य हेत्यै जगतां पतये नमो नमो रुद्रायाततायिने क्षेत्राणां पतये नमो नमः सूतायाहन्त्यै वनानां पतये नमः ॥१८ ॥
translation: Homage to the brown-hued piercer, to the Lord of food be homage. Homage to Bhava’s weapon, homage to the Lord of moving things! homage to Rudra whose bow is bent to slay, to the Lord of fields homage, homage to the charioteer who injures, none, to the Lord of forests be homage.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमो रोहिताय स्थपतये वृक्षाणां पतये नमो नमो भुवन्तये वारिवस्कृतायौषधीनां पतये नमो नमो मन्त्रिणे वाणिजाय कक्षाणां पतये नमो नमऽउच्चैर्घोषायाक्रन्दयते पत्तीनां पतये नमः ॥१९ ॥
translation: Homage to the red architect, to the Lord of trees homage! Homage to him who stretched out the earth, to him who gives relief be homage. Homage to the Lord of Plants, homage to the prudent merchant! Homage to the Lord of bushes, to the shouting Lord of foot-soldiers who makes foes weep be homage.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमः कृत्स्नायतया धावते सत्वनां पतये नमो नमः सहमानाय निव्याधिनऽआव्याधिनीनां पतये नमो नमो निषङ्गिणे ककुभाय स्तेनानां पतये नमो नमो निचेरवे परिचरायारण्यानां पतये नमः ॥२० ॥
translation: Homage to the runner at full stretch, to the Lord of ministering spirits, homage! Homage to the conquering, piercing Lord of assailing bands, homage to the towering sword-bearer, to the Lord of thieves homage! Homage to the gliding robber, to the roamer, to the Lord of forests homage!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमो वञ्चते परिवञ्चते स्तायूनां पतये नमो नमो निषङ्गिणऽइषुधिमते तस्कराणां पतये नमो नमः सृकायिभ्यो जिघासद्भ्यो मुष्णतां पतये नमो नमोऽसिमद्भ्यो नक्तं चरद्भ्यो विकृन्तानां पतये नमः ॥२१ ॥
translation: Homage to the cheat, to the arch-deceiver, to the Lord of stealers homage! Homage to the wearer of sword and quiver, to the Lord of robbers homage! Homage to the boltarmed homicides, to the Lord of pilferers homage! Homage to the sword-bearers, to those who roam at night, to the Lord of plunderers homage!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमऽउष्णीषिणे गिरिचराय कुलुञ्चानां पतये नमो नमऽइषुमद्भ्यो धन्वायिभ्यश्च वो नमो नमऽआतन्वानेभ्यः प्रतिदधानेभ्यश्च वो नमो नमऽआयच्छद्भ्योऽस्यद्भ्यश्च वो नमः ॥२२ ॥
translation: To the turban-wearing haunter of mountains, Lord of land-grabbers homage! Homage to you who bear arrows and to you who carry bows. Homage to you with bent bows, and to you who adjust your arrows, to you who draw the bow and to you who shoot be homage!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमो विसृजद्भ्यो विद्ध्यद्भ्यश्च वो नमो नमः स्वपद्भ्यो जाग्रद्भ्यश्च वो नमो नमः शयानेभ्यऽआसीनेभ्यश्च वो नमो नमस्तिष्ठद्भ्यो धावद्भ्यश्च वो नमः ॥२३ ॥
translation: Homage to you who let fly and to you who pierce, homage to you who sleep and to you who wake, homage to you who lie and to you who sit, homage to you who stand and to you who run.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमः सभाभ्यः सभापतिभ्यश्च वो नमो नमोऽश्वेभ्योऽश्वपतिभ्यश्च वो नमो नमऽआव्याधिनीभ्यो विविध्यन्तीभ्यश्च वो नमो नमऽउगणाभ्यस्तृꣳहतीभ्यश्च वो नमः ॥२४ ॥
translation: Homage to assemblies and to you lords of assemblies, homage to horses and to you masters of horses, homage to you hosts that wound and pierce, to you destructive armies with excellent bands be homage.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमो गणेभ्यो गणपतिभ्यश्च वो नमो नमो व्रातेभ्यो व्रातपतिभ्यश्च वो नमो नमो गृत्सेभ्यो गृत्सपतिभ्यश्च वो नमो नमो विरूपेभ्यो विश्वरूपेभ्यश्च वो नमः ॥२५ ॥
translation: Homage to the troops and to you lords of troops be homage. Homage to the companies and to you lords of companies, homage. Homage to sharpers and to you lords of sharpers, homage. Homage to you the deformed, and to you who wear all forms, homage!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमः सेनाभ्यः सेनानिभ्यश्च वो नमो नमो रथिभ्योऽअरथेभ्यश्च वो नमो नमः क्षत्तृभ्यः सङ्ग्रहीतृभ्यश्च वो नमो नमो महद्भ्योऽअर्भकेभ्यश्च वो नमः ॥२६ ॥
translation: Homage to armies and to you the leaders of armies, homage. Homage to you car-borne and to you who are carless, homage. Homage to the charioteers and to you drivers of horses, homage. Homage to you the great and to you the small, homage.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमस्तक्षभ्यो रथकारेभ्यश्च वो नमो नमः कुलालेभ्यः कर्मारेभ्यश्च वो नमो नमो निषादेभ्यः पुञ्जिष्ठेभ्यश्च वो नमो नमः श्वनिभ्यो मृगयुभ्यश्च वो नमः ॥२७ ॥
translation: Homage to you carpenters, and to you chariot-makers homage. Homage to you potters and to you blacksmiths, homage. Homage to you Nishâdas and to you Puñjishthas, homage. Homage to you dog-leaders, and to you hunters, homage.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमः श्वभ्यः श्वपतिभ्यश्च वो नमो नमो भवाय च रुद्राय च नमः शर्वाय च पशुपतये च नमो नीलग्रीवाय च शितिकण्ठाय च ॥२८ ॥
translation: Homage to dogs, and to you masters of dogs, homage. Homage to Bhava, and to Rudra homage, homage to Sarva and to Pasupati, and to Nîlagrîva and Sitikantha, homage.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमः कपर्दिने च व्युप्तकेशाय च नमः सहस्राक्षाय च शतधन्वने च नमो गिरिशयाय च शिपिविष्टाय च नमो मीढुष्टमाय चेषुमते च ॥२९ ॥
translation: Homage to him with braided hair and to him with shaven hair, homage! homage to the thousand-eyed and to him with a hundred bows, homage! To the mountain-haunter and to Sipivishta, homage! To the most bountiful, armed with arrows, homage! 30 Homage to the short, and to the dwarf, homage, homage to the great and to the adult, homage! Homage to the full-grown and to the growing, to the foremost and to the first be homage.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमऽआशवे चाजिराय च नमः शीघ्र्याय च शीभ्याय च नमऽऊर्म्याय चावस्वन्याय च नमो नादेयाय च द्वीप्याय च ॥३१ ॥
translation: Homage to the swift, and to the active be homage, and to the hasty and to the rapid mover be homage! Homage to him who dwells in waves, and in still waters, to him who dwells in rivers and on islands. 63
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमो ज्येष्ठाय च कनिष्ठाय च नमः पूर्वजाय चापरजाय च नमो मध्यमाय चापगल्भाय च नमो जघन्याय च बुध्न्याय च ॥३२ ॥
translation: Homage to the eldest and to the youngest, to the first-born and to the last-born, homage! Homage to the middle-most and to the immature, to the lowest and to him who is in the depth, be homage!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमः सोभ्याय च प्रतिसर्याय च नमो याम्याय च क्षेम्याय च नमः श्लोक्याय चावसान्याय च नमऽउर्वर्याय च खल्याय च ॥३३ ॥
translation: Homage to Sobhya and to the dweller in the magic amulet, homage! Homage to him who is allied to Yama, to him who prospers be homage! Homage to the famous and to the endmost, to him of the sown corn-land and to him of the threshing-floor be homage.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमो वन्याय च कक्ष्याय च नमः श्रवाय च प्रतिश्रवाय च नमऽआशुषेणाय चाशुरथाय च नमः शूराय चावभेदिने च ॥३४ ॥
translation: Homage to him in woods and to him in bushes, homage! Homage to him as sound and to him as echo, homage! Homage to him with swift armies and to him with swift chariots, homage! Homage to the hero, and to him who rends asunder be homage.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमो बिल्मिने च कवचिने च नमो वर्मिणे च वरूथिने च नमः श्रुताय च श्रुतसेनाय च नमो दुन्दुभ्याय चाहनन्याय च ॥३५ ॥
translation: Homage to him who wears a helmet, and to him who wears a cuirass, homage! To him who wears mail and defensive armour, homage! To the renowned one and to him whose army is renowned be homage, to him who is in drums and to him who makes himself known by beating them.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमो धृष्णवे च प्रमृशाय च नमो निषङ्गिणे चेषुधिमते च नमस्तीक्ष्णेषवे चायुधिने च नमः स्वायुधाय च सुधन्वने च ॥३६ ॥
translation: Homage to the bold one and to the prudent, homage to him who carries sword and quiver, homage to him who hath keen arrows and is armed with weapons, homage to him who hath good weapons and a good bow.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमः स्रुत्याय च पथ्याय च नमः काट्याय च नीप्याय च नमः कुल्याय च सरस्याय च नमो नादेयाय च वैशन्ताय च ॥३७ ॥
translation: Homage to him who dwells on paths and roads, homage to him who dwells in rugged spots and on the skirts of mountains, homage to him who dwells in water courses and lakes, homage to him who dwells in rivers and mores.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमः कूप्याय चावट्याय च नमो वीध्र्याय चातप्याय च नमो मेघ्याय च विद्युत्याय च नमो वर्ष्याय चावर्ष्याय च ॥३८ ॥
translation: Homage to him who dwells in wells and pits, homage to him who dwells in bright sky and sunlight. Homage to him who dwells in cloud and lightning, homage to him who dwells in rain and to him who dwells in fair weather.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमो वात्याय च रेष्म्याय च नमो वास्तव्याय च वास्तुपाय च नमः सोमाय च रुद्राय च नमस्ताम्राय चारुणाय च ॥३९ ॥
translation: Homage to him who dwells in wind and to him who dwells in tempest, homage to the dweller in houses and to the house-protector. Homage to Soma and to Rudra, homage to the copper-coloured and to the ruddy One.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमः शङ्गवे च पशुपतये च नम उग्राय च भीमाय च नमोऽग्रेवधाय च दूरेवधाय च नमो हन्त्रे च हनीयसे च नमो वृक्षेभ्यो हरिकेशेभ्यो नमस्ताराय ॥४० ॥
translation: Homage to the giver of weal, and to Pasupati, homage to the fierce and to the terrific. Homage to him who slays in front and to him who slays at a distance, homage to the slayer and to the frequent slayer, homage to the green-tressed trees, homage to the deliverer.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमः शम्भवाय च मयोभवाय च नमः शङ्कराय च मयस्कराय च नमः शिवाय च शिवतराय च ॥४१ ॥
translation: Homage to the source of happiness and to the source of delight, homage to the causer of happiness and to the causer of delight, homage to the auspicious, homage to the most auspicious.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमः पार्याय चावार्याय च नमः प्रतरणाय चोत्तरणाय च नमस्तीर्थ्याय च कूल्याय च नमः शष्प्याय च फेन्याय च ॥४२ ॥
translation: Homage to him who is beyond and to him who is on this side, homage to him who crosses over and to him who crosses back. Homage to him who is in fords and on river banks, homage to him who is in tender grass and in foam.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमः सिकत्याय च प्रवाह्याय च नमः किꣳशिलाय च क्षयणाय च नमः कपर्दिने च पुलस्तये च नमऽइरिण्याय च प्रपथ्याय च ॥४३ ॥
translation: Homage to him who is in sand and to him who is in running water, homage to him who is on pebbly ground and to him who is where still water stands. Homage to him who wears braided hair and to him whose hair is smooth. Homage to him who is in deserts and to him who is on broad roads.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमो व्रज्याय च गोष्ठ्याय च नमस्तल्प्याय च गेह्याय च नमो हृदय्याय च निवेष्याय च नमः काट्याय च गह्वरेष्ठाय च ॥४४ ॥
translation: Homage to him who is in herds of cattle and to him who is in cow-pens, homage to him who is on beds and to him who is in houses. Homage to him who is in hearts, and to him who is in whirlpools, homage to him who is in wells and to him who is in abysses.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमः शुष्क्याय च हरित्याय च नमः पासव्याय च रजस्याय च नमो लोप्याय चोलप्याय च नमऽऊर्व्याय च सूर्व्याय च ॥४५ ॥
translation: Homage to him who is in dry things and to him who is in green things. Homage to him who is in dust and to him who is in vapour. Homage to him who is in inaccessible places, 64 homage to him who is in creeping plants, homage to him who is in the earth and to him who is in good soil.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नमः पर्णाय च पर्णशदाय च नमऽउद्गुरमाणाय चाभिघ्नते च नमऽआखिदते च प्रखिदते च नमऽइषुकृद्भ्यो धनुष्कृद्भ्यश्च वो नमो नमो वः किरिकेभ्यो देवाना हृदयेभ्यो नमो विचिन्वत्केभ्यो नमो विक्षिणत्केभ्यो नमऽआनिर्हतेभ्यः ॥४६ ॥
translation: Homage to him who is in leaves and to him who is in the falling of leaves. Homage to him with the threatening voice and to him who slays, homage to him who troubles and to him who afflicts. Homage to you arrow-makers and to you bow-makers, homage to you sprinklers, to the hearts of the Gods. Homage to the discerners, homage to the destroyers; homage to the indestructible.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: द्रापेऽअन्धसस्पते दरिद्र नीललोहित। आसां प्रजानामेषां पशूनां मा भेर्मा रोङ् मो च नः किं चनाममत् ॥४७ ॥
translation: Pursuer, Lord of Soma juice, thou cleaver, coloured blue and red, Cleave not, destroy not one of these our children, nor of these our beasts, let nothing that is ours be sick. 48 To the strong Rudra bring we these our songs of praise, to him the Lord of Heroes, with the braided hair, That it be well with all our cattle and our men, that in this village all be healthy and well-fed. 49 Rudra, with that auspicious form of thine which healeth every day, Auspicious, healer of disease, be kind to us that we may live.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: परि नो रुद्रस्य हेतिर्वृणक्तु परि त्वेषस्य दुर्मतिरघायोः। अव स्थिरा मघवद्भ्यस्तनुष्व मीढ्वस्तोकाय तनयाय मृड ॥५० ॥
translation: May Rudra’s missile turn aside and spare us, the great wrath of the impetuous One avoid us. Turn, Bounteous God, thy strong bow from our princes, and be thou gracious to our seed and offspring.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मीढुष्टम शिवतम शिवो नः सुमना भव। परमे वृक्षऽआयुधं निधाय कृत्तिं वसानऽआ चर पिनाकम्बिभ्रदा गहि ॥५१ ॥
