translation: Hail to breath! Hail to the Vasu! Hail to the Mighty! Hail to Vivasvân! Hail to the trooping one! Hail to the Troop’s Lord! Hail to the Superior! Hail to the Overlord! Hail to Strength! Hail to Samsarpa! Hail to the Moon! Hail to light! Hail to Malimlucha! Hail to him who flies by day!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मधवे स्वाहा माधवाय स्वाहा शुक्राय स्वाहा शुचये स्वाहा नभसे स्वाहा नभस्याय स्वाहेषाय स्वाहोर्जाय स्वाहा सहसे स्वाहा सहस्याय स्वाहा तपसे स्वाहा तपस्याय स्वाहाहसस्पतये स्वाहा ॥३१ ॥
translation: Hail to Madhu! Hail to Mâdhava! Hail to Sukra! Hail to Suchi! Hail to Nabhas! Hail to Nabhasya! Hail to Isha! Hail to Ûrja! Hail to Sahas! Hail to Sahasya! Hail to Tapas! Hail to Tapasya! Hail to Amhasaspati!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वाजाय स्वाहा प्रसवाय स्वाहापिजाय स्वाहा क्रतवे स्वाहा स्वः स्वाहा मूर्ध्ने स्वाहा व्यश्नुविने स्वाहान्त्याय स्वाहान्त्याय भौवनाय स्वाहा भुवनस्य पतये स्वाहाधिपतये स्वाहा प्रजापतये स्वाहा ॥३२ ॥
translation: Hail to Strength! Hail to impulse! Hail to After-born! Hail to will! Heaven, Hail? Hail to the head! Hail to Vyasnuvin! To the final, Hail! Hail to the mundane final! Hail to the Lord of the world! Hail to the Overlord! Hail to the Lord of Creatures!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आयुर्यज्ञेन कल्पता स्वाहा प्राणो यज्ञेन कल्पता स्वाहाऽपानो यज्ञेन कल्पता स्वाहा व्यानो यज्ञेन कल्पता स्वाहोदानो यज्ञेन कल्पता स्वाहा समानो यज्ञेन कल्पता स्वाहा चक्षुर्यज्ञेन कल्पता स्वाहा श्रोत्रं यज्ञेन कल्पता स्वाहा वाग्यज्ञेन कल्पता स्वाहा मनो यज्ञेन कल्पता स्वाहाऽऽत्मा यज्ञेन कल्पता स्वाहा ब्रह्मा यज्ञेन कल्पता स्वाहा ज्योतिर्यज्ञेन कल्पता स्वाहा स्वर्यज्ञेन कल्पता स्वाहा पृष्ठं यज्ञेन कल्पता स्वाहा यज्ञो यज्ञेन कल्पता स्वाहा ॥३३ ॥
translation: May life succeed by sacrifice, Hail! May breath succeed by sacrifice, Hail! May downward breath, diffusive. breath, upward breath, digestive breath, vision, hearing, speech, mind, self, devotion, light, heaven, hymn-arrangement, sacrifice succeed by sacrifice. All- hail!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: एकस्मै स्वाहा द्वाभ्या स्वाहा शताय स्वाहैकशताय स्वाहा व्युष्ट्यै स्वाहा स्वर्गाय स्वाहा ॥३४ ॥
translation: Hail to One! Hail to Two! Hail to Hundred! Hail to Hundred-and-One! Hail to Daybreak! Hail to Heaven! 96
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: हिरण्यगर्भः समवर्त्तताग्रे भूतस्य जातः पतिरेकऽआसीत्। स दाधार पृथिवीं द्यामुतेमां कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥१ ॥
translation: IN the beginning rose Hiranyagarbha, etc:
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उपयामगृहीतोऽसि प्रजापतये त्वा जुष्टं गृह्णाम्येष ते योनिः सूर्य्यस्ते महिमा। यस्तेऽहन्त्संवत्सरे महिमा सम्बभूव यस्ते वायावन्तरिक्षे महिमा सम्बभूव यस्ते दिवि सूर्ये महिमा सम्बभूव तस्मै ते महिम्ने प्रजापतये स्वाहा देवेभ्यः ॥२ ॥
translation: Taken upon a base art thou. I take thee welcome to Prajâpati. This is thy place: Sûrya thy majesty. The majesty that has accrued to thee in the day, in a year, that majesty which has accrued in the wind, in the firmament, to that majesty of thine, to Prajâpati, to the Gods, All- hail!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यः प्राणतो निमिषतो महित्वैकऽइद्राजा जगतो बभूव। यऽईशेऽअस्य द्विपदश्चतुष्पदः कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥३ ॥
translation: Who, by his, grandeur hath become sole Ruler of all the. moving world that breathes and slumbers; He who is Sovran of these men and cattle—what God shall we adore with our oblation?
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उपयामगृहीतोऽसि प्रजापतये त्वा जुष्टं गृह्णाम्येष ते योनिश्चन्द्रमास्ते महिमा। यस्ते रात्रौ संवत्सरे महिमा सम्बभूव यस्ते पृथिव्यामग्नौ महिमा सम्बभूव यस्ते नक्षत्रेषु चन्द्रमसि महिमा सम्बभूव तस्मैं ते महिम्ने प्रजापतये देवेभ्यः स्वाहा ॥४ ॥
translation: Taken upon a base art thou. I take thee welcome to Prajâpati, This is thy place: the Moon thy majesty. Thy majesty that has accrued to thee by night, in a year, thy majesty that has accrued in the earth, in Agni, in the stars and in the Moon, to that majesty of thine, to Prajâpati and to the Gods, All-hail!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: युञ्जन्ति ब्रध्नमरुषं चरन्तं परि तस्थुषः। रोचन्ते रोचना दिवि ॥५ ॥
translation: They who stand round hills as he moves harness the bright, the ruddy Steed: The lights are shining in the sky.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: युञ्जन्त्यस्य काम्या हरी विपक्षसा रथे। शोणा धृष्णू नृवाहसा ॥६ ॥
translation: On both sides to the car they yoke the two. Bay Coursers dear to him, Bold; tawny, bearers of the Chief.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यद्वातोऽअपोऽअगनीगन्प्रियामिन्द्रस्य तन्वम्। एतस्तोतरनेन पथा पुनरश्वमावर्त्तयासि नः ॥७ ॥
translation: When, swift as wind, the Horse has reached the form that Indra loves, the flood, Again, O singer, by this path bring thou our Courser hitherward.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वसवस्त्वाञ्जन्तु गायत्रेण छन्दसा रुद्रास्त्वाञ्जन्तु त्रैष्टुभेन छन्दसादित्यास्त्वाञ्जन्तु जागतेन छन्दसा। भूर्भुवः स्वर्लाजी३ञ्छाची३न्यव्ये गव्यऽएतदन्नमत्त देवाऽएतदन्नमद्धि प्रजापते ॥८ ॥
translation: Let the Vasus anoint thee with Gâyatrî metre. Let the Rudras anoint thee with Trishtup metre. Let the Âdityas anoint thee with Jagatî metre. Earth! Ether! Heaven! O Gods, eat this food, parched grains and groats in the product of barley and in the product of cows: eat this food, Prajâpati.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: कः स्विदेकाकी चरति कऽउ स्विज्जायते पुनः। किस्विद्धिमस्य भेषजं किम्वावपनं महत्॥९ ॥
translation: Who moveth single and alone? Who is brought forth to life again? What is the remedy of cold, or what the great receptacle?
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सूर्यऽएकाकी चरति चन्द्रमा जायते पुनः। अग्निर्हिमस्य भेषजं भूमिरावपनं महत्॥१० ॥
translation: The Sun moves single and alone. The Moon is brought to life again, Fire is the remedy of cold; Earth is the great receptacle.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: का स्विदासीत्पूर्वचित्तिः किस्विदासीद् बृहद्वयः। का स्विदासीत्पिलिप्पिला का स्विदासीत्पिशङ्गिला ॥११ ॥
translation: What was the antecedent thought? What was the bird of mighty size? The slippery matron, who was she? Who was the reddish-coloured one?
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: द्यौरासीत्पूर्वचित्तिरश्वऽआसीद् बृहद्वयः। अविरासीत्पिलिप्पिला रात्रिरासीत्पिशङ्गिला ॥१२ ॥
translation: Heaven was the antecedent thought. The Courser was the mighty bird. The slippery matron was the earth, Night was the reddish-coloured one.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वायुष्ट्वा पचतैरवत्वसितग्रीवश्छागैर्न्यग्रोधश्चमसैः शल्मलिर्वृद्ध्या। एष स्य राथ्यो वृषा पड्भिश्चतुर्भिरेदगन्ब्रह्मा कृष्णश्च नोऽवतु नमोऽग्नये ॥१३ ॥
translation: Vâyu help thee with cooked viands! Blackneck with goats; Nyagrodha with cups; Salmali with increase; this Stallion here, good for the chariot—let him verily come with his four feet. Brahmâkrishna help us! Obeisance to Agni!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सꣳशितो रश्मिना रथः सꣳशितो रश्मिना हयः। सꣳशितो अप्स्वप्सुजा ब्रह्मा सोमपुरोगवः ॥१४ ॥
translation: The car is fitted with the rein, the steed is fitted with the rein. Fitted in waters, water-born, is Brahmâ following Soma’s lead.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: स्वयं वाजिँस्तन्वं कल्पयस्व स्वयं यजस्व स्वयं जुषस्व। महिमा तेऽन्येन न सन्नशे ॥१५ ॥
translation: Steed, from thy body, of thyself, sacrifice and accept thyself. Thy greatness can be gained by none but thee. 97
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: न वाऽउऽएतन्म्रियसे न रिष्यसि देवाँ२ऽइदेषि पथिभिः सुगेभिः। यत्रासते सुकृतो यत्र ते ययुस्तत्र त्वा देवः सविता दधातु ॥१६ ॥
translation: No, here thou diest not, thou art not injured: only by fair paths to the Gods thou guest, May Savitar the God in that world place thee where dwell the pious, whether they have journeyed.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्निः पशुरासीत्तेनायजन्त सऽएतं लोकमजयद् यस्मिन्नग्निः स ते लोको भविष्यति तं जेष्यसि पिबैताऽअपः। वायुः पशुरासीत्तेनायजन्त सऽएतं लोकमजयद् यस्मिन् वायुः स ते लोको भविष्यति तं जेष्यसि पिबैताऽअपः। सूर्यः पशुरासीत्तेनायजन्त सऽएतं लोकमजयद् यस्मिन्त्सूर्य्यः स ते लोको भविष्यति तं जेष्यसि पिबैताऽअपः ॥१७ ॥
translation: Agni was the victim. With him they sacrificed. He won this world in which Agni is. This shall become thy world. This shalt thou win. Drink these waters. Vâyu was the victim. With him they sacrificed. He won this world in which Vâyu is. This shall become, etc., as above. Sûrya was the victim, etc, He won the world in which Sûrya is. This shall become, etc.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: प्राणाय स्वाहापानाय स्वाहा व्यानाय स्वाहा। अम्बेऽअम्बिकेऽम्बालिके न मा नयति कश्चन। ससस्त्यश्वकः सुभद्रिकां काम्पीलवासिनीम् ॥१८ ॥
translation: To vital breath, Hail! To out-breathing, Hail! To diffusive breath, Hail! Ambâ! Ambikâ! Ambâlikâ! No one is taking me away. The sorry horse will lie beside another, as Subhadrâ, the dweller in Kâmpila.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: गणानां त्वा गणपतिꣳहवामहे प्रियाणां त्वा प्रियपतिꣳहवामहे निधीनां त्वा निधिपतिꣳ हवामहे वसो मम। आहमजानि गर्भधमा त्वमजासि गर्भधम् ॥१९ ॥
translation: Thee we invoke, troop-lord of troops, Thee we invoke, the loved ones’ lord. Thee, lord of treasures, we invoke. My precious wealth! . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: दधिक्राव्णोऽअकारिषं जिष्णोरश्वस्य वाजिनः। सुरभि नो मुखा करत्प्र णऽआयूषि तारिषत्॥३२ ॥
translation: Now have I glorified with praise strong Dadhikrâvan, conquering steed, Sweet may he make our mouths: may he prolong the days we have to live.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: गायत्री त्रिष्टुब्जगत्यनुष्टुप्पङ्क्त्या सह। बृहत्युष्णिहा ककुप्सूचीभिः शम्यन्तु त्वा ॥३३ ॥
translation: Gâyatrî, Trishtup, Jagatî, and Pankti with Anushtup joined, Brihatî, Kakup, Ushnihâ pacify thee with needle-points!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: द्विपदा याश्चतुष्पदास्त्रिपदा याश्च षट्पदाः। विच्छन्दा याश्च सच्छन्दाः सूचीभिः शम्यन्तु त्वा ॥३४ ॥
translation: Two-footed, those that have four feet, those with three feet and those with five, Metteless, with one metre; these pacify thee with needle-points!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: महानाम्न्यो रेवत्यो विश्वा आशाः प्रभूवरीः। मैघीर्विद्युतो वाचः सूचीभिः शम्यन्तु त्वा ॥३५ ॥
translation: May Mahânâmnîs, Revatîs, all far-spread Regions of the sky, Voices, and lightnings from the cloud pacify thee with needle-points!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नार्यस्ते पत्न्यो लोम विचिन्वन्तु मनीषया। देवानां पत्न्यो दिशः सूचीभिः शम्यन्तु त्वा ॥३६ ॥
translation: May married dames of human birth skilfully separate thy hair: The Regions, Consorts of the Gods, pacify thee with needle-points!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: रजता हरिणीः सीसा युजो युज्यन्ते कर्मभिः। अश्वस्य वाजिनस्त्वचि सिमाः शम्यन्तु शम्यन्तीः ॥३७ ॥
translation: They, made of silver, gold, and lead, are used as helpers in the work. As lines on the strong Courser’s skin may they console and give thee rest.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: कुविदङ्ग यवमन्तो यवञ्चिद्यथा दान्त्यनुपूर्वं वियूय। इहेहैषां कृणुहि भोजनानि ये बर्हिषो नमऽउक्तिं यजन्ति ॥३८ ॥
translation: What then? As men whose fields are full of barley, etc., as in X. 32.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: कस्त्वाछ्यति कस्त्वा विशास्ति कस्ते गात्राणि शम्यति। कऽउ ते शमिता कविः ॥३९ ॥
translation: Who flays thee? Who dissects thee? Who prepares thy limbs for sacrifice? Who is the Sage that slaughters thee?
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ऋतवस्तऽऋतुथा पर्व शमितारो विशासतु। संवत्सरस्य तेजसा शमीभिः शम्यन्तु त्वा ॥४० ॥
translation: In due time let the seasons as thy Slaughterers divide thy joints, And with the splendour of the Year sacrifice thee with holy rites.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अर्द्धमासाः परूषि ते मासाऽआच्छ्यन्तु शम्यन्तः। अहोरात्राणि मरुतो विलिष्टꣳ सूदयन्तु ते ॥४१ ॥
translation: Let the Half-months and let the Months, while sacrificing, flay thy limbs: Let Day and Night and Maruts mend each fault in sacrificing thee.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: दैव्याऽअध्वर्यवस्त्वाच्छ्यन्तु वि च शासतु। गात्राणि पर्वशस्ते सिमाः कृण्वन्तु शम्यन्तीः ॥४२ ॥
translation: Let the divine Adhvaryus flay thy body and dissect thy frame, And let the sacrificing lines prepare thy members joint by joint,
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: द्यौस्ते पृथिव्यन्तरिक्षं वायुश्छिद्रं पृणातु ते। सूर्यस्ते नक्षत्रैः सह लोकं कृणोतु साधुया ॥४३ ॥
translation: May Sky, Earth, Air, and Wind supply each failing and defect of thine: May Sûrya with the Stars of heaven duly prepare a world for thee.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: शं ते परेभ्यो गात्रेभ्यः शमस्त्ववरेभ्यः। शमस्थभ्यो मज्जभ्यः शम्वस्तु तन्वै तव ॥४४ ॥
translation: Well be it with thine upper parts, well be it with the parts below! Well he it with thy bones and with thy marrow and with all thy frame!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: कः स्विदेकाकी चरति कऽउ स्विज्जायते पुनः। किस्विद्धिमस्य भेषजं किम्वावपनं महत्॥४५ ॥
translation: Who moveth singly? etc., as in verse 9.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सूर्य्यऽएकाकी चरति चन्द्रमा जायते पुनः। अग्निर्हिमस्य भेषजं भूमिरावपनं महत्॥४६ ॥
translation: The Sun moves singly, etc., as in verse 10.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: किꣳस्वित्सूर्यसमं ज्योतिः किꣳसमुद्रसमꣳसरः। किꣳस्वित्पृथिव्यै वर्षीयः कस्य मात्रा न विद्यते ॥४७ ॥
translation: What lustre is like Sûrya’s light? What lake is equal to the Sea? What is more spacious than the Earth? What thing is that which naught can mete? 98
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ब्रह्म सूर्यसमं ज्योतिर्द्यौः समुद्रसमꣳसरः। इन्द्रः पृथिव्यै वर्षीयान् गोस्तु मात्रा न विद्यते ॥४८ ॥
translation: Brahma is lustre like the Sea. Heaven is a flood to match the Sea. Indra is vaster than the Earth. Beyond all measure is the Cow.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: पृच्छामि त्वा चितये देवसख यदि त्वमत्र मनसा जगन्थ। येषु विष्णुस्त्रिषु पदेष्वेष्टस्तेषु विश्वं भुवनमाविवेशाँ३ऽ ॥४९ ॥
translation: Friend of the Gods, I ask, for information, if thou in spirit hast obtained the knowledge, Hath Vishnu this whole Universe pervaded in the three steps wherein the God is worshipped?
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अपि तेषु त्रिषु पदेष्वस्मि येषु विश्वं भुवनमा विवेश। सद्यः पर्येमि पृथिवीमुत द्यामेकेनाङ्गेन दिवोऽअस्य पृष्ठम् ॥५० ॥
translation: I also am in those three steps of Vishnu wherewith this Universe he permeated. The earth and heaven I circle in a moment and this heaven’s summit with a single organ.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: केष्वन्तः पुरुषऽआ विवेश कान्यन्तः पुरुषेऽअर्पितानि। एतद् ब्रह्मन्नुप वल्हामसि त्वा किस्विन्नः प्रति वोचास्यत्र ॥५१ ॥
translation: What are the things which Purusha hath entered? What things hath Purusha contained within him? This riddle we propound to thee, O Brahman. Why dost thou give no answer to my question?
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: पञ्चस्वन्तः पुरुषऽआविवेश तान्यन्तः पुरुषेऽअर्पितानि। एतत्त्वात्र प्रतिमन्वानोऽअस्मि न मायया भवस्युत्तरो मत्॥५२ ॥
translation: Within five things hath Purusha found entrance; these Purusha hath within himself connected. This is the thought which I return in answer. Thou art not my superior in wisdom.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: का स्विदासीत्पूर्वचित्तिः किस्विदासीद् बृहद्वयः। का स्विदासीत्पिलिप्पिला का स्विदासीत्पिशङ्गिला ॥५३ ॥
translation: What was the antecedent thought? etc., as in verse 11.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: द्यौरासीत्पूर्वचित्तिरश्वऽआसीद् बृहद्वयः। अविरासीत्पिलिप्पिला रात्रिरासीत्पिशङ्गिला ॥५४ ॥
translation: Heaven was the antecedent thought, etc., as in 12.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: काऽईमरे पिशङ्गिला काऽर्इं कुरुपिशङ्गिला। कऽर्इमास्कन्दमर्षति कऽर्इं पन्थां विसर्पति ॥५५ ॥
translation: Who, tell me, is the yellowish she? Who is the darkly- yellowish? Who moves with rapid spring and bound? Who glides and winds along the path?
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अजारे पिशङ्गिला श्वावित्कुरुपिशङ्गिला। शशऽआस्कन्दमर्षत्यहिः पन्थां वि सर्पति ॥५६ ॥
translation: The she-goat, Sir, is yellowish, dark-yellowish is the porcupine. The hare moves swift with leap and bound: the snake creeps winding on the path.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: कत्यस्य विष्ठाः कत्यक्षराणि कति होमासः कतिधा समिद्धः। यज्ञस्य त्वा विदथा पृच्छमत्र कति होतारऽऋतुशो यजन्ति ॥५७ ॥
translation: How many different forms hath this, how many syllables, burnt-oblations, brands for kindling? Here, of the rites of sacrifice I ask thee. How many Hotars in due season worship?
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: षडस्य विष्ठाः शतमक्षराण्यशीतिर्होमाः समिधो ह तिस्रः। यज्ञस्य ते विदथा प्र ब्रवीमि सप्त होतारऽऋतुशो यजन्ति ॥५८ ॥
translation: Sixfold its form, its syllables a hundred, eighty burnt-offerings, just three brands for kindling. To thee I tell the rites of sacrificing. Seven Hotars worship in appointed season.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: कोऽअस्य वेद भुवनस्य नाभिं को द्यावापृथिवीऽअन्तरिक्षम्। कः सूर्यस्य वेद बृहतो जनित्रं को वेद चन्द्रमसं यतोजाः ॥५९ ॥
translation: Who knoweth this world’s central point? Who knoweth the heaven, the earth, and the wide air between them? Who knows the birthplace of the mighty Sûrya? Who knows the Moon, whence he was generated?
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वेदाहमस्य भुवनस्य नाभिं वेद द्यावापृथिवीऽअन्तरिक्षम्। वेद सूर्यस्य बृहतो जनित्रमथो वेद चन्द्रमसं यतोजाः ॥६० ॥
translation: I know the centre of the world about us. I know heaven, earth, and the wide air between them. I know the birthplace of the mighty Sûrya. I know the Moon, whence he was generated.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: पृच्छामि त्वा परमन्तं पृथिव्याः पृच्छामि यत्र भुवनस्य नाभिः। पृच्छामि त्वा वृष्णोऽअश्वस्य रेतः पृच्छामि वाचः परमं व्योम ॥६१ ॥
translation: I ask thee of the earth’s extremest limit, where is the centre of the world, I ask thee. I ask thee of the Stallion’s genial humour, I ask of highest heaven where Speech abideth.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इयं वेदिः परोऽअन्तः पृथिव्याऽअयं यज्ञो भुवनस्य नाभिः। अयꣳ सोमो वृष्णोऽअश्वस्य रेतो ब्रह्मायं वाचः परमं व्योम ॥६२ ॥
translation: This altar is the earth’s extremest limit; this sacrifice of ours is the world’s centre. This Soma is the Stallion’s genial humour, this Brahman highest heaven where Speech abideth.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सुभूः स्वयम्भूः प्रथमोऽन्तर्महत्यर्णवे। दधे ह गर्भमृत्वियं यतो जातः प्रजापतिः ॥६३ ॥
translation: The Strong, the Self-existent One, the First, within the mighty flood Laid down the timely embryo from which Prajâpati was born.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षत्प्रजापतिꣳ सोमस्य महिम्नः। जुषतां पिबतु सोमꣳ होतर्यज ॥६४ ॥
translation: Let the Hotar sacrifice to Prajâpati from the Mahiman-Soma. Let him accept. Let him drink the Soma. Hotar, sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: प्रजापते न त्वदेतान्यन्यो विश्वा रूपाणि परि ता बभूव। यत्कामास्ते जुहुमस्तन्नोऽअस्तु वयꣳ स्याम पतयो रयीणाम् ॥६५ ॥
translation: Prajâpati, thou only, etc., as in X. 20. 99
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अश्वस्तूपरो गोमृगस्ते प्राजापत्याः कृष्णग्रीवऽआग्नेयो रराटे पुरस्तात्सारस्वती मेष्यधस्ताद्धन्वोराश्विनावधोरामौ बाह्वोः सौमापौष्णः श्यामो नाभ्या सौर्ययामौ श्वेतश्च कृष्णश्च पार्श्वयोस्त्वाष्ट्रौ लोमशसक्थौ सक्थ्योर्वायव्यः श्वेतः पुच्छऽइन्द्राय स्वपस्याय वेहद्वैष्णवो वामनः ॥१ ॥
translation: HORSE, hornless goat, Gomriga, these belong to Prajâpati. A black-necked goat, devoted to Agni, (is to be bound) in front to the forehead (of the horse); Sarasvatî’s ewe below his jaws; two goats belonging to the Asvins, with marks on the lower parts of the body, to his fore- legs; a dark-coloured goat, Soma’s and Pûshan’s, to his navel; a white and a black, sacred to Soma and Varna, to his sides; Tvashtar’s two, with bushy tails, to his hind feet; Vâyu’s white goat to his tail; for Indra the Good Worker a cow who slips her calf; a dwarf belonging to Vishnu.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: रोहितो धूम्ररोहितः कर्कन्धुरोहितस्ते सौम्या बभ्रुररुणबभ्रुः शुकबभ्रुस्ते वारुणाः शितिरन्ध्रोऽन्यतःशितिरन्ध्रः समन्तशितिरन्ध्रस्ते सावित्राः शितिबाहुरन्यतःशितिबाहुः समन्तशितिबाहुस्ते बार्हस्पत्याः पृषती क्षुद्रपृषती स्थूलपृषती ता मैत्रावरुण्यः ॥२ ॥
translation: The red goat, the smoky-red, the jujube-red, these belong to Soma. The brown, the ruddy- brown, the parrot-brown, these are Varuna’s. One with white ear holes, one with partly white, one with wholly white, belong to Savitar. One with fore feet white, partly white, wholly white, belongs to Brihaspati. She goats speckled, with small spots, with big spots, these belong to Mitra-Varuna.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: शुद्धवालः सर्वशुद्धवालो मणिवालस्तऽआश्विनाः श्येतः श्येताक्षोऽरुणस्ते रुद्राय पशुपतये कर्णा यामाऽअवलिप्ता रौद्रा नभोरूपाः पार्जन्याः ॥३ ॥
translation: The bright-tailed, the wholly bright-tailed, the jewel-tailed, these belong to the Asvins. The white, the white-eyed, the reddish, these are for Rudra Lord of Beasts. Long-eared goats are for Yama; proud ones for Rudra; cloud-coloured ones for Parjanya.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: पृश्निस्तिरश्चीनपृश्निरूर्ध्वपृश्निस्ते मारुताः फल्गूर्लोहितोर्णी पलक्षी ताः सारस्वत्यः प्लीहाकर्णः शुण्ठाकर्णोऽध्यालोहकर्णस्ते त्वाष्ट्राः कृष्णग्रीवः शितिकक्षोऽञ्जिसक्थस्तऽऐन्द्राग्नाः कृष्णाञ्जिरल्पाञ्जिर्महाञ्जिस्तऽउषस्याः ॥४ ॥
translation: Goats speckled, transversely speckled, upward speckled are for the Maruts. The reddish she-goat, the red-haired, the white, these belong to Sarasvatî. The goat with diseased ears, the short-eared, the red eared are Tvashtar’s. The black-necked, the white-flanked, one with bright-coloured thighs belong to Indra and Agni. Those with black marks, small marks, large marks belong to Dawn.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: शिल्पा वैश्वदेव्यो रोहिण्यस्त्र्यवयो वाचेऽविज्ञाताऽअदित्यै सरूपा धात्रे वत्सतर्यो देवानां पत्नीभ्यः ॥५ ॥
translation: Parti-coloured female victims belong to the All-Gods; red-coloured, eighteen mouths old to Vâk; victims without distinguishing marks to Aditi; those of one same colour to Dhâtar; weaned kids sacred to the Consorts of the Gods.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: कृष्णग्रीवा आग्नेयाः शितिभ्रवो वसूना रोहिता रुद्राणा श्वेताऽअवरोकिणऽ आदित्यानां नभोरूपाः पार्जन्याः ॥६ ॥
translation: Black-necked victims for Agni; white browed for the Vasus; red for Rudra; bright ones for the Âdityas; cloud-coloured for Parjanya.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उन्नत ऋषभो वामनस्तऽऐन्द्रावैष्णवाऽउन्नतः शितिबाहुः शितिपृष्ठस्तऽऐन्द्राबार्हस्पत्याः शुकरूपा वाजिनाः कल्माषाऽआग्निमारुताः श्यामाः पौष्णाः ॥७ ॥
translation: The tall goat, the sturdy, the dwarf, these are Indra-Vishnu’s; the tall, the white fore-footed, the black-backed, Indra-Brihaspati’s; parrot-coloured the Vâjins’; speckled Agni-Maruts’; dark-coloured Pûshan’s.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: एताऽऐन्द्राग्ना द्विरूपाऽअग्नीषोमीया वामनाऽअनड्वाहऽ आग्नावैष्णवा वशा मैत्रावरुण्योऽन्यतऽएन्यो मैत्र्यः ॥८ ॥
translation: Variegated, Indra-Agni’s; two-coloured, Agni-Soma’s; dwarf oxen, Agni-Vishnu’s; barren cows, Mitra-Varuna’s; partly variegated, Mitra’s.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: कृष्णग्रीवाऽआग्नेया बभ्रवः सौम्याः श्वेता वायव्याऽअविज्ञाताऽअदित्यै सरूपा धात्रे वत्सतर्यो देवानां पत्नीभ्यः ॥९ ॥
translation: Black-necked ones, Agni’s; brown, Soma’s; white, Vâyu’s; undistinguished, Aditi’s; self- coloured, Dhâtar’s; weanlings, the Gods’ Consorts’.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: कृष्णा भौमा धूम्राऽआन्तरिक्षा बृहन्तो दिव्याः शबला वैद्युताः सिध्मास्तारकाः ॥१० ॥
translation: Black ones for Earth; smoke-coloured for Firmament; tall ones for Sky; brindled ones for Lightning; blotched ones for Stars.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: धूम्रान् वसन्तायालभते श्वेतान् ग्रीष्माय कृष्णान् वर्षाभ्योऽरुणाञ्छरदे पृषतो हेमन्ताय पिशङ्गाञ्छिशिराय ॥११ ॥
translation: Smoke-coloured ones he sacrifices to Spring; white to Summer; black to the Rains; red ones to Autumn; speckled to Winter; reddish-yellow to the Dewy Season.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: त्र्यवयो गायत्र्यै पञ्चावयस्त्रिष्टुभे दित्यवाहो जगत्यै त्रिवत्साऽअनुष्टुभे तुर्यवाहऽउष्णिहे ॥१२ ॥
translation: Calves eighteen months old to Gâyatrî; steers of two and a half years to Trishtup; two year old steers to Jagatî; three year olds to Anushtup; four year olds to Ushnih.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: पष्ठवाहो विराजऽउक्षाणो बृहत्याऽऋषभाः ककुभेऽनड्वाहः पङ्क्त्यै धेनवोऽतिछन्दसे ॥१३ ॥
translation: Four year old steers to Virâj; full grown bulls to Brihatî; strong bulls to Kakup; draught oxen to Pankti; milch-cows to Atichhandas. 100
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: कृष्णग्रीवाऽआग्नेया बभ्रवः सौम्याऽउपध्वस्ताः सावित्रा वत्सतर्यः सारस्वत्यः श्यामाः पौष्णाः पृश्नयो मारुता बहुरूपा वैश्वदेवा वशा द्यावापृथिवीयाः ॥१४ ॥
translation: Black-necked victims sacred to Agni; brown to Soma; spotted to Savitar; weaned she-kids to Sarasvatî; dark-coloured goats to Pûshan; speckled victims to the Maruts; many-coloured to the All-Gods; barren cows to Heaven and Earth.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उक्ताः सञ्चराऽएताऽऐन्द्राग्नाः कृष्णा वारुणाः पृश्नयो मारुताः कायास्तूपराः ॥१५ ॥
translation: Called contemporary, the dappled belong to Indra-Agni; black ones to Varuna; speckled to the Maruts; hornless he-goats to Ka.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्नयेऽनीकवते प्रथमजानालभते मरुद्भ्यः सान्तपनेभ्यः सवात्यान् मरुद्भ्यो गृहमेधिभ्यो बष्किहान् मरुद्भ्यः क्रीडिभ्यः सꣳसृष्टान् मरुद्भ्यः स्वतवद्भ्योऽनुसृष्टान् ॥१६ ॥
translation: To Agni foremost in place he sacrifices firstling goats; to the consuming Maruts those born of one mother; to the Maruts who perform domestic rites those born after a long time; to the sportive Maruts those born together; to the self-strong Maruts those born in succession.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उक्ताः सञ्चराऽएताऽऐन्द्राग्नाः प्राशृङ्गा माहेन्द्रा बहुरूपा वैश्वकर्मणाः ॥१७ ॥
translation: Called contemporaneous, the dappled belonging to Indra-Agni; those with projecting horns to Mahendra; the many-coloured to Visvakarman.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: धूम्रा बभ्रुनीकाशाः पितॄणासोमवतां बभ्रवो धूम्रनीकाशाः पितॄणां बर्हिषदां कृष्णा बभ्रुनीकाशाः पितॄणामग्निष्वात्तानां कृष्णाः पृषन्तस्त्रैयम्बकाः ॥१८ ॥
translation: Smoke-coloured, those of brownish hue, to be offered to the Soma-possessing Fathers; the brown and the smoky-looking to the Fathers who sit on sacred grass; the black and the brownish-looking to the Fathers who have been tasted by Agni; the black and the spotted belong to Tryambaka.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उक्ताः सञ्चराऽएताः शुनासीरीयाः श्वेता वायव्याः श्वेताः सौर्याः ॥१९ ॥
translation: Called contemporaneous, the dappled belong to Suna and Sîra; white ones to Vâyu; white ones to Sûrya.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वसन्ताय कपिञ्जलानालभते ग्रीष्माय कलविङ्कान् वर्षाभ्यस्तित्तिरीञ्छरदे वर्त्तिका हेमन्ताय ककराञ्छिशिराय विककरान् ॥२० ॥
translation: To Spring he offers Kapiñjalas; to Summer sparrows; to the Rains partridges; to Autumn quails; to Winter. Kakaras; to the Dewy Season Vikakaras.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: समुद्राय शिशुमारानालभते पर्जन्याय मण्डूकानद्भ्यो मत्स्यान् मित्राय कुलीपयान् वरुणाय नाक्रान् ॥२१ ॥
translation: To the Sea he sacrifices porpoises; to Parjanya frogs; to the Waters fishes; to Mitra Kulîpayas; to Varuna crocodiles.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सोमाय हꣳसानालभते वायवे बलाकाऽइन्द्राग्निभ्यां क्रुञ्चान् मित्राय मद्गून् वरुणाय चक्रवाकान् ॥२२ ॥
translation: To Soma he sacrifices wild geese; to Vâyu female cranes; to Indra-Agni curlews; to Mitra divers; to Varuna Chakravâkas.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्नये कुटरूनालभते वनस्पतिभ्यऽउलूकानग्नीषोमाभ्यां चाषानश्विभ्यां मयूरान् मित्रावरुणाभ्यां कपोतान् ॥२३ ॥
translation: To Agni he sacrifices cocks; to Vanaspatis owls; to Agni-Soma blue jays; to the Asvins peacocks; to Mitra-Varuna pigeons.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सोमाय लबानालभते त्वष्ट्रे कौलीकान् गोषादीर्देवानां पत्नीभ्यः कुलीका देवजामिभ्योऽग्नये गृहपतये पारुष्णान् ॥२४ ॥
translation: To Soma he sacrifices quails; to Tvashtar Kaulîkas; Mainas to the Gods’ Consorts; Kulîkas to the Gods’ Sisters; Pârushnas to Agni Lord of the Homestead.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अह्ने पारावतानालभते रात्र्यै सीचापूरहोरात्रयोः सन्धिभ्यो जतूर्मासेभ्यो दात्यौहान्त्संवत्सराय महतः सुपर्णान् ॥२५ ॥
translation: To Day he sacrifices doves; to Night Sîchâpûs; to the Joints of Day and Night bats; to the Months gallinules; to the Year great eagles.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: भूम्याऽआखूनालभतेऽन्तरिक्षाय पाङ्क्तान् दिवे कशान् दिग्भ्यो नकुलान् बभ्रुकानवान्तरदिशाभ्यः ॥२६ ॥
translation: To Ground he sacrifices rats; to Firmament field-rats; to Day voles; to the Quarters mungooses; to the Intermediate Spaces brownish ichneumons.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वसुभ्यऽऋश्यानालभते रुद्रेभ्यो रुरूनादित्येभ्यो न्यङ्कून् विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यः पृषतान्त्साध्येभ्यः कुलुङ्गान् ॥२७ ॥
translation: To the Vasus he sacrifices black-bucks; to the Rudras stags; to the Âdityas Nyanku deer; to the All-Gods spotted deer; to the Sâdhyas Kulinga antelopes,
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ईशानाय त्वा परस्वतऽआ लभते मित्राय गौरान् वरुणाय महिषान् बृहस्पतये गवयाँस्त्वष्ट्र उष्ट्रान् ॥२८ ॥
translation: To Îsâna he sacrifices wild asses; to Mitra Gauras; to Varuna buffaloes; to Brihaspati Gayals; to Tvashtar camels.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: प्रजापतये पुरुषान् हस्तिनऽआ लभते वाचे प्लुषीँश्चक्षुषे मशकाञ्छ्रोत्राय भृङ्गाः ॥२९ ॥
translation: To Prajâpati he sacrifices men elephants; to Vâk white ants; to Sight flies; to Hearing black bees.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: प्रजापतये च वायवे च गोमृगो वरुणायारण्यो मेषो यमाय कृष्णो मनुष्यराजाय मर्कटः शार्दूलाय रोहिदृषभाय गवयी क्षिप्रश्येनाय वर्त्तिका नीलङ्गोः कृमिः समुद्राय शिशुमारो हिमवते हस्ती ॥३० ॥
translation: To Prajâpati and to Vâyu a Gayal is to be offered; to Varuna a wild ram; to Yama a black ram; to a human king a monkey; to the Tiger a red doe; to the Bull a female Gayal, to the Kshiprasyena a quail; to the Nilangu a worm; to the Sea a porpoise; to the Snowy Mountain an elephant.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मयुः प्राजापत्यऽउलो हलिक्ष्णो वृषदꣳशस्ते धात्रे दिशां कङ्को धुङ्क्षाग्नेयी कलविङ्को लोहिताहिः पुष्करसादस्ते त्वाष्ट्रा वाचे क्रुञ्चः ॥३१ ॥
translation: The Kinnara belongs to Prajâpati; the Ula, the Halikshna, the cat belong to Dhâtar; the heron belongs to the Quarters; the Dhunkshâ to Agni; sparrow, red snake, Sâras, these are Tvashtar’s; the curlew belongs to Vâk. 101
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सोमाय कुलुङ्गऽआरण्योऽजो नकुलः शका ते पौष्णाः क्रोष्टा मायोरिन्द्रस्य गौरमृगः पिद्वो न्यङ्कुः कक्कटस्तेऽनुमत्यै प्रतिश्रुत्कायै चक्रवाकः ॥३२ ॥
translation: To Soma an antelope is to be offered; wild goat, mungoose, Sakâ. these are Pûshan’s; the jackal is the Mâyu’s; the Gaura Indra’s; Pidva, antelope, cock, these are Anumati’s; the Chakravâka is for Echo.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सौरी बलाका शार्गः सृजयः शयाण्डकस्ते मैत्राः सरस्वत्यै शारिः पुरुषवाक्श्वाविद् द्भौमी शार्दूलो वृकः पृदाकुस्ते मन्यवे सरस्वते शुकः पुरुषवाक्॥३३ ॥
translation: The female crane is Sûrya’s; Sârga, Srijays, Sayândaka, these are Mitra’s; to Sarasvatî belongs the human-voiced Maina; to Ground the porcupine; tiger, wolf, viper belong to Passion; to Sarasvân the human-voiced parrot.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सुपर्णः पार्जन्यऽआतिर्वाहसो दर्विदा ते वायवे बृहस्पतये वाचस्पतये पैङ्गराजोऽलजऽआन्तरिक्षः प्लवो मद्गुर्मत्स्यस्ते नदीपतये द्यावापृथिवीयः कूर्मः ॥३४ ॥
translation: The eagle is Parjanya’s; the Âti, the Vâhasa, the wood-pecker, these are for Vâyu; for Brihaspati Lord of Speech is the Paingarâja; the Alaja belongs to Firmament; pelican, cormorant, fish, these belong to the Lord of Rivers; the tortoise belongs to Heaven and Earth.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: पुरुषमृगश्चन्द्रमसो गोधा कालका दार्वाघाटस्ते वनस्पतीनां कृकवाकुः सावित्रो हꣳसो वातस्य नाक्रो मकरः कुलीपयस्तेऽकूपारस्य ह्रियै शल्यकः ॥३५ ॥
translation: The book belongs to the Moon; iguana, Kâlakâ, woodpecker, these belong to the Vanaspatis; the cock belongs to Savitar; the swan is Vâta’s; crocodile, dolphin, Kulîpaya, these belong to the Sea; the porcupine to Modesty.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: एण्यह्नो मण्डूको मूषिका तित्तिरिस्ते सर्पाणां लोपाशऽआश्विनः कृष्णो रात्र्याऽऋक्षो जतूः सुषिलीका तऽइतरजनानां जहका वैष्णवी ॥३६ ॥
translation: The Black-doe belongs to Day; frog, female rat, partridge, these belong to the Serpents; the jackal belongs to the Asvins; the Black-buck to Night; bear, bat, Sushilikâ, these belong to the Other Folk (i.e. fairies--JBH); the polecat belongs to Vishnu.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अन्यवापोऽर्द्धमासानामृश्यो मयूरः सुपर्णस्ते गन्धर्वाणामपामुद्रो मासान् कश्यपो रोहित्कुण्डृणाची गोलत्तिका तेऽप्सरसां मृत्यवेऽसितः ॥३७ ॥
translation: The cuckoo belongs to the Half Months; antelope, peacock, eagle, these are the Gandharvas’; the otter belongs to the Months; tortoise, doe-antelope, iguana, Golathikâ belong to the Apsarases; the black snake belongs to Death.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वर्षाहूर्ऋतूनामाखुः कशो मान्थालस्ते पितॄणां बलायाजगरो वसूनां कपिञ्जलः कपोतऽउलूकः शशस्ते निर्ऋत्यै वरुणायारण्यो मेषः ॥३८ ॥
translation: The frog belongs to the Seasons; the vole, the rat, the mouse, these are the Fathers’; the Python, the Balâva belong to the Vasus; Kapiñjala, pigeons owl, hare belong to Nirriti; the wild ram to Varuna.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: श्वित्रऽआदित्यानामुष्ट्रो घृणीवान् वार्ध्रीनसस्ते मत्याऽअरण्याय सृमरो रुरू रौद्रः क्वयिः कुटरुर्दात्यौहस्ते वाजिनां कामाय पिकः ॥३९ ॥
translation: The white animal belongs to the Âdityas; the camel, the Ghrintîvân, the rhinoceros to Mati; the Srimara belong to the Forest-God; the Raru buck is Rudra’s; Kvayi, cock, gallinule, these are the Vâjins’; the cuckoo belongs to Kâma.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: खड्गो वैश्वदेवः श्वा कृष्णः कर्णो गर्दभस्तरक्षुस्ते रक्षसामिन्द्राय सूकरः सिꣳहो मारुतः कृकलासः पिप्पका शकुनिस्ते शरव्यायै विश्वेषां देवानां पृषतः ॥४० ॥
translation: The Khanga is the All-Gods’; the black dog, the long eared, the ass, the hyena, these are the Râkshasas; the boar is for Indra; the lion is for the Maruts; the chameleon, the Pipoaka, the vulture, these belong to Saravyâ; the spotted antelope belongs to the All-Gods. 102
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: शादं दद्भिरवकां दन्तमूलैर्मृदं बर्स्वैस्ते गां दष्ट्राभ्यासरस्वत्याऽअग्रजिह्वं जिह्वायाऽ उत्सादमवक्रन्देन तालु वाजꣳहनुभ्यामपऽआस्येन वृषणमाण्डाभ्यामादित्याँ श्मश्रुभिः पन्थानं भ्रूभ्यां द्यावापृथिवी वर्त्तोभ्यां विद्युतं कनीनकाभ्या शुक्राय स्वाहा कृष्णाय स्वाहा पार्याणि पक्ष्माण्यवार्याऽइक्षवोऽवार्याणि पक्ष्माणि पार्या इक्षवः ॥१ ॥
translation: I GRATIFY Fresh Grass with his teeth, Avakâ with his gums, Clay with his tooth-sockets, Tegas with his fangs. The tongue-tip for Sarasvatî; I gratify the root of the tongue and the palate with his neigh, Vâja with his jaws, the Waters with his mouth, the Stallion with his testicles, the Âdityas with the beard, Path with his eyebrows, Heaven and Earth with his eyelashes, Lightning with the pupils of his eyes. Hail to the white! Hail to the black! Effectual are his eyelashes, irresistible are his lower eyelashes; irresistible are his eyelashes, effectual are his lower eyelashes.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वातं प्राणेनापानेन नासिकेऽउपयाममधरेणौष्ठेन सदुत्तरेण प्रकाशेनान्तरमनूकाशेन बाह्यं निवेष्यं मूर्ध्ना स्तनयित्नुं निर्बाधेनाशनिं मस्तिष्केण विद्युतं कनीनकाभ्यां कर्णाभ्या श्रोत्र श्रोत्राभ्यां कर्णौ तेदनीमधरकण्ठेनापः शुष्ककण्ठेन चित्तं मन्याभिरदितिꣳ शीर्ष्णा निर्ऋतिं निर्जर्जल्पेन शीर्ष्णा संक्रोशैः प्राणान् रेष्माण स्तुपेन ॥२ ॥
translation: With his breath I gratify Vâta; with his outbreath the two Nostrils; with his lower lip the Upayâma; with his upper lip Existence. With his bright look I please Antara, with his reflection Bâhya; the Whirlpool with his head; Thunder with his frontal bone; the Lightning- flash with his brain; Lightning with the pupils of his eyes; Hearing with his external ears; Ears with his internal ears; Blood with his lower neck; Waters with the fleshless part of his neck; Thought with the back neck-tendons; Aditi with his head; Nirriti with his ragged head; Vital Breathings with his roars; Tempest with his crest.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मशकान् केशैरिन्द्र स्वपसा वहेन बृहस्पतिꣳशकुनिसादेन कूर्म्माञ्छफैराक्रमण स्थूराभ्यामृक्षलाभिः कपिञ्जलाञ्जवं जङ्घाभ्यामध्वानं बाहुभ्यां जाम्बीलेनारण्यमग्निमतिरुग्भ्यां पूषणं दोर्भ्यामश्विनावꣳसाभ्या रुद्रꣳ रोराभ्याम् ॥३ ॥
translation: I gratify Flies with his hair; Indra with his active shoulder; Brihaspati with his quick spring; Tortoises with his hoofs; Approach with his fetlocks; Kapiñjalas with his heel-ropes; Speed with his two thighs; the Way with his two fore-legs; the Forest-God with a kneepan; Agni with his two knees; Pûshan with his two fore-feet; the Asvins with his shoulders; Rudra with his shoulder-joints,
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्नेः पक्षतिर्वायोर्निपक्षतिरिन्द्रस्य तृतीया सोमस्य चतुर्थ्यदित्यै पञ्चमीन्द्राण्यै षष्ठी मरुता सप्तमी बृहस्पतेरष्टम्यर्यम्णो नवमी धातुर्दशमीन्द्रस्यैकादशी वरुणस्य द्वादशी यमस्य त्रयोदशी ॥४ ॥
translation: The first rib is Agni’s; the second Vâyu’s; the third Indra’s; the fourth Soma’s; the fifth Aditi’s; the sixth Indrânî’s; the seventh the Maruts’; the eighth Brihaspati’s; the ninth Aryaman’s; the tenth Dhâtar’s; the eleventh Indra’s; the twelfth Varuna’s; the thirteenth Yama’s.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इन्द्राग्न्योः पक्षतिः सरस्वत्यै निपक्षतिर्मित्रस्य तृतीयाऽपां चतुर्थी निर्ऋत्यै पञ्चम्यग्नीषोमयोः षष्ठी सर्पाणा सप्तमी विष्णोरष्टमी पूष्णो नवमी त्वष्टुर्दशमीन्द्रस्यैकादशी वरुणस्य द्वादशी यम्यै त्रयोदशी द्यावापृथिव्योर्दक्षिणं पार्श्वं विश्वेषां देवानामुत्तरम् ॥५ ॥
translation: (On the left side) the first rib belongs to Indra-Agni; the second to Sarasvatî; the third to Mitra; the fourth to the Waters; the fifth to Nirriti; the sixth to Agni-Soma; the seventh to the Serpents; the eighth to Vishnu; the ninth to Pûshan; the tenth to Tvashtar; the eleventh to Indra; the twelfth to Varuna; the thirteenth to Yama. The right flank belongs to Heaven and Earth, the left to the All-Gods.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मरुता स्कन्धा विश्वेषां देवानां प्रथमा कीकसा रुद्राणां द्वितीयाऽऽदित्यानां तृतीया वायोः पुच्छमग्नीषोमयोर्भासदौ क्रुञ्चौ श्रोणिभ्यामिन्द्राबृहस्पतीऽऊरुभ्यां मित्रावरुणावल्गाभ्यामाक्रमण स्थूराभ्यां बलं कुष्ठाभ्याम् ॥६ ॥
translation: The shoulders belong to the Maruts; the first rib-cartilages to the All-Gods; the second to the Rudras; the third to the Âdityas; the tail belongs to Vâyu; the hind-quarters to Agni-Soma. I gratify the two Curlews with the hips; Indra-Brihaspati with the thighs; Mitra-Varuna with the groins; Approach with the buttocks; Strength with the two cavities of the loins.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: पूषणं वनिष्ठुनान्धाहीन्त्स्स्थूलगुदया सर्पान् गुदाभिर्विह्रुतऽआन्त्रैरपो वस्तिना वृषणमाण्डाभ्यां वाजिनꣳ शेपेन प्रजा रेतसा चाषान् पित्तेन प्रदरान् पायुना कूश्माञ्छकपिण्डैः ॥७ ॥
translation: I gratify Pûshan with the rectum; Blind-worms with the large intestines; Serpents with the entrails; Worms with the guts; the Waters with the bladder; Scrotum with the testicles; the Vâjins with his penis; Offspring with his seed; Blue jays with his bile; Fissures with his arms; Kûshmas with his lumps of dung.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इन्द्रस्य क्रोडोऽदित्यै पाजस्यं दिशां जत्रवोऽदित्यै भसज्जीमूतान् हृदयौपशेनान्तरिक्षं पुरीतता नभऽउदर्येण चक्रवाकौ मतस्नाभ्यां दिवं वृक्काभ्यां गिरीन् प्लाशिभिरुपलान् प्लीह्ना वल्मीकान् क्लोमभिर्ग्लौभिर्गुल्मान् हिराभिः स्रवन्तीर्ह्रदान् कुक्षिभ्या समुद्रमुदरेण वैश्वानरं भस्मना ॥८ ॥
translation: His chest belongs to Indra; his belly to Aditi; his clavicles to the Quarters; his nether hind- part to Aditi. I gratify Clouds with his aorta; Firmament with his pericardium; Mist with his belly; the two Chakravâkas with his cardiac bones; Sky with his kidneys; Mountains with his ducts; hocks with his spleen; Ant-hills with his lungs; Shrubs with his heart-vessels; Streams with his veins; Lakes with his flanks; Sea with his belly; Vaisvânara with his ashes. 103
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: विधृतिं नाभ्या घृतꣳरसेनापो यूष्णा मरीचीर्विप्रुड्भिर्नीहारमूष्मणा शीनं वसया प्रुष्वाऽ अश्रुभिर्ह्रादुनीर्दूषीकाभिरस्ना रक्षासि चित्राण्यङ्गैर्नक्षत्राणि रूपेण पृथिवीं त्वचा जुम्बकाय स्वाहा ॥९ ॥
translation: I gratify Separation with his navel; Butter with his flavour; the Waters with his broth; Sunbeams with his drops of fat; Hoar-frost with his heat; Ice with his marrow; Hailstones with his tears; Thunderbolts with the rheum of his eyes; Râkshasas with his blood; Bright things with his limbs; Stars with his beauty; Earth with his skin. All-hail to Jumbaka!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: हिरण्यगर्भः समवर्त्तताग्रे भूतस्य जातः पतिरेकऽआसीत्। स दाधार पृथिवीं द्यामुतेमां कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥१० ॥
translation: In the beginning rose Hiranyagarbha, etc., as in XIII. 4; XXIII. 1.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यः प्राणतो निमिषतो महित्वैकऽइद्राजा जगतो बभूव। य ईशेऽअस्य द्विपदश्चतुष्पदः कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥११ ॥
translation: Who by his grandeur, etc., as in XXIII. 3.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यस्येमे हिमवन्तो महित्वा यस्य समुद्रꣳ रसया सहाहुः। यस्येमाः प्रदिशो यस्य बाहू कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥ ॥१२ ॥
translation: Whose, by his might, are these snow-covered mountains, and men call sea and Rasâ his possession: Whose are these arms, whose are these heavenly regions. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यऽआत्मदा बलदा यस्य विश्वऽउपासते प्रशिषं यस्य देवाः। यस्य छायाऽमृतं यस्य मृत्युः कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥१३ ॥
translation: Giver of vital breath, of power and vigour, he whose commandment all the Gods acknowledge: The Lord of death, whose shade is life immortal. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आ नो भद्राः क्रतवो यन्तु विश्वतोऽदब्धासोऽअपरीतासऽउद्भिदः। देवा नो यथा सदमिद् वृधेऽअसन्नप्रायुवो रक्षितारो दिवेदिवे ॥१४ ॥
translation: May powers auspicious come to us from every side, never deceived, unhindered and victorious, That the Gods ever may be with us for our gain, our guardians day by day, unceasing in their care.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवानां भद्रा सुमतिर्ऋजूयतां देवाना रातिरभि नो निवर्त्तताम्। देवाना सख्यमुपसेदिमा वयं देवा नऽआयुः प्रतिरन्तु जीवसे ॥१५ ॥
translation: May the auspicious favour of the Gods be ours, on us descend the bounty of the righteous Gods. The friendship of the Gods have we devoutly sought: so may the Gods extend our life that we may live.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तान् पूर्वया निविदा हूमहे वयं भगं मित्रमदितिं दक्षमस्रिधम्। अर्यमणं वरुणꣳ सोममश्विना सरस्वती नः सुभगा मयस्करत्॥१६ ॥
translation: We call them hither with a hymn of olden time, Bhaga, the friendly Daksha, Mitra, Aditi, Aryaman, Varuna, Soma, the Asvins. May Sarasvatî, auspicious, grant felicity.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तन्नो वातो मयोभु वातु भेषजं तन्माता पृथिवी तत्पिता द्यौः। तद्ग्रावाणः सोमसुतो मयोभुवस्तदश्विना शृणुतं धिष्ण्या युवम् ॥१७ ॥
translation: May the Wind waft to us that pleasant medicine, may Earth our Mother give it, and our Father Heaven, And the joy-giving stones that press the Soma’s juice. Asvins, may ye, for whom our spirits long, hear this.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तमीशानं जगतस्तस्थुषस्पतिं धियञ्जिन्वमवसे हूमहे वयम्। पूषा नो यथा वेदसामसद् वृधे रक्षिता पायुरदब्धः स्वस्तये ॥१८ ॥
translation: Him we invoke for aid who reigns supreme, the Lord of all that stands or moves, inspirer of the soul, That Pûshan may promote the increase of our wealth, our keeper and our guard infallible for our good.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: स्वस्ति नऽइन्द्रो वृद्धश्रवाः स्वस्ति नः पूषा विश्ववेदाः। स्वस्ति नस्तार्क्ष्योऽअरिष्टनेमिः स्वस्ति नो बृहस्पतिर्दधातु ॥१९ ॥
translation: Illustrious far and wide, may Indra prosper us: may Pûshan prosper us, the Master of all wealth. May Târkshya with uninjured fellies prosper us: Brihaspati vouchsafe to us prosperity.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: पृषदश्वा मरुतः पृश्निमातरः शुभं यावानो विदथेषु जग्मयः। अग्निजिह्वा मनवः सूरचक्षसो विश्वे नो देवाऽअवसागमन्निह ॥२० ॥
translation: The Maruts, Sons of Prisni, borne by spotted steeds, moving in glory, oft visiting holy rites, Sages whose tongue is Agni and their eyes the Sun,——hither let all the Gods for our protection come.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: भद्रं कर्णेभिः शृणुयाम देवा भद्रं पश्येमाक्षभिर्यजत्राः। स्थिरैरङ्गैस्तुष्टुवासस्तनूभिर्व्यशेमहि देवहितं यदायुः ॥२१ ॥
translation: Gods, may we with our ears listen to what is good, and with our eyes see what is good, ye Holy Ones. With limbs and bodies firm may we extolling you attain the term of life appointed by the Gods.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: शतमिन्नु शरदोऽअन्ति देवा यत्रा नश्चक्रा जरसं तनूनाम्। पुत्रासो यत्र पितरो भवन्ति मा नो मध्या रीरिषतायुर्गन्तोः ॥२२ ॥
translation: A hundred autumns stand before us, O ye Gods, within whose space ye bring our bodies to decay; Within whose space our sons become fathers in turn. Break ye not in the midst our course of fleeting life.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अदितिर्द्यौरदितिरन्तरिक्षमदितिर्माता स पिता स पुत्रः। विश्वे देवाऽअदितिः पञ्च जनाऽअदितिर्जातमदितिर्जनित्वम् ॥२३ ॥
translation: Aditi is the heaven, Aditi is mid-air, Aditi is the Mother and the Sire and Son. Aditi is all Gods, Aditi five-classed men, Aditi all that hath been born and shall be born.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मा नो मित्रो वरुणोऽअर्यमायुरिन्द्रऽऋभुक्षा मरुतः परिख्यन्। यद्वाजिनो देवजातस्य सप्तेः प्रवक्ष्यामो विदथे वीर्याणि ॥२४ ॥
translation: Slight us not Varuna, Aryaman, or Mitra, Ribhukshan, Indra, Âyu, or the Maruts, When we declare amid the congregation the virtues of the Strong Steed, God-descended. 104
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यन्निर्णिजा रेक्णसा प्रावृतस्य रातिं गृभीतां मुखतो नयन्ति। सुप्राङजो मेम्यद्विश्वरूपऽइन्द्रापूष्णोः प्रियमप्येति पाथः ॥२५ ॥
translation: What time they bear before the Courser, covered with trappings and with wealth, the grasped oblation, The dappled goat goeth straightforward, bleating, to the place dear to Indra and to Pûshan.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: एष छागः पुरोऽअश्वेन वाजिना पूष्णो भागो नीयते विश्वदेव्यः। अभिप्रियं यत्पुरोडाशमर्वता त्वष्टेदेनꣳ सौश्रवसाय जिन्वति ॥२६ ॥
translation: Dear to all Gods, this goat, the share of Pûshan, is first led forward with the vigorous Courser, While Tvashtar sends him forward with the Charger, acceptable for sacrifice, to glory.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यद्धविष्यमृतुशो देवयानं त्रिर्मानुषाः पर्यश्वं नयन्ति। अत्रा पूष्णः प्रथमो भागऽएति यज्ञं देवेभ्यः प्रतिवेदयन्नजः ॥२७ ॥
translation: When thrice the men lead round the Steed, in order, who goeth to the Gods as meet oblation, The goat precedeth him, the share of Pûshan, and to the Gods the sacrifice announceth.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होताध्वर्युरावयाऽअग्निमिन्धो ग्रावग्राभऽउत शस्ता सुविप्रः। तेन यज्ञेन स्वरङ्कृतेन स्विष्टेन वक्षणाऽआ पृणध्वम् ॥२८ ॥
translation: Invoker, ministering priest, stoner, fire-kindler, Soma-presser, sage, reciter, With this well ordered sacrifice, well finished, do ye fill full the channels of the rivers.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यूपव्रस्काऽउत ये यूपवाहाश्चषालं येऽअश्वयूपाय तक्षति। ये चार्वते पचनꣳ सम्भरन्त्युतो तेषामभिगूर्त्तिर्नऽइन्वतु ॥२९ ॥
translation: The hewers of the post and those who carry it, and those who carve the knob to deck the Horse’s stake; Those who prepare the cooking-vessels for the Steed,—may the approving help of these promote our work.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उप प्रागात्सुमन्मेऽधायि मन्म देवानामाशाऽउप वीतपृष्ठः। अन्वेनं विप्राऽऋषयो मदन्ति देवानां पुष्टे चकृमा सुबन्धुम् ॥३० ॥
translation: Forth, for the regions of the Gods, the Charger with his smooth back is come; my prayer attends him. In him rejoice the singer and the sages. A good friend have we won for the Gods’ banquet.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यद्वाजिनो दाम सन्दानमर्वतो या शीर्षण्या रशना रज्जुरस्य। यद्वा घास्य प्रभृतमास्ये तृणꣳ सर्वा ता तेऽअपि देवेष्वस्तु ॥३१ ॥
translation: May the fleet Courser’s halter and his heel-ropes, the headstall and the girths and cords about him, And the grass put within his mouth to bait him,—among the Gods, too, let all these be with thee.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यदश्वस्य क्रविषो मक्षिकाश यद्वा स्वरौ स्वधितौ रिप्तमस्ति। यद्धस्तयोः शमितुर्यन्नखेषु सर्वा ता तेऽअपि देवेष्वस्तु ॥३२ ॥
translation: What part of the Steed’s flesh the fly hath eaten, or is left sticking to the post or hatchet, Or to the slayer’s hands and nails adhereth,—among the Gods, tog, may all this he with thee.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यदूवध्यमुदरस्यापवाति यऽआमस्य क्रविषो गन्धोऽअस्ति। सुकृता तच्छमितारः कृण्वन्तूत मेधꣳ शृतपाकं पचन्तु ॥३३ ॥
translation: Food undigested steaming from his belly, and any odour of raw flesh remaining, This let the immolators set in order and dress the sacrifice with perfect cooking.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यत्ते गात्रादग्निना पच्यमानादभि शूलं निहतस्यावधावति। मा तद्भूम्यामाश्रिषन्मा तृणेषु देवेभ्यस्तदुशद्भ्यो रातमस्तु ॥३४ ॥
translation: What from thy body which with fire is roasted, when thou art set upon the spit, distilleth,— Let not that lie on earth or grass neglected, but to the longing Gods let all be offered.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ये वाजिनं परिपश्यन्ति पक्वं यऽईमाहुः सुरभिर्निर्हरेति। ये चार्वतो मासभिक्षामुपासतऽउतो तेषामभिगूर्त्तिर्नऽइन्वतु ॥३५ ॥
translation: They who, observing that the Horse is ready, call out and say, The smell is good; remove it; And, craving meat, await the distribution,—may their approving help promote our labour.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यन्नीक्षणं माँस्पचन्याऽउखाया या पात्राणि यूष्णऽआसेचनानि। ऊष्मण्याऽपिधाना चरूणामङ्काः सूनाः परि भूषन्त्यश्वम् ॥३६ ॥
translation: The trial-fork of the flesh cooking caldron, the vessels out of which the broth is sprinkled, The warming-pots, the covers of the dishes, hooks, carving-boards,—all these attend the Charger.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मा त्वाग्निर्ध्वनयीद् धूमगन्धिर्मोखा भ्राजन्त्यभि विक्त जघ्रिः। इष्टं वीतमभिगूर्त्तं वषट्कृतं तं देवासः प्रति गृभ्णन्त्यश्वम् ॥३७ ॥
translation: Let not the fire, smoke-scented, make thee crackle, nor glowing caldron smell and break to pieces. Offered, beloved, approved, and consecrated,—such Charger do the Gods accept with favour.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: निक्रमणं निषदनं विवर्त्तनं यच्च पड्वीशमर्वतः। यच्च पपौ यच्च घासिं जघास सर्वा ता तेऽअपि देवेष्वस्तु ॥३८ ॥
translation: The starting-place, his place of rest and rolling, the ropes wherewith the Charger’s feet were fastened, The water that he drank, the food he tasted,—among the Gods, too, may all these attend thee.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यदश्वाय वासऽउपस्तृणन्त्यधीवासं या हिरण्यान्यस्मै। सन्दानमर्वन्तं पड्वीशं प्रिया देवेष्वा यामयन्ति ॥३९ ॥
translation: The robe they spread upon the Horse to clothe him, the upper covering and the golden trappings, The halters which restrain the Steed, the heel-ropes,—all these, as grateful to the Gods, they offer.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यत्ते सादे महसा शूकृतस्य पार्ष्ण्या वा कशया वा तुतोद। स्रुचेव ता हविषोऽअध्वरेषु सर्वा ता ते ब्रह्मणा सूदयामि ॥४० ॥
translation: If one, when seated, with excessive urging hath with his heel or with his whip distressed thee, All these thy woes, as with oblation’s ladle at sacrifices, with my prayer I banish. 105
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: चतुस्त्रिꣳशद्वाजिनो देवबन्धोर्वङ्क्रीरश्वस्य स्वधितिः समेति। अच्छिद्रा गात्रा वयुना कृणोतु परुष्परुरनुघुष्या वि शस्त ॥४१ ॥
translation: The four-and-thirty ribs of the swift Courser, kin to the Gods, the slayer’s hatchet pierces. Cut ye with skill so that the parts be flawless, and piece by piece declaring them dissect them.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: एकस्त्वष्टुरश्वस्या विशस्ता द्वा यन्तारा भवतस्तथऽऋतुः। या ते गात्राणामृतुथा कृणोमि ताता पिण्डानां प्र जुहोम्यग्नौ ॥४२ ॥
translation: Of Tvashtar’s Courser there is one dissector: this is the custom: two there are who guide him. Such of his limbs as I divide in order, all these, amid the lumps, in fire I offer.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मा त्वा तपत्प्रियऽआत्मापियन्तं मा स्वधितिस्तन्वऽआ तिष्ठिपत्ते। मा ते गृध्नुरविशस्तातिहाय छिद्रा गात्राण्यसिना मिथू कः ॥४३ ॥
translation: Let not thy dear soul burn thee as thou comest, let not the hatchet linger in thy body. Let not a greedy clumsy immolator, missing the joints, mangle thy limbs unduly.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: न वाऽउऽएतान्म्रियसे न रिष्यसि देवाँ२ऽइदेषि पथिभिः सुगेभिः। हरी ते युञ्जा पृषतीऽअभूतामुपास्थाद् वाजी धुरि रासभस्य ॥४४ ॥
translation: No, here thou diest not, thou art not injured: only by easy paths to Gods thou goest. Both Bays, both Spotted Mares are now thy fellows, and to the Ass’s pole is yoked the Courser.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सुगव्यं नो वाजी स्वश्व्यं पुꣳसः पुत्राँ२ऽउत विश्वापुषꣳ रयिम्। अनागास्त्वं नोऽअदितिः कृणोतु क्षत्रं नोऽअश्वो वनता हविष्मान् ॥४५ ॥
translation: May this Steed bring us all-sustaining riches, wealth in good kine, good horses, manly offspring. Freedom from sin may Aditi vouchsafe us; the Steed with our oblations gain us lordship!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इमा नु कं भुवना सीषधामेन्द्रश्च विश्वे च देवाः। आदित्यैरिन्द्रः सगणो मरुद्भिरस्मभ्यं भेषजा करत्। यज्ञं च नस्तन्वं च प्रजां चादित्यैरिन्द्रः सह सीषधाति ॥४६ ॥
translation: We will, with Indra and all Gods to help us, bring these existing worlds into subjection. With the Âdityas, with the band of Maruts, may Indra give us medicine to heal us. Our sacrifice, our bodies, and our offspring may Indra regulate with the Âdityas.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्ने त्वं नोऽ अन्तमऽउत त्राता शिवो भवा वरूथ्यः। वसुरग्निर्वसुश्रवाऽअच्छा नक्षि द्युमत्तमꣳ रयिं दाः ॥४७ ॥ तं त्वा शोचिष्ठ दीदिवः सुम्नाय नूनमीमहे सखिभ्यः। स नो बोधि श्रुधी हवमुरुष्या णो अघायतः समस्मात्॥४८ ॥
translation: O Agni, be our nearest Friend, etc., as in III. 25. To thee then, O Most Bright, etc., as in III. 26. 106
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्निश्च पृथिवी च सन्नते ते मे सं नमतामदो वायुश्चान्तरिक्षं च सन्नते ते मे सं नमतामदऽ आदित्यश्च द्यौश्च सन्नते ते मे सं नमतामदऽआपश्च वरुणश्च सन्नते ते मे सं नमतामदः। सप्त सꣳसदोऽ अष्टमी भूतसाधनी। सकामाँ२ ॥ऽअध्वनस्कुरु संज्ञानमस्तु मेऽमुना ॥१ ॥
translation: AGNI and Prithivî, closely connected, may they bring low for me the boon I mention. Vâyu and Firmament, closely connected, may they, etc. Closely connected Dyaus and the Âditya, may they, etc. Closely connected Varuna and Waters, may they, etc. Lord of the seven communities and her who forms all beings, eighth, Make our ways full of pleasantness: may So-and-So and I agree.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यथेमां वाचं कल्याणीमावदानि जनेभ्यः। ब्रह्मराजन्याभ्या शूद्राय चार्याय च स्वाय चारणाय च। प्रियो देवानां दक्षिणायै दातुरिह भूयासमयं मे कामः समृध्यतामुप मादो नमतु ॥२ ॥
translation: That I to all the people may address this salutary speech, To priest and nobleman, Sûdra and Arya, to one of our own kin and to the stranger. Dear may I be to Gods and guerdon- giver. Fulfilled be this my hope: be that my portion!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: बृहस्पतेऽअति यदर्योऽअर्हाद् द्युमद्विभाति क्रतुमज्जनेषु। यद्दीदयच्छवसऽ ऋतप्रजात तदस्मासु द्रविणं धेहि चित्रम्। उपयामगृहीतोऽसि बृहस्पतये त्वैष ते योनिर्बृहस्पतये त्वा ॥३ ॥
translation: Give us, Brihaspati, that wondrous treasure, that which exceeds the merit of the foeman, Which shines among the folk effectual, splendid, that, Son of Law, which is with might refulgent. Taken upon a base art thou. Thee for Brihaspati. This is thy home. Thee for Brihaspati,
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इन्द्र गोमन्निहा याहि पिबा सोमꣳ शतक्रतो। विद्यद्भिर्ग्रावभिः सुतम्। उपयामगृहीतोऽसीन्द्राय त्वा गोमतऽएष ते योनिरिन्द्राय त्वा गोमते ॥४ ॥
translation: Come hither, Indra, rich in kine! Drink Soma, Lord of Hundred Powers, Effused by braying pressing-stones. Taken upon a base art thou. Thee for Indra, rich in kine. This is thy home. Thee for Indra, rich in kine.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इन्द्रा याहि वृत्रहन् पिबा सोमꣳ शतक्रतो। गोमद्भिर्ग्रावभिः सुतम्। उपयामगृहीतोऽसीन्द्राय त्वा गोमतऽएष ते योनिरिन्द्राय त्वा गोमते ॥५ ॥
translation: O Indra, Vritra-slayer, come. Drink Soma, Lord of Hundred Powers, Expressed with stones whose wealth is kine. Taken upon a base art thou, etc., as in verse 4.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ऋतावानं वैश्वानरमृतस्य ज्योतिषस्पतिम्। अजस्रं घर्ममीमहे। उपयामगृहीतोऽसि वैश्वानराय त्वैष ते योनिर्वैश्वानराय त्वा ॥६ ॥
translation: Vaisvânara the righteous One, the Lord of sacrifice and light, The heat that wasteth not, we seek. Taken upon a base art thou. Thee for Vaisvânara. This is thy home: thee for Vaisvânara.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वैश्वानरस्य सुमतौ स्याम राजा हि कं भुवनानामभिश्रीः। इतो जातो विश्वमिदं वि चष्टे वैश्वानरो यतते सूर्येण। उपयामगृहीतोऽसि वैश्वानराय त्वैष ते योनिर्वैश्वानराय त्वा ॥७ ॥
translation: Still in Vaisvânara’s grace may we continue: yea, he is King Supreme o’er all things living. Sprung hence to life upon this All he looketh. Vaisvânara hath rivalry with Sûrya. Taken upon a base art thou, etc., as in verse 6.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वैश्वानरो न ऊतयऽआ प्र यातु परावतः। अग्निरुक्थेन वाहसा। उपयामगृहीतोऽसि वैश्वानराय त्वैष ते योनिर्वैश्वानराय त्वा ॥८ ॥
translation: Hitherward come Vaisvânara to succour us from far away, Agni through laud that brings him near! Taken upon a base, etc, as in verse 6.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्निर्ऋषिः पवमानः पाञ्चजन्यः पुरोहितः। तमीमहे महागयम्। उपयामगृहीतोऽस्यग्नये त्वा वर्चसऽएष ते योनिरग्नये त्वा वर्चसे ॥९ ॥
translation: Agni is Pavamâna, Sage, the Tribe-Priest of the Races Five: To him of mighty wealth we pray. Taken upon a base art thou. Thee for lustre. This is thy home. Thee for lustre.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: महाँ२ ॥ऽइन्द्रो वज्रहस्तः षोडशी शर्म यच्छतु। हन्तु पाप्मानं योऽस्मान् द्वेष्टि। उपयामगृहीतोऽसि महेन्द्राय त्वैष ते योनिर्महेन्द्राय त्वा ॥१० ॥
translation: May mighty Indra, thunder-armed, may Shodasî protect us well, and slay the wicked man who hateth us. Taken upon a base art thou. Thee for Mahendra. This is thy home. Thee for Mahendra.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तं वो दस्ममृतीषहं वसोर्मन्दानमन्धसः। अभि वत्सं न स्वसरेषु धेनवऽइन्द्रं गीर्भिर्नवामहे ॥११ ॥
translation: As cows low to their calves in stalls so with our songs we glorify This Indra, e’en your wondrous God who checks assault, who joys in the delicious juice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यद्वाहिष्ठं तदग्नये बृहदर्च विभावसो। महिषीव त्वद्रयिस्त्वद्वाजाऽउदीरते ॥१२ ॥
translation: Agni’s is the most fetching song. Shine mightily, thou rich in light! Like the Chief Consort of a King, riches and strength proceed from thee.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: एह्यू षु ब्रवाणि तेऽग्नऽ इत्थेतरा गिरः। एभिर्वर्द्धासऽइन्दुभिः ॥१३ ॥
translation: Come, here, O Agni, will I sing verily other songs to thee, And with these drops shalt thou grow strong.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ऋतवस्ते यज्ञं वितन्वन्तु मासा रक्षन्तु ते हविः। संवत्सरस्ते यज्ञं दधातु नः प्रजां च परि पातु नः ॥१४ ॥
translation: The Seasons spread thy sacrifice! the Mouths protect thine offering! May the Year guard our sacrifice for thee and keep our children safe.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उपह्वरे गिरीणा सङ्गमे च नदीनाम्। धिया विप्रो अजायत ॥१५ ॥
translation: There where the mountains downward slope, there by the meeting of the streams The sage was manifest with song. 107
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उच्चा ते जातमन्धसो दिवि सद्भूम्याददे। उग्रꣳशर्म महि श्रवः ॥१६ ॥
translation: High is thy juice’s birth: though sat in heaven, on earth it hath obtained Strong sheltering power and great renown.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: स नऽइन्द्राय यज्यवे वरुणाय मरुद्भ्यः। वरिवोवित्परि स्रव ॥१७ ॥
translation: Finder of room and freedom, flow for Indra, meet for worship, flow For Varuna and the Marut host.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: एना विश्वान्यर्यऽआ द्युम्नानि मानुषाणाम्। सिषासन्तो वनामहे ॥१८ ॥
translation: Striving to win, with him we gain all wealth of the ungodly one, Yea, all the glories of mankind.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अनु वीरैरनु पुष्यास्म गोभिरन्वश्वैरनु सर्वेण पुष्टैः। अनु द्विपदाऽनु चतुष्पदा वयं देवा नो यज्ञमृतुथा नयन्तु ॥१९ ॥
translation: May we be prosperous with brave sons, cattle, horses, each wish of ours, and varied blessings, With quadrupeds, and with the men about us. May the Gods guide our sacrifice in season.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्ने पत्नीरिहा वह देवानामुशतीरुप। त्वष्टारꣳ सोमपीतये ॥२० ॥
translation: O Agni, bring thou hitherward the yearning Consorts of the Gods Bring Tvashtar to the Soma-draught.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अभि यज्ञं गृणीहि नो ग्नावो नेष्टः पिबऽऋतुना। त्वहि रत्नधा ऽअसि ॥२१ ॥
translation: O Neshtar girt by Dames, accept our sacrifice: with Ritu drink, For thou art he who giveth wealth.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: द्रविणोदाः पिपीषति जुहोत प्र च तिष्ठत। नेष्ट्रादृतुभिरिष्यत ॥२२ ॥
translation: He with the Ritus fain would drink, Wealth-river, from the Neshtar’s bowl. Begin, pay offerings: hasten ye.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तवायꣳ सोमस्त्वमेह्यर्वाङ् शश्वत्तमꣳ सुमनाऽअस्य पाहि। अस्मिन् यज्ञे बर्हिष्या निषद्या दधिष्वेमं जठरऽइन्दुमिन्द्र ॥२३ ॥
translation: Thine is this Soma: come thou near, approach it. Drink thou thereof, benevolent, and cease not. Sit on the sacred grass at this our worship, and take these drops into thy belly, Indra.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अमेव नः सुहवाऽआ हि गन्तन नि बर्हिषि सदतना रणिष्टन। अथा मदस्व जुजुषाणो ऽअन्धसस्त्वष्टर्देवेभिर्जनिभिः सुमद्गणः ॥२४ ॥
translation: Come unto us, ye swift to listen! as at home, upon the sacred grass sit and enjoy yourselves. And, Tvashtar, well content be joyful in the juice with Gods and Goddesses in gladsome company.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: स्वादिष्ठया मदिष्ठया पवस्व सोम धारया। इन्द्राय पातवे सुतः ॥२५ ॥
translation: In sweetest and most gladdening stream flow pure, O Soma, on thy way, Pressed out for Indra, for his drink.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: रक्षोहा विश्वचर्षणिरभि योनिमयोहते। द्रोणे सधस्थमासदत् ॥२६ ॥
translation: Fiend-queller, Friend of all men, he hath in the vat attained unto His place, his iron- fashioned home. 108
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: समास्त्वाऽग्न ऋतवो वर्द्धयन्तु संवत्सराऽऋषयो यानि सत्या। सं दिव्येन दीदिहि रोचनेन विश्वाऽ आ भाहि प्रदिशश्चतस्रः ॥१ ॥
translation: HALF-YEARS and Seasons strengthen thee, O Agni, the Years and all the Verities and Rishis! Flash forth with thy celestial effulgence: illumine all four regions of the heaven.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सं चेध्यस्वाग्ने प्र च बोधयैनमुच्च तिष्ठ महते सौभगाय। मा च रिषदुपसत्ता तेऽ अग्ने ब्रह्माणस्ते यशसः सन्तु माऽन्ये ॥२ ॥
translation: Kindle thee, Agni, rake this man to knowledge: rise up erect for great and happy fortune. Agni, be those uninjured who adore thee, thy priests be glorious and none beside them!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: त्वामग्ने वृणते ब्राह्मणाऽ इमे शिवोऽ अग्ने संवरणे भवा नः। सपत्नहा नो अभिमातिजिच्च स्वे गये जागृह्यप्रयुच्छन् ॥३ ॥
translation: The Brahmans present here elect thee, Agni: be thou propitious in our sanctuary. Slayer of rivals, Agni, quell our foemen: watch in thy house with care that never ceases.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इहैवाग्नेऽ अधि धारया रयिं मा त्वा निक्रन् पूर्वचितो निकारिणः। क्षत्रमग्ने सुयममस्तु तुभ्यमुपसत्ता वर्द्धतां तेऽअनिष्टृतः ॥४ ॥
translation: Even here do thou, O Agni, stablish wealth: let not oppressors injure thee by thinking of thee first. Light be thy task of ruling, Agni, with thy power: may he who worships thee wax strong, invincible.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: क्षत्रेणाग्ने स्वायुः सꣳरभस्व मित्रेणाग्ने मित्रधेये यतस्व। सजातानां मध्यमस्थाऽ एधि राज्ञामग्ने विहव्यो दीदिहीह ॥५ ॥
translation: Kind to the people, grasp thy power, O Agni: contend thou with the Friend by way of friendship. Placed, Agni, in the centre of our kinsmen, flash forth to be invoked by Kings around thee.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अति निहोऽ अति स्रिधोऽत्यचित्तिमत्यरातिमग्ने। विश्वा ह्यग्ने दुरिता सहस्वाथाऽस्मभ्यꣳ सहवीरा रयिं दाः ॥६ ॥
translation: Past those who slay, past enemies, past thoughtless men, past those who hate,— Yes, Agni, drive away all woe and trouble: vouchsafe us opulence with men about us.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अनाधृष्यो जातवेदाऽ अनिष्टृतो विराडग्ने क्षत्रभृद् दीदिहीह। विश्वाऽ आशाः प्रमुञ्चन् मानुषीर्भियः शिवेभिरद्य परि पाहि नो वृधे ॥७ ॥
translation: Holder of sway, shine here refulgent, Agni! invincible, unconquered Jâtavedas. Light all the regions, chasing human terrors: with happy helps guard us to-day for increase.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: बृहस्पते सवितर्बोधयैनꣳसꣳशितं चित्सन्तरा सꣳशिशाधि। वर्धयैनं महते सौभगाय विश्वऽएनमनु मदन्तु देवाः ॥८ ॥
translation: Brihaspati, Savitar, give this man knowledge: sharpen him thoroughly though already sharpened. To great and high felicity exalt him: in him let all the Gods rejoice and triumph.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अमुत्रभूयादध यद्यमस्य बृहस्पतेऽ अभिशस्तेरमुञ्चः। प्रत्यौहतामश्विना मृत्युमस्माद् देवानामग्ने भिषजा शचीभिः ॥९ ॥
translation: As thou, Brihaspati, from curse hast freed us, from dwelling yonder in the realm of Yama, The Asvins, Leeches of the Gods, O Agni, have chased Death far from us with mighty powers.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उद्वयन्तमसस्परि स्वः पश्यन्तऽ उत्तरम्। देवं देवत्रा सूर्यमगन्म ज्योतिरुत्तमम् ॥१० ॥
translation: Looking upon the loftier light, etc., as in XX. 21.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ऊर्ध्वाऽ अस्य समिधो भवन्त्यूर्ध्वा शुक्रा शोचीष्यग्नेः। द्युमत्तमा सुप्रतीकस्य सूनोः ॥११ ॥
translation: Uplifted are the brands that are his fuel: lofty and brilliant are the flames of Agni, Splendidly bright of the Son fair of aspect.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तनूनपादसुरो विश्ववेदा देवो देवेषु देवः। पथो अनक्तु मध्वा घृतेन ॥१२ ॥
translation: Tanûnapât the Asura, all-possessing, God among Gods, the God with mead and butter shall bedew the paths.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मध्वा यज्ञं नक्षसे प्रीणानो नराशꣳसोऽ अग्ने। सुकृद्देवः सविता विश्ववारः ॥१३ ॥
translation: With mead to sacrifice thou comest, Agni, earnest as friendly- minded Narâsamsa, and Savitar righteous God who brings all blessings.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अच्छायमेति शवसा घृतेनेडानो वह्निर्नमसा। अग्नि स्रुचोऽ अध्वरेषु प्रयत्सु ॥१४ ॥
translation: He cometh hitherward with power and fatness, the luminous, implored with adoration. While rites proceed the ladles move to Agni.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: स यक्षदस्य महिमानमग्नेः सऽर्इं मन्द्रा सुप्रयसः। वसुश्चेतिष्ठो वसुधातमश्च ॥१५ ॥
translation: Let him pay worship to this Agni’s greatness, daintily fed: he verily gives enjoyments: The wisest Vasu he, and best wealth giver.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: द्वारो देवीरन्वस्य विश्वे व्रता ददन्तेऽ अग्नेः। उरुव्यचसो धाम्ना पत्यमानाः ॥१६ ॥
translation: Widely expansive, ruling by foundation, the Doors divine— and, after, all— Preserve this Agni’s holy works.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तेऽअस्य योषणे दिव्ये न योनाऽ उषासानक्ता। इमं यज्ञमवतामध्वरं नः ॥१७ ॥
translation: May Dawn and Night protect—his heavenly Consorts—in a his home this our sacrificial worship.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: दैव्या होताराऽ उर्ध्वमध्वरं नोऽग्नेर्जिह्वामभि गृणीतम्। कृणुतं नः स्विष्टिम् ॥१८ ॥
translation: Ye two celestial Hotars, greet with praises this lofty rite of ours, the tongue of Agni. Cause that our sacrifice be well conducted. 109
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तिस्रो देवीर्बर्हिरेदꣳ सदन्त्विडा सरस्वती भारती। मही गृणाना ॥१९ ॥
translation: Upon this grass three Goddesses be seated, Idâ, Sarasvatî, Bhâratî the Mighty glorified with song.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तन्नस्तुरीपमद्भुतं पुरुक्षु त्वष्टा सुवीर्यम्। रायस्पोषं विष्यतु नाभिमस्मे ॥२० ॥
translation: This our productive wondrous flow may Tvashtar pour down on this man’s kin, and wealth and heroes.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वनस्पतेऽव सृजा रराणस्त्मना देवेषु। अग्निर्हव्यꣳ शमिता सूदयाति ॥२१ ॥
translation: Vanaspatî, presenting of thyself, send God-ward! Let Agni, Immolator, season our oblation.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्ने स्वाहा कृणुहि जातवेदऽ इन्द्राय हव्यम्। विश्वे देवा हविरिदं जुषन्ताम् ॥२२ ॥
translation: Pay sacrifice to Indra, Jâtavedas Agni! with Hail! All Gods accept the gift we offer!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: पीवोऽअन्ना रयिवृधः सुमेधाः श्वेतः सिषक्ति नियुतामभिश्रीः। ते वायवे समनसो वितस्थुर्विश्वेन्नरः स्वपत्यानि चक्रुः ॥२३ ॥
translation: Wise, bright, arranger of his teams, he seeketh men with rich food whose treasures are abundant. They have stood firm of one accord with Vâyu: yea, the men wrought all noble operations.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: राये नु यं जज्ञतू रोदसीमे राये देवी धिषणा धाति देवम्। अध वायुं नियुतः सश्चत स्वाऽ उत श्वेतं वसुधितिं निरेके ॥२४ ॥
translation: The God whom both these worlds brought forth for riches, whom heavenly Dhishanâ for our wealth appointeth— His team of harnessed horses waits on Vâyu and, foremost, on the radiant treasure-holder.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आपो ह यद् बृहतीर्विश्वमायन् गर्भं दधाना जनयन्तीरग्निम्। ततो देवाना समवर्त्ततासुरेकः कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥२५ ॥
translation: What time the mighty waters came containing the universal germ, producing Agni, Thence sprang the Gods’ one spirit into being. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यश्चिदापो महिना पर्यपश्यद् दक्षं दधाना जनयन्तीर्यज्ञम्। यो देवेष्वधि देवऽ एकऽ आसीत् कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥२६ ॥
translation: Who in his might surveyed the floods enclosing productive force and generating Worship, He who is God mid Gods, and none beside him—What God shall we adore with our oblation?
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: प्र याभिर्यासि दाश्वासमच्छा नियुद्भिर्वायविष्टये दुरोणे। नि नो रयिꣳ सुभोजसं युवस्व नि वीरं गव्यमश्व्यं च राधः ॥२७ ॥
translation: The teams wherewith thou seekest him who offers, within his house, O Vâyu, to direct him, Therewith send wealth to us with full enjoyment, a hero son and gifts of kine and horses.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आ नो नियुद्भिः शतिनीभिरध्वरꣳ सहस्रिणीभिरुप याहि यज्ञम्। वायोऽ अस्मिन्त्सवने मादयस्व यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥२८ ॥
translation: With thy yoked teams in hundreds and in thousands come to our sacrifice and solemn worship. O Vâyu, make thee glad at this libation. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नियुत्वान् वायवा गह्ययꣳ शुक्रोऽ अयामि ते। गन्तासि सुन्वतो गृहम् ॥२९ ॥
translation: Drawn by thy team, O Vâyu, come: to thee is offered this, the pure. Thou visitest the presser’s house.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वायो शुक्रोऽ अयामि ते मध्वोऽअग्रं दिविष्टिषु। आ याहि सोमपीतये स्पार्हो देव नियुत्वता ॥३० ॥
translation: Vâyu, the bright is offered thee, best of the meath at holy rites. Come thou to drink the Soma juice, God longed-for, on thy team-drawn car.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वायुरग्रेगा यज्ञप्रीः साकं गन्मनसा यज्ञम्। शिवो नियुद्भिः शिवाभिः ॥३१ ॥
translation: Lover of worship, leader, come Vâyu with thought, to sacrifice, Propitious with propitious teams!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वायो ये ते सहस्रिणो रथासस्तेभिरा गहि। नियुत्वान्त्सोमपीतये ॥३२ ॥
translation: With all the thousand chariots that are thine, O Vâyu, come to us, Team-drawn, to drink the Soma juice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: एकया च दशभिश्च स्वभूते द्वाभ्यामिष्टये विꣳशती च। तिसृभिश्च वहसे त्रिꣳशता च नियुद्भिर्वायविह ता वि मुञ्च ॥३३ ॥
translation: Come thou with one, and ten, O Self-Existent! with two unto the sacrifice, and twenty. Three are the teams and thirty which convey thee. O Vâyu, in this place unyoke thy coursers.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तव वायवृतस्पते त्वष्टुर्जामातरद्भुत। अवास्या वृणीमहे ॥३४ ॥
translation: Wonderful Vâyu, Lord of Truth, thou who art Tvashtar’s Son in-law, Thy saving succour we elect.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अभि त्वा शूर नोनुमोऽदुग्धाऽ इव धेनवः। ईशानमस्य जगतः स्वर्दृशमीशानमिन्द्र तस्थुषः ॥३५ ॥
translation: Like kine unmilked we call aloud, Hero, to thee and sing thy praise, Looker on heavenly light, Lord of this moving world, Lord, Indra! of what moveth not.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: न त्वावाँ २ ॥ऽ अन्यो दिव्यो न पार्थिवो न जातो न जनिष्यते। अश्वायन्तो मघवन्निन्द्र वाजिनो गव्यन्तस्त्वा हवामहे ॥३६ ॥
translation: None other like to thee, of earth or of the heavens, hath been or ever will be born. Desiring horses, Indra, Bounteous Lord! and kine, as men of might we call on thee.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: त्वामिद्धि हवामहे सातौ वाजस्य कारवः। त्वां वृत्रेष्विन्द्र सत्पतिं नरस्त्वां काष्ठास्वर्वतः ॥३७ ॥
translation: That we may win us wealth and power, we poets call on only thee. In war men call on thee, Indra! the hero’s Lord, in the steed’s race-course call on thee. 110
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: स त्वं नश्चित्र वज्रहस्त धृष्णुया मह स्तवानोऽअद्रिवः। गामश्वꣳ रथ्यमिन्द्र संकिर सत्रा वाजं न जिग्युषे ॥३८ ॥
translation: As such, O Wonderful, whose hand holds thunder, praised as mighty, Caster of the Stone! Pour on us boldly, Indra, kine and chariot-steeds ever to be the conqueror’s strength.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: कया नश्चित्रऽ आ भुवदूती सदावृधः सखा। कया शचिष्ठया वृता ॥३९ ॥
translation: What succour will he bring to us, wonderful, ever-prospering Friend? With what most mighty company?
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: कस्त्वा सत्यो मदानां मꣳहिष्ठो मत्सदन्धसः। दृढा चिदारुजे वसु ॥४० ॥
translation: What, genuine and most liberal draught will spirit thee with juice to burst Open e’en strongly-guarded wealth
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अभी षु णः सखीनामविता जरितॄणाम्। शतं भवास्यूतये ॥४१ ॥
translation: Do thou who art protector of us thy friends who praise thee With hundred aids approach us.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यज्ञायज्ञा वोऽअग्नये गिरागिरा च दक्षसे। प्रप्र वयममृतं जातवेदसं प्रियं मित्रं न शꣳसिषम् ॥४२ ॥
translation: Sing to your Agni with each song, at every sacrifice, for strength. Come, let us praise the Wise and Everlasting God even as a well-belovèd Friend.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: पाहि नोऽ अग्नऽ एकया पाह्युत द्वितीयया। पाहि गीर्भिस्तिसृभिरूर्जां पते पाहि चतसृभिर्वसो ॥४३ ॥
translation: Protect us, Agni, through the first, protect us through the second hymn. Protect us through three hymns, O Lord of Power and Might; through four hymns, Vasu! guard thou us.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ऊर्जो नपातꣳस हिनायमस्मयुर्दाशेम हव्यदातये। भुवद्वाजेष्वविता भुवद् वृधऽउत त्राता तनूनाम् ॥४४ ॥
translation: The Son of Strength; for is he not our Friend? Let us serve him for offering our gifts. In battles may he be our help and strengthener, yea, be the saviour of our lives.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: संवत्सरोऽसि परिवत्सरोऽसीदावत्सरोऽसीद्वत्सरोऽसि वत्सरोऽसि। उषसस्ते कल्पन्तामहोरात्रास्ते कल्पन्तामर्द्धमासास्ते कल्पन्तां मासास्ते कल्पन्तामृतवस्ते कल्पन्ता संवत्सरस्ते कल्पताम्। प्रेत्याऽएत्यै सं चाञ्च प्र च सारय। सुपर्णचिदसि तया देवतयाऽङ्गिरस्वद् ध्रुवः सीद ॥४५ ॥
translation: Thou art Samvatsara; thou art Parivatsara; thou art Idâvatsara; thou art Idvatsara; thou art Vatsara. Prosper thy Dawns! Prosper thy Day-and-Nights! Prosper thy Half-months, Months, Seasons, and Years! Combine them for their going and their coming, and send then forward on their ordered courses. In eagle’s shape thou art piled up and layered. With that divinity, Angiras-like, lie steady. 111
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षत्समिधेन्द्रमिडस्पदे नाभा पृथिव्याऽ अधि। दिवो वर्ष्मन्त्समिध्यतऽओजिष्ठश्चर्षणीसहां वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥१ ॥
translation: ON the earth’s centre, at libation’s place let the Priest worship Indra with the kindling-stick. The mightiest of the lords of men is kindled on the height of heaven. Let him enjoy the butter. Hotar, worship.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षत् तनूनपातमूतिभिर्जेतारमपराजितम्। इन्द्रं देवस्वर्विदं पथिभिर्मधुमत्तमैर्नराशꣳसेन तेजसा वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥२ ॥
translation: Him let the Hotar worship, him Tanûnapât with ready aids; the conqueror never overcome, Indra, the God who finds heaven’s light on paths most rich in pleasant sweets, with Narâsamsa all aglow. Let him enjoy, etc., as in verse 1.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षदिडाभिरिन्द्रमीडितमाजुह्वानममर्त्यम्। देवो देवैः सवीर्यो वज्रहस्तः पुरन्दरो वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥३ ॥
translation: With viands let the Hotar worship Indra immortal, praised, receiver of oblations. The God, the equal of the Gods in vigour, the thunder-wielder, breaker-down of castles. Let him enjoy, etc.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षद् बर्हिषीन्द्रं निषद्वरं वृषभं नर्यापसम्। वसुभी रुद्रैरादित्यैः सयुग्भिर्बर्हिरासदद् वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥४ ॥
translation: Let the Priest worship Indra, Bull who sitteth on sacred grass, doer of manly actions. Let him be seated on the grass with Vasus and Rudras and Âdityas for companions. Let him enjoy, etc.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षदोजो न वीर्यꣳ सहो द्वारऽ इन्द्रमवर्द्धयन्। सुप्रायणाऽ अस्मिन् यज्ञे वि श्रयन्तामृतावृधो द्वार इन्द्राय मीढुषे व्यन्त्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥५ ॥
translation: Let the Priest sacrifice. The Doors have strengthened Indra, his force and conquering might and vigour. At this our worship let the Doors be opened, easy to pass, the strengtheners of Order: wide let them open out for bounteous Indra. Let them enjoy, etc.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षदुषेऽ इन्द्रस्य धेनू सुदुघे मातरा मही। सवातरौ न तेजसा वत्समिन्द्रमवर्द्धतां वीतामाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥६ ॥
translation: Let the Priest sacrifice to Night and Morning, the teeming Cows of Indra, Mighty Mothers. Indra their calf with lustre have they strengthened, even as two mothers of a calf in common. Let them enjoy, etc.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षद् दैव्या होतारा भिषजा सखाया हविषेन्द्रं भिषज्यतः। कवी देवौ प्रचेतसाविन्द्राय धत्तऽ इन्द्रियं वीतामाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥७ ॥
translation: Let the Priest worship both the heavenly Hotars, Friends, Leeches, healing Indra with oblation. The sages, Gods preëminent for wisdom bestow on Indra his surpassing power. Let them enjoy, etc.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षत् तिस्रो देवीर्न भेषजं त्रयस्त्रिधातवोऽपसऽ इडा सरस्वती भारती महीः। इन्द्रपत्नीर्हविष्मतीर्व्यन्त्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥८ ॥
translation: Let the Priest offer sacrifice to the three Goddesses and balm. Let the three triple active Ones, let Idâ and Sarasvatî and Bhâratî the mighty Dames, Consorts of Indra, who receive our sacrificial offerings, enjoy the butter, etc.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षत् त्वष्टारमिन्द्रं देवं भिषजꣳसुयजं घृतश्रियम्। पुरुरूपꣳ सुरेतसं मघोनमिन्द्राय त्वष्टा दधदिन्द्रियाणि वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥९ ॥
translation: Let the Priest worship Tvashtar radiant Indra, Physician good at sacrifice, graced with butter, Multiform and prolific, rich and bounteous. Let Tvashtar, giving wondrous powers to Indra, enjoy, etc.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षद् वनस्पतिꣳशमितारꣳ शतक्रतुं धियो जोष्टारमिन्द्रियम्। मध्वा समञ्जन् पथिभिः सुगेभिः स्वदाति यज्ञं मधुना घृतेन वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥१० ॥
translation: Let the Priest worship him, the Forest-Sovran, the Immolator, Lord of Hundred Powers, the lover of the prayer, the friend of Indra. Balming with mead, may he on easy pathways sweeten our sacrifice with savoury butter. Let him enjoy, etc.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षदिन्द्र स्वाहाज्यस्य स्वाहा मेदसः स्वाहा स्तोकाना स्वाहा स्वाहाकृतीना स्वाहा हव्यसूक्तीनाम्। स्वाहा देवाऽ आज्यपा जुषाणाऽ इन्द्रऽ आज्यस्य व्यन्तु होतर्यज ॥११ ॥
translation: Let the Priest offer sacrifice to Indra: with Hail! to Gods of butter; with Hail! to Gods of marrow; with Hail! to Gods of drops; with Hail! to Gods of offerings paid with Svâhâ; with Hail! to Gods of sacrificial hymns.
