All hail! May butter-drinking Gods and Indra rejoicing taste the butter. Hotar, worship.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवं बर्हिरिन्द्रꣳ सुदेवं देवैर्वीरवत् स्तीर्णं वेद्यामवर्द्धयत्। वस्तोर्वृतं प्राक्तोर्भृतꣳ राया बर्हिष्मतोऽत्यगाद् वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वेतु यज ॥१२ ॥
translation: Vigorous, strewn by Gods upon the altar the right Gods’ sacred Grass hath strengthened Indra. Cut in the day, cherished by night it hath surpassed those who have sacrificial Grass with wealth. For gain of riches let him taste. Pay sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवीर्द्वारऽ इन्द्रꣳसङ्घाते वीड्वीर्यामन्नवर्द्धयन्। आ वत्सेन तरुणेन कुमारेण च मीवतापार्वाणꣳ रेणुककाटं नुदन्तां वसुवने वसुधेयस्य व्यन्तु यज ॥१३ ॥
translation: Firm, closely joined, the Doors divine have strengthened Indra in the rite. Pressed by a calf or tender boy may they drive off the courser as he tosses up the sand. For gain of wealth let then enjoy. Pay sacrifice. 112
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवीऽ उषासानक्तेन्द्रं यज्ञे प्रयत्यह्वेताम्। दैवीर्विशः प्रायासिष्टा सुप्रीते सुधिते वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वीतां यज ॥१४ ॥
translation: Morning and Night, the Goddesses, have called on Indra as the rite advanced. May they well-pleased and ordered well make the Celestial Tribes come forth. For gain of wealth let them enjoy. Pay sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवी जोष्ट्री वसुधिती देवमिन्द्रमवर्धताम्। अयाव्यन्याघा द्वेषास्यान्या वक्षद्वसु वार्याणि यजमानाय शिक्षिते वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वीतां यज ॥१५ ॥
translation: Two Goddesses, wealth-givers, kind, have heightened radiant Indra’s strength. One drives away hatreds and sins; the other shall bring the Sacrificer boons and treasure. Instructed, let them both enjoy, for gain of wealth. Pay sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवीऽऊर्जाहुती दुघे सुदुघे पयसेन्द्रमवर्द्धताम्। इषमूर्जमन्या वक्षत्सग्धिꣳ सपीतिमन्या नवेन पूर्वं दयमाने पुराणेन नवमधातामूर्जमूर्जाहुतीऽ ऊर्जयमाने वसु वार्याणि यजमानाय शिक्षिते वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वीतां यज ॥१६ ॥
translation: Bringers of strengthening sacrifice, the Goddesses, the teeming Cows, have prospered Indra with their milk. Let one bring food and energy, the other feast and banqueting. Bringers of strengthening sacrifice, allotting the several portions they have put together old energy with new and new with olden, strengthening boons and treasures for the Sacrificer. Instructed, let them, etc., as in verse 15.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवा दैव्या होतारा देवमिन्द्रमवर्द्धताम्। हताघशꣳसावाभार्ष्टां वसु वार्याणि यजमानाय शिक्षितौ वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वीतां यज ॥१७ ॥
translation: The two Celestial Hotars, Gods, have heightened radiant Indra’s might. Freed from slain sinners these have brought the Sacrificer wealth and boons. Instructed, let them, etc.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवीस्तिस्रस्तिस्रो देवीः पतिमिन्द्रमवर्धयन्। अस्पृक्षद् भारती दिवꣳ रुद्रैर्यज्ञꣳ सरस्वतीडा वसुमती गृहान् वसुवने वसुधेयस्य व्यन्तु यज ॥१८ ॥
translation: Goddesses three, three Goddesses have heightened their Lord Indra’s strength. One, Bhâratî, hath touched the sky, Sarasvatî the sacrifice with Rudras, and, enriched with wealth, Idâ the homesteads of the folk. For gain of wealth let them enjoy. Pay sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवऽइन्द्रो नराशꣳसस्त्रिवरूथस्त्रिबन्धुरो देवमिन्द्रमवर्धयत्। शतेन शितिपृष्ठानामाहितः सहस्रेण प्र वर्त्तते मित्रावरुणेदस्य होत्रमर्हतो बृहस्पति स्तोत्रमश्विनाऽध्वर्यवं वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वेतु यज ॥१९ ॥
translation: The radiant Indra, Praise of Men, thrice-shielding, borne on three car-seats, hath heightened radiant Indra’s strength. Set on a hundred white-backed cows, yea, on a thousand forth he goes. Mitra and Varuna alone deserve to be his Hotar-Priests, Brihaspati his Chanter, and the Asvins his Adhvaryavas. For gain of wealth let him enjoy. Pay sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवो देवैर्वनस्पतिर्हिरण्यपर्णो मधुशाखः सुपिप्पलो देवमिन्द्रमवर्धयत्। दिवमग्रेणास्पृक्षदान्तरिक्षं पृथिवीमदृꣳहीद्वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वेतु यज ॥२० ॥
translation: Vanaspatî, a God with Gods, with golden leaves, sweet boughs, fair fruit, hath heightened radiant Indra’s strength. Sky with his summit hath he touched, and firmament, and stablished earth. For gain of wealth let him enjoy. Pay sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवं बर्हिर्वारितीनां देवमिन्द्रमवर्धयत्। स्वासस्थमिन्द्रेणासन्नमन्या बर्हीष्यभ्यभूद् वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वेतु यज ॥२१ ॥
translation: The grassy robe of water-plants, divine, hath heightened Indra’s strength. This, the fair seat where Indra sits, hath topped all other sacred grass. For gain of wealth let it enjoy. Pay sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवोऽअग्निः स्विष्टकृद्देवमिन्द्रमवर्धयत्। स्विष्टं कुर्वन्त्स्विष्टकृत् स्विष्टमद्य करोतु नो वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वेतु यज ॥२२ ॥
translation: Agni, Fair-offering-maker, bright, hath heightened radiant Indra’s strength. To-day may Svishtakrit, Fair-offering-maker, paying good sacrifice, for us perform it. For gain of wealth let him enjoy. Pay sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्निमद्य होतारमवृणीतायं यजमानः पचन् पक्तीः पचन् पुरोडाशं बध्नन्निन्द्राय च्छागम्। सूपस्थाऽ अद्य देवो वनस्पतिरभवदिन्द्राय च्छागेन। अद्यत्तं मेदस्तः प्रति पचताग्रभीदवीवृधत् पुरोडाशेन त्वामद्य ऋषे ॥२३ ॥
translation: To-day the Sacrificer hath elected—dressing messes of cooked food and a rice-cake, binding a goat for Indra—Agni as his Hotar. To-day divine Vanaspatî hath with a goat served Indra well. He hath eaten from the fat, he hath accepted the cooked food, he hath waxed strong with the rice-cake. Thee, to-day, O Rishi, etc., as in XXI. 61.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षत्समिधानं महद्यशः सुसमिद्धं वरेण्यमग्निमिन्द्रं वयोधसम्। गायत्रीं छन्दऽइन्द्रियं त्र्यविं गां वयो दधद् वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥२४ ॥
translation: Let the Priest worship Agni, Indra, kindled, splendidly kindled, excellent strength-giver, Lending him mighty power, Gâyatrî metre, a cow aged eighteen months, and vital vigour. Let him enjoy the butter. Hotar, worship.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षत्तनूनपातमुद्भिदं यं गर्भमदितिर्दधे शुचिमिन्द्रं वयोधसम्। उष्णिहं छन्दऽ इन्द्रियं दित्यवाहं गां वयो दधद्वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥२५ ॥
translation: Let the Priest serve with sacrifice him who breaks forth, Tanûnapât, the germ which Aditi conceived, pure Indra who bestoweth strength, Bringing him mighty power, the Ushnih metre, an ox of two years old, and vital vigour. Let him enjoy; etc.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षदीडेन्यमीडितं वृत्रहन्तममिडाभिरीड्यꣳ सहः सोममिन्द्रं वयोधसम्। अनुष्टुभं छन्दऽइन्द्रियं पञ्चाविं गां वयो दधद्वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥२६ ॥
translation: Let the Priest sacrifice to Soma, Indra, adorable, adored, best Vritra-slayer, strength-giver, might, to be adored with viands, Bringing him mighty power, Anushtup metre, a cow of thirty months, and vital vigour. Let him enjoy, etc 113
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षत्सुबर्हिषं पूषण्वन्तममर्त्यꣳ सीदन्तं बर्हिषि प्रियेऽमृतेन्द्रं वयोधसम्। बृहतीं छन्दऽइन्द्रियं त्रिवत्सं गां वयो दधद्वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥२७ ॥
translation: Let the Priest worship Indra, strength-bestower, immortal, with fair grass, allied with Pûshan, seated on sacred grass, dear, everlasting, Bringing him mighty power, Brihatî metre, a steer of three years’ age and vital vigour. Let him enjoy, etc.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षद् व्यचस्वतीः सुप्रायणाऽऋतावृधो द्वारो देवीर्हिरण्ययीर्ब्रह्माणमिन्द्रं वयोधसम्। पङ्क्तिं छन्दऽइहेन्द्रियं तुर्यवाहं गां वयो दधद् व्यन्त्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥२८ ॥
translation: Let the Priest worship the wide-opening Portals, easy to pass, divine, Law-strengthening, golden, Indra, the Brahman Priest, the strength-bestower, Bringing him mighty power, the Pankti metre, a bullock four years old, and vital vigour. Let them enjoy the butter. Hotar, worship.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षत्सुपेशसा सुशिल्पे बृहतीऽउभे नक्तोषासा न दर्शते विश्वमिन्द्रं वयोधसम्। त्रिष्टुभं छन्दऽइहेन्द्रियं पष्ठवाहं गां वयो दधद् वीतामाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥२९ ॥
translation: Let the Priest worship lofty Night and Morning, well-decked, of varied hue, lovely to look on, Indra the Universal, strength-bestower, Bringing him mighty power, the Trishtup metre, a bullock four years old, and vital vigour. Let them enjoy the butter. Hotar, worship.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षत्प्रचेतसा देवानामुत्तमं यशो होतारा दैव्या कवी सयुजेन्द्रं वयोधसम्। जगतीं छन्दऽ इन्द्रियमनड्वाहं गां वयो दधद् वीतामाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥३० ॥
translation: Let the Priest worship both celestial Hotars, the Gods’ best glory, sages famed for wisdom, the two companions, Indra strength-bestower, Bringing him mighty power, Jagatî metre, an ox that draws the wain, and vital vigour. Let them enjoy the butter. Hotar, worship.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षत् पेशस्वतीस्तिस्रो देवीर्हिरण्ययीर्भारतीर्बृहतीर्महीः पतिमिन्द्रं वयोधसम्। विराजं छन्दऽइहेन्द्रियं धेनुं गां न वयो दधद् व्यन्त्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥३१ ॥
translation: Let the Priest sacrifice to three well-decorated Goddesses, gold-decked, great, lofty, Bhâratîs, Indra their Lord who giveth strength, Bringing him mighty power, Virâj the metre, and a cow in milk. Let him enjoy the butter. Hotar, worship.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षत् सुरेतसं त्वष्टारं पुष्टिवर्द्धनꣳ रूपाणि बिभ्रतं पृथक् पुष्टिमिन्द्रं वयोधसम्। द्विपदं छन्दऽइन्द्रियमुक्षाणं गां न वयो दधद् वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥३२ ॥
translation: Let the Priest worship Tvashtar the prolific, strengthener of growth, maintaining varied growth and form, Indra who giveth vital force, Bringing him Dvipad metre, mighty power, and an ox full-grown. Let him enjoy the butter. Hotar, sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षद् वनस्पतिꣳ शमितारꣳ शतक्रतुꣳ हिरण्यपर्णमुक्थिनꣳ रशनां बिभ्रतं वशिं भगमिन्द्रं वयोधसम्। ककुभं छन्दऽइहेन्द्रियं वशां वेहतं गां वयो दधद् वेत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥३३ ॥
translation: Let the Priest serve with sacrifice the Forest Lord Vanaspatî, the Immolator, hundred- powered, praise-worthy, golden-leafed, who wears the girdle, loved, the gracious Lord, Indra who gives the strength of life, Giving him Kakup metre, mighty power, a barren, a calf- slipping cow, and vital vigour. Let him enjoy the butter. Hotar, sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: होता यक्षत् स्वाहाकृतीरग्निं गृहपतिं पृथग्वरुणं भेषजं कविं क्षत्रमिन्द्रं वयोधसम्। अतिच्छन्दसं छन्दऽइन्द्रियं बृहदृषभं गां वयो दधद् व्यन्त्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज ॥३४ ॥
translation: Let the Priest offer worship to the Svâhâkriti Goddesses, to Agni Household Lord apart, to Varuna the Leech and Sage. might, Indra who bestoweth strength, Bringing him Atichhandas metre, great and mighty power, a strong bull, his prime, and vital vigour. Let them enjoy the butter. Hotar, sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवं बर्हिर्वयोधसं देवमिन्द्रमवर्धयत्। गायत्र्या छन्दसेन्द्रियं चक्षुरिन्द्रे वयो दधद् वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वेतु यज ॥३५ ॥
translation: The Grass divine hath added might to radiant Indra strength-giver, Laying in Indra wondrous power and sight and strength by Gâyatrî. For gain of wealth let him enjoy the butter. Offer sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवीर्द्वारो वयोधसꣳ शुचिमिन्द्रमवर्धयन्। उष्णिहा छन्दसेन्द्रियं प्राणमिन्द्रे वयो दधद् वसुवने वसुधेयस्य व्यन्तु यज ॥३६ ॥
translation: The Doors divine have magnified bright Indra, who bestoweth strength. With Ushnih laying mighty power in Indra, vital breath and force. For gain of wealth let them enjoy the butter. Offer sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवीऽउषासानक्ता देवमिन्द्रं वयोधसं देवी देवमवर्धताम्। अनुष्टुभा छन्दसेन्द्रियं बलमिन्द्रे वयो दधद् वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वीतां यज ॥३७ ॥
translation: Morning and Night, divine Ones, have strengthened bright Indra, strength-giver, the Goddesses advanced the God, With the Anushtup laying power in Indra, strength and vital force. For gain of wealth let them enjoy. Pay sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवी जोष्ट्री वसुधिती देवमिन्द्रं वयोधसं देवी देवमवर्धताम्। बृहत्या छन्दसेन्द्रिय श्रोत्रमिन्द्रे वयो दधद् वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वीतां यज ॥३८ ॥
translation: Kind, bounteous, and divine, they have strengthened bright Indra, force-giver, the Goddesses advanced the God, Laying in Indra power and force and hearing with the Brihatî. For gain of wealth let them enjoy. Pay sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवीऽऊर्जाहुती दुघे सुदुघे पयसेन्द्रं वयोधसं देवी देवमवर्धताम्। पङ्क्त्या छन्दसेन्द्रियꣳ शुक्रमिन्द्रे वयो दधद् वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वीतां यज ॥३९ ॥
translation: Bringers of strengthening sacrifice, the Goddesses, two teeming cows, have heightened Indra’s power with milk, Laying bright power in Indra with Pankti, and vital energy. For gain of wealth let them enjoy. Pay sacrifice. 114
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवा दैव्या होतारा देवमिन्द्रं वयोधसं देवौ देवमवर्धताम्। त्रिष्टुभा छन्दसेन्द्रियं त्विषिमिन्द्रे वयो दधद् वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वीतां यज ॥४० ॥
translation: The Gods, two heavenly Hotars, have strengthened bright Indra, force-giver, those Gods have magnified the God, With Trishtup giving Indra power, impetuous might, and vital strength. For gain of wealth let them enjoy. Pay sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवीस्तिस्रस्तिस्रो देवीर्वयोधसं पतिमिन्द्रमवर्धयन्। जगत्या छन्दसेन्द्रियꣳ शूषमिन्द्रे वयो दधद् वसुवने वसुधेयस्य व्यन्तु यज ॥४१ ॥
translation: Goddesses three, three Goddesses have heightened their Lord Indra’s strength, his who bestoweth vital force, Laying in Indra power and might and vital strength with Jagatî. For gain of wealth let them enjoy. Pay sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवो नराशꣳसो देवमिन्द्रं वयोधसं देवो देवमवर्द्धयत्। विराजा छन्दसेन्द्रियꣳ रूपमिन्द्रे वयो दधद् वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वेतु यज ॥४२ ॥
translation: The God, the Praise of all men, hath strengthened bright Indra force-giver, the God hath magnified the God, Laying in Indra with Virâj beauty and power and vital force. For gain of wealth let him enjoy. Pay sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवो वनस्पतिर्देवमिन्द्रं वयोधसं देवो देवमवर्धयत्। द्विपदा छन्दसेन्द्रियं भगमिन्द्रे वयो दधद् वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वेतु यज ॥४३ ॥
translation: The God the Forest Sovran hath strengthened bright Indra, force-giver, the God hath magnified the God, With Dvipad storing Indra with fortune and power and vital strength. For gain of wealth let him enjoy. Pay sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवं बर्हिर्वारितीनां देवमिन्द्रं वयोधसं देवं देवमवर्धयत्। ककुभा छन्दसेन्द्रियं यशऽइन्द्रे वयो दधद् वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वेतु यज ॥४४ ॥
translation: The Grass divine of water-plants hath helped bright Indra force-giver, the God hath magnified the God, Laying in Indra mighty power with Kakup, fame and vital strength. For gain of wealth let it enjoy. Pay sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवोऽअग्निः स्विष्टकृद् देवमिन्द्रं वयोधसं देवो देवमवर्धयत्। अतिछन्दसा छन्दसेन्द्रियं क्षत्रमिन्द्रे वयो दधद् वसुधेयस्य वसुवने वेतु यज ॥४५ ॥
translation: Agni, the God who makes fair rites, hath strengthened Indra force-giver, the God hath magnified the God, Laying with Atichhandas power in Indra, sway, and vital strength. For gain of wealth let him enjoy. Pay sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्निमद्य होतारमवृणीतायं यजमानः पचन् पक्तीः पचन् पुरोडाशं बध्नन्निन्द्राय वयोधसे छागम्। सूपस्थाऽअद्य देवो वनस्पतिरभवदिन्द्राय वयोधसे छागेन। अघत्तं मेदस्तः प्रतिपचताऽग्रभीदवीवृधत् पुरोडशेन। त्वामद्यऽऋषे ॥४६ ॥
translation: To-day the Sacrificer hath elected, etc., as in verse 23. To-day divine Vanaspatî, etc. . . . . . . Thee, to-day, O Rishi, etc. . . . . . . 115
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: समिद्धोऽअञ्जन् कृदरं मतीनां घृतमग्ने मधुमत् पिन्वमानः। वाजी वहन् वाजिनं जातवेदो देवानां वक्षि प्रियमा सधस्थम् ॥१ ॥
translation: DECKING the treasure-house of prayers, O Agni, enkindled, pouring forth sweet-tasted butter, Swift-moving, bearing curd, O Jâtavedas, bear what they love to the Gods’ habitation.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: घृतेनाञ्जन्त्सं पथो देवयानान् प्रजानन् वाज्यप्येतु देवान्। अनु त्वा सप्ते प्रदिशः सचन्ता स्वधामस्मै यजमानाय धेहि ॥२ ॥
translation: Balming the paths that lead to heaven with fatness, let the Steed go unto the Gods well- knowing. Courser, the Quarters of the sky attend thee! Bestow thou food upon this Sacrificer.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ईड्यश्चासि वन्द्यश्च वाजिन्नाशुश्चाऽसि मेध्यश्च सप्ते। अग्निष्ट्वा देवैर्वसुभिः सजोषाः प्रीतं वह्निं वहतु जातवेदाः ॥३ ॥
translation: Thou, Steed, art meet for laud and veneration; swift, fit for sacrifice art thou, O Courser. In concert with the Gods and Vasus Agni Omniscient waft thee a contented bearer!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: स्तीर्णं बर्हिः सुष्टरीमा जुषाणोरु पृथु प्रथमानं पृथिव्याम्। देवेभिर्युक्तमदितिः सजोषाः स्योनं कृण्वाना सुविते दधातु ॥४ ॥
translation: Pleased with much Sacred Grass which we have scattered wide spread upon the earth, a pleasant carpet, Joined with the Gods may Aditi, accordant, bestowing bliss award it happy fortune.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: एताऽउ वः सुभगा विश्वरूपा वि पक्षोभिः श्रयमाणाऽउदातैः। ऋष्वाः सतीः कवषाः शुम्भमाना द्वारो देवीः सुप्रायणा भवन्तु ॥५ ॥
translation: May these your Doors divine that wear all colours, auspicious, with uplifted leaves unfolding, Lofty and closely fitted and sonorous, rich in adornment, offer easy passage.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अन्तरा मित्रावरुणा चरन्ती मुखं यज्ञानामभि संविदाने। उषासा वासुहिरण्ये सुशिल्पेऽऋतस्य योनाविह सादयाभि ॥६ ॥
translation: Your two Dawns rich in gold and varied colour, travelling on ‘twixt Varuna and Mitra, Acquainted with the face of sacrifices, I settle here within the home of Order.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: प्रथमा वाꣳसरथिना सुवर्णा देवौ पश्यन्तौ भुवनानि विश्वा। अपिप्रयं चोदना वां मिमाना होतारा ज्योतिः प्रदिशा दिशन्ता ॥७ ॥
translation: Your two chief Hotars have I pleased, bright-coloured, borne on one car, Gods who behold all creatures, Those who prepare your rules and ordinances and make you see the light by their direction.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आदित्यैर्नो भारती वष्टु यज्ञꣳ सरस्वती सह रुद्रैर्नऽआवीत्। इडोपहूता वसुभिः सजोषा यज्ञं नो देवीरमृतेषु धत्त ॥८ ॥
translation: Bhâratî with Âdityas love our worship! Sarasvatî with Rudras be our helper, And Idâ in accord, invoked with Vasus! Goddesses, place our rite among the Immortals.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: त्वष्टा वीरं देवकामं जजान त्वष्टुरर्वा जायतऽआशुरश्वः। त्वष्टेदं विश्वं भुवनं जजान बहोः कर्त्तारमिह यक्षि होतः ॥९ ॥
translation: The God-devoted son Tvashtar produces: from Tvashtar springs to life your fleet-foot Courser. Tvashtar gave being to this All about us. Priest, worship here the mighty work’s achiever.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अश्वो घृतेन त्मन्या समक्तऽउप देवाँ२ऽऋतुशः पाथऽएतु। वनस्पतिर्देवलोकं प्रजानन्नग्निना हव्या स्वदितानि वक्षत् ॥१० ॥
translation: Let the Steed seek his home, and balmed with butter go of himself unto the Gods in season. To the Gods’ world Vanaspatî, well-knowing, bear our oblations which the fire has tasted!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: प्रजापतेस्तपसा वावृधानः सद्यो जातो दधिषे यज्ञमग्ने। स्वाहाकृतेन हविषा पुरोगा याहि साध्या हविरदन्तु देवाः ॥११ ॥
translation: Thou, waxing by Prajâpati’s strong fervour, born quickly, guardest sacrifice, O Agni. With consecrated offering go, preceding, and let the Sâdhyas, Gods, eat our oblation.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यदक्रन्दः प्रथमं जायमानऽउद्यन्त्समुद्रादुत वा पुरीषात्। श्येनस्य पक्षा हरिणस्य बाहूऽउपस्तुत्यं महि जातं तेऽअर्वन् ॥१२ ॥
translation: What time, first springing into life, thou neighedst, proceeding from the sea or cloudy vapour, Limbs of the deer hadst thou, and eagle pinions. O Steed, thy birth is high and must be lauded.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यमेन दत्तं त्रितऽएनमायुनगिन्द्रऽएणं प्रथमोऽअध्यतिष्ठत्। गन्धर्वोऽअस्य रशनामगृभ्णात् सूरादश्वं वसवो निरतष्ट ॥१३ ॥
translation: This Steed, bestowed by Yama, Trita harnessed, and Indra was the first to mount and ride him. His bridle the Gandharva grasped. O Vasus, from out the Sun ye fashioned forth the Courser.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: असि यमोऽअस्यादित्योऽअर्वन्नसि त्रितो गुह्येन व्रतेन। असि सोमेन समया विपृक्तऽआहुस्ते त्रीणि दिवि बन्धनानि ॥१४ ॥
translation: Yama art thou, O Horse; thou art Âditya; Trita art thou by secret operation. From Soma thou art thoroughly divided. They say there are three bonds in heaven that hold thee.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: त्रीणि तऽआहुर्दिवि बन्धनानि त्रीण्यप्सु त्रीण्यन्तः समुद्रे। उतेव मे वरुणश्छन्त्स्यर्वन् यत्रा तऽआहुः परमं जनित्रम् ॥१५ ॥
translation: Three bonds, they say, thou hast in heaven to bind thee, three in the waters, three within the ocean. To me thou seemest Varuna, O Courser, there where they say is thy sublimest birthplace. 116
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इमा ते वाजिन्नवमार्जनानीमा शफाना सनितुर्निधाना। अत्रा ते भद्रा रशनाऽअपश्यमृतस्य याऽअभिरक्षन्ति गोपाः ॥१६ ॥
translation: Here, Courser, are the places where they groomed thee; here are the traces of thy hooves as winner. Here have I seen the auspicious reins that guide thee, which those who guard the holy Law keep safely.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आत्मानं ते मनसारादजानामवो दिवा पतयन्तं पतङ्गम्। शिरोऽअपश्यं पथिभिः सुगेभिररेणुभिर्जेहमानं पतत्त्रि ॥१७ ॥
translation: Thyself from far I recognized in spirit, a Bird that from below flew through the heaven. I saw thy head still soaring, striving upward by paths unsoiled by dust, pleasant to travel.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अत्रा ते रूपमुत्तममपश्यं जिगीषमाणमिषऽआऽपदे गोः। यदा ते मर्त्तोऽअनु भोगमानडादिद् ग्रसिष्ठऽओषधीरजीगः ॥१८ ॥
translation: Here I beheld thy form matchless in beauty, eager to win thee food at the Cow’s station. Whene’er a man brings thee to thine enjoyment, thou swallowest the herbs, most greedy eater.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अनु त्वा रथोऽअनु मर्योऽअर्वन्ननु गावोऽनु भगः कनीनाम्। अनु व्रातासस्तव सख्यमीयुरनु देवा ममिरे वीर्यं ते ॥१९ ॥
translation: After thee, Courser, come the car, the bridegroom, the kine come after, and the charm of maidens. Full companies have followed for thy friendship: the pattern of thy vigour Gods have followed.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: हिरण्यशृङ्गोऽयोऽअस्य पादा मनोजवाऽअवरऽइन्द्रऽआसीत्। देवाऽइदस्य हविरद्यमायन्योऽअर्वन्तं प्रथमोऽअध्यतिष्ठत् ॥२० ॥
translation: His horns are golden and his feet are iron. Less fleet than he, though swift as thought, was Indra. The Gods came only to the oblation-banquet of him who mounted first of all the Courser.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ईर्मान्तासः सिलिकमध्यमासः सꣳशूरणासो दिव्यासोऽअत्याः। हꣳसाऽइव श्रेणिशो यतन्ते यदाक्षिषुर्दिव्यमज्ममश्वाः ॥२१ ॥
translation: Symmetrical in flank, with rounded haunches, mettled like heroes, the celestial Coursers Put forth their strength like swans in lengthened order when they, the Steeds, have reached the heavenly causeway.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तव शरीरं पतयिष्ण्वर्वन्तव चित्तं वातऽइव ध्रजीमान्। तव शृङ्गाणि विष्ठिता पुरुत्रारण्येषु जर्भुराणा चरन्ति ॥२२ ॥
translation: A body formed for flight hast thou, O Charger; swift as the wind in motion is thy spirit. Thy horns are spread abroad in all directions; they move with restless beat in wildernesses.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उप प्रागाच्छसनं वाज्यर्वा देवद्रीचा मनसा दीध्यानः। अजः पुरो नीयते नाभिरस्यानु पश्चात् कवयो यन्ति रेभाः ॥२३ ॥
translation: The strong Steed hath come forward to the slaughter, pondering with a mind directed God- ward. The goat who is his kin is led before him: the sages and the singers follow after.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उप प्रागात् परमं यत्सधस्थमर्वाँ२ऽअच्छा पितरं मातरं च। अद्या देवाञ्जुष्टतमो हि गम्याऽअथाशास्ते दाशुषे वार्याणि ॥२४ ॥
translation: The Steed is come unto the noblest mansion, is come unto his Father and his Mother. This day shall he approach the Gods, most welcome: then he declares good gifts to him who worships.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: समिद्धोऽअद्य मनुषो दुरोणे देवो देवान् यजसि जातवेदः। आ च वह मित्रमहश्चिकित्वान् त्वं दूतः कविरसि प्रचेताः ॥२५ ॥
translation: Thou in the house of man this day enkindled worshippest Gods, a God, O Jâtavedas. Wealthy in friends! observant, bring them hither. Thou art a sapient envoy, full of wisdom.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तनूनपात् पथऽऋतस्य यानान् मध्वा समञ्जन्त्स्वदया सुजिह्व। मन्मानि धीभिरुत यज्ञमृन्धन् देवत्रा च कृणुह्यध्वरं नः ॥२६ ॥
translation: Tanûnapât, fair-tongued, with sweet mead balming the paths and ways of Order, make them pleasant. Convey our sacrifice to heaven, exalting with holy thoughts our hymns of praise and worship.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नराशꣳसस्य महिमानमेषामुप स्तोषाम यजतस्य यज्ञैः। ये सुक्रतवः शुचयो धियन्धाः स्वदन्ति देवाऽउभयानि हव्या ॥२७ ॥
translation: With sacrifice to these we with laudations will honour holy Narâsamsa’s greatness— To these the pure, most wise, the thought-inspirers, Gods who enjoy both sorts of our oblations.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आजुह्वानऽईड्यो वन्द्यश्चायाह्यग्ने वसुभिः सजोषाः। त्वं देवानामसि यह्व होता सऽएनान् यक्षीषितो यजीयान् ॥२८ ॥
translation: Invoked, deserving laud and adoration, O Agni, come accordant with the Vasus. Thou art, O vigorous One, the Gods’ Invoker, so, best of Sacrificers, bring them quickly.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: प्राचीनं बर्हिः प्रदिशा पृथिव्या वस्तोरस्या वृज्यतेऽअग्रेऽअह्नाम्। व्यु प्रथते वितरं वरीयो देवेभ्योऽअदितये स्योनम् ॥२९ ॥
translation: By rule the Sacred Grass is scattered eastward, a robe to clothe the earth when dawns are breaking. Widely it spreads around and far extended, fair for the Gods and bringing peace and freedom.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: व्यचस्वतीरुर्विया वि श्रयन्तां पतिभ्यो न जनयः शुम्भमानाः। देवीर्द्वारो बृहतीर्विश्वमिन्वा देवेभ्यो भवत सुप्रायणाः ॥३० ॥
translation: Let the expansive Doors be widely opened, like wives who deck their beauty for their husbands. Lofty, celestial, all-impelling Portals, admit the Gods and give them easy access.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आ सुष्वयन्ती यजतेऽउपाकेऽउषासानक्ता सदतां नि योनौ। दिव्ये योषणे बृहती सुरुक्मेऽअधि श्रियꣳ शुक्रपिशं दधाने ॥३१ ॥
translation: Pouring sweet dews, let holy Night and Morning, each close to each, be seated at their station— Lofty, celestial Dames, with gold to deck them, assuming all their fair and radiant beauty.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: दैव्या होतारा प्रथमा सुवाचा मिमाना यज्ञं मनुषो यजध्यै। प्रचोदयन्ता विदथेषु कारू प्राचीनं ज्योतिः प्रदिशा दिशन्ता ॥३२ ॥
translation: Come the two chief celestial sweet-voiced Hotars, arranging sacrifice for man to worship, As singers who inspire us in assemblies, showing the eastward light with their direction! 117
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आ नो यज्ञं भारती तूयमेत्विडा मनुष्वदिह चेतयन्ती। तिस्रो देवीर्बर्हिरेद स्योनꣳ सरस्वती स्वपसः सदन्तु ॥३३ ॥
translation: Let Bhâratî come quickly to our worship, and Idâ showing like a human being. So let Sarasvatî and both her fellows, deft Goddesses, on this fair grass be seated.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यऽइमे द्यावापृथिवी जनित्री रूपैरपिꣳशद् भुवनानि विश्वा। तमद्य होतरिषितो यजीयान् देवं त्वष्टारमिह यक्षि विद्वान् ॥३४ ॥
translation: Hotar more skilled in sacrifice, bring hither with speed today God Tvashtar, thou who knowest, Even him who framed these two, the Earth and Heaven, the Parents, with their forms, and every creature.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उपावसृज त्मन्या समञ्जन् देवानां पाथऽऋतुथा हवीꣳषि। वनस्पतिः शमिता देवोऽअग्निः स्वदन्तु हव्यं मधुना घृतेन ॥३५ ॥
translation: Send to our offerings which thyself thou balmest the Companies of Gods in ordered season. Agni, Vanaspatî, the Immolator sweeten our offered gift with mead and butter.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सद्यो जातो व्यमिमीत यज्ञमग्निर्देवानामभवत् पुरोगाः। अस्य होतुः प्रदिश्यृतस्य वाचि स्वाहाकृतꣳ हविरदन्तु देवाः ॥३६ ॥
translation: Agni as soon as he was born made ready the sacrifice and was the Gods’ preceder. May the Gods eat our offering consecrated according to the true Priest’s voice and guidance.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: केतुं कृण्वन्नकेतवे पेशो मर्याऽअपेशसे। समुषद्भिरजायथाः ॥३७ ॥
translation: Thou, making light where no light was, and form, O men! where form was not, Wast born together with the Dawns.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: जीमूतस्येव भवति प्रतीकं यद्वर्मी याति समदामुपस्थे। अनाविद्धया तन्वा जय त्वꣳ स त्वा वर्मणो महिमा पिपर्त्तु ॥३८ ॥
translation: The warrior’s look is like a thunderous rain-cloud’s when, armed with mail, he seeks the lap of battle. Be thou victorious with unwounded body: so let the thickness of thine armour save thee.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: धन्वना गा धन्वनाजिं जयेम धन्वना तीव्राः समदो जयेम। धनुः शत्रोरपकामं कृणोति धन्वना सर्वाः प्रदिशो जयेम ॥३९ ॥
translation: With Bow let us win kine, with Bow the battle, with Bow be victors in our hot encounters. The Bow brings grief and sorrow to the foeman: armed with the Bow may we subdue all regions.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वक्ष्यन्तीवेदा गनीगन्ति कर्णं प्रियꣳ सखायं परिषस्वजाना। योषेव शिङ्क्ते वितताधि धन्वञ्ज्या इयꣳ समने पारयन्ती ॥४० ॥
translation: Close to his ear, as fain to speak, She presses, holding her well-loved Friend in her embraces. Strained on the Bow, She whispers like a woman—this Bow-string that preserves us in the combat.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तेऽआचरन्ती समनेव योषा मातेव पुत्रं बिभृतामुपस्थे। अप शत्रून् विध्यता संविदानेऽआर्त्नीऽइमे विष्फुरन्तीऽअमित्रान् ॥४१ ॥
translation: These, meeting like a woman and her lover, bear, mother-like, their child upon their bosom. May the two Bow-ends, starting swift asunder scatter, in unison, the foes who hate us.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: बह्वीनां पिता बहुरस्य पुत्रश्चिश्चा कृणेति समनावगत्य। इषुधिः सङ्काः पृतनाश्च सर्वाः पृष्ठे निनद्धो जयति प्रसूतः ॥४२ ॥
translation: With many a son, father of many daughters, He clangs and clashes as he goes to battle. Slung on the back, pouring his brood, the Quiver vanquishes all opposing bauds and armies.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: रथे तिष्ठन्नयति वाजिनः पुरो यत्रयत्र कामयते सुषारथिः। अभीशूनां महिमानं पनायत मनः पश्चादनु यच्छन्ति रश्मयः ॥४३ ॥
translation: Upstanding in the Car the skilful Charioteer guides his strong Horses on whitherso’er he will. See and admire the strength of those controlling Reins which from behind declare the will of him who drives
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तीव्रान् घोषान् कृण्वते वृषपाणयोऽश्वा रथेभिः सह वाजयन्तः। अवक्रामन्तः प्रपदैरमित्रान् क्षिणन्ति शत्रूँ१ ॥ऽरनपव्ययन्तः ॥४४ ॥
translation: Horses whose hoofs rain dust are neighing loudly, yoked to the Chariots, showing forth their vigour. With their forefeet descending on the foemen, they, never flinching, trample and destroy them.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: रथवाहनꣳ हविरस्य नाम यत्रायुधं निहितमस्य वर्म। तत्रा रथमुप शग्मꣳ सदेम विश्वाहा वयꣳ सुमनस्यमानाः ॥४५ ॥
translation: Car-bearer is the name of his oblation, whereon are laid his Weapons and his Armour. So let us here, each day that passes, honour the helpful Car with hearts exceeding joyful.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: स्वादुषꣳ सदः पितरो वयोधाः कृच्छ्रेश्रितः शक्तींवन्तो गभीराः। चित्रसेनाऽइषुबलाऽअमृध्राः सतोवीराऽउरवो व्रातसाहाः ॥४६ ॥
translation: In sweet association lived the fathers who gave us life, profound and strong in trouble, Unwearied, armed with shafts and wondrous weapons, free, real heroes, conquerors of armies.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ब्राह्मणासः पितरः सोम्यासः शिवे नो द्यावापृथिवीऽअनेहसा। पूषा नः पातु दुरितादृतावृधो रक्षा माकिर्नोऽअघशꣳसऽईशत ॥४७ ॥
translation: The Brâhmans, and the Fathers meet for Soma draughts, and, graciously inclined, unequalled Heaven and Earth. Guard us from evil, Pûshan! guard us strengtheners of Law! let not the evil-wisher master us.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सुपर्णं वस्ते मृगोऽअस्या दन्तो गोभिः सन्नद्धा पतति प्रसूता। यत्रा नरः सं च वि च द्रवन्ति तत्रास्माभ्यमिषवः शर्म यꣳसन् ॥४८ ॥
translation: Her tooth a deer, dressed in an eagle’s feathers, bound with cow-hide, launched forth, She flieth onward. There where the heroes speed hither and thither, there may the arrows shelter and protect us.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ऋजीते परि वृङ्धि नोऽश्मा भवतु नस्तनूः। सोमोऽअधि ब्रवीतु नोऽदितिः शर्म यच्छतु ॥४९ ॥
translation: Avoid as thou whose flight is straight, and let our bodies be as stone. May Soma kindly speak to us, and Aditi protect us well. 118
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आ जङ्घन्ति सान्वेषां जघनाँ२ऽउप जिघ्नते। अश्वाजनि प्रचेतसोऽश्वान्त्समत्सु चोदय ॥५० ॥
translation: He lays his blows upon their backs, He deals his strokes upon their thighs. Thou Whip who urgest horses, drive sagacious chargers in the fray.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अहिरिव भोगैः पर्येति बाहुँ ज्याया हेतिं परिबाधमानः। हस्तघ्नो विश्वा वयुनानि विद्वान् पुमान् पुमासं परि पातु विश्वतः ॥५१ ॥
translation: It compasses the arm with serpent windings, fending away the friction of the bowstring: So may the Brace, well skilled in all its duties, guard manfully the man from every quarter.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वनस्पते वीड्वङ्गो हि भूयाऽअस्मत्सखा प्रतरणः सुवीरः। गोभिः सन्नद्धोऽअसि वीडयस्वास्थाता ते जयतु जेत्वानि ॥५२ ॥
translation: Lord of the Wood, be firm and strong in body: be, bearing us, a brave victorious hero. Show forth thy strength, compact with straps of leather, and let thy rider win all spoils of battle.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: दिवः पृथिव्याः पर्योजऽउद्भृतं वनस्पतिभ्यः पर्य्याभृतꣳ सहः। अपामोज्मानं परि गोभिरावृतमिन्द्रस्य वज्रꣳ हविषा रथं यज ॥५३ ॥
translation: Its mighty strength was borrowed from the heaven and earth its conquering force was brought from sovrans of the wood. Honour with holy gifts the Car like Indra’s bolt, the Car bound round with straps, the vigour of the floods.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इन्द्रस्य वज्रो मरुतामनीकं मित्रस्य गर्भो वरुणस्य नाभिः। सेमां नो हव्यदातिं जुषाणो देव रथ प्रति हव्या गृभाय ॥५४ ॥
translation: Thou bolt of Indra, Vanguard of the Maruts, close knit to Varuna and Child of Mitra,— As such, accepting gifts which here we offer, receive, O Godlike Chariot, these oblations.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उप श्वासय पृथिवीमुत द्यां पुरुत्रा ते मनुतां विष्ठितं जगत्। स दुन्दुभे सजूरिन्द्रेण देवैर्दूराद् दवीयोऽअप सेध शत्रून् ॥५५ ॥
translation: Send forth thy voice aloud through earth and heaven, and let the world in all its breadth regard thee; O Drum, accordant with the Gods and Indra, drive thou afar, yea, very far, our foemen.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आ क्रन्दय बलमोजो नऽआधा निष्टनिहि दुरिता बाधमानः। अप प्रोथ दुन्दुभे दुच्छुनाऽइतऽइन्द्रस्य मुष्टिरसि वीडयस्व ॥५६ ॥
translation: Thunder out strength and fill us fall of vigour: yea, thunder forth and drive away all dangers. Drive hence, O War-drum, drive away misfortune: thou art the Fist of Indra: show thy firmness.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आमूरज प्रत्यावर्त्तयेमाः केतुमद् दुन्दुभिर्वावदीति। समश्वपर्णाश्चरन्ति नो नरोऽस्माकमिन्द्र रथिनो जयन्तु ॥५७ ॥
translation: Drive hither those, and these again bring hither: the War-drum speaks aloud as battle’s signal. Our heroes, winged with horses, come together. Let our car-warriors, Indra, be triumphant.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आग्नेयः कृष्णग्रीवः सारस्वती मेषी बभ्रुः सौम्यः पौष्णः श्यामः शितिपृष्ठो बार्हस्पत्यः शिल्पो वैश्वदेवऽऐन्द्रोऽरुणो मारुतः कल्माषऽऐन्द्राग्नः सꣳहितोऽधोरामः सावित्रो वारुणः कृष्णऽएकशितिपात्पेत्वः ॥५८ ॥
translation: The black-necked victim belongs to Agni; the ewe to Sarasvatî; the brown victim is Soma’s; the dusky Pûshan’s; the white-backed is Brihaspati’s; the dappled belongs to the All- Gods; the red to Indra; the spotted to the Maruts; the strong-bodied to Indra-Agni; one with white marks below to Savitar; to Varuna a black ram with one white foot
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्नयेऽनीकवते रोहिताञ्जिरनड्वानधोरामौ सावित्रौ पौष्णौ रजतनाभी वैश्वदेवौ पिशङ्गौ तूपरौ मारुतः कल्माषऽआग्नेयः कृष्णोऽजः सारस्वती मेषी वारुणः पेत्वः ॥५९ ॥
translation: To Agni Anîkavân is sacrificed a red-marked ox; two with white spots below are for Savitar; two with silvery navels for Pûshan; two yellow hornless he-goats for the All-Gods; a spotted one for the Maruts; the black-faced he-goat is Agni’s; the ewe is Sarasvatî’s; the ram is Varuna’s.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्नये गायत्राय त्रिवृते राथन्तरायाष्टाकपालऽइन्द्राय त्रैष्टुभाय पञ्चदशाय बार्हतायैकादशकपालो विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यो जागतेभ्यः सप्तदशेभ्यो वैरूपेभ्यो द्वादशकपालो मित्रावरुणाभ्यामानुष्टुभाभ्यामेकविꣳशाभ्यां वैराजाभ्यां पयस्या बृहस्पतये पाङ्क्ताय त्रिणवाय शाक्वराय चरुः सवित्रऽऔष्णिहाय त्रयस्त्रिꣳशाय रैवताय द्वादशकपालः प्राजापत्यश्चरुरदित्यै विष्णुपत्न्यै चरुरग्नये वैश्वानराय द्वादशकपालोऽनुमत्याऽअष्टाकपालः ॥६० ॥
translation: To Agni of the Gâyatrî, of the Trivrit hymn and of the Rathantara Sâman is to be offered a rice-cake on eight potsherds; to Indra of the Trishtup, the Pañchadasa hymn and the Brihat Sâman one on eleven potsherds; to the All-Gods of the Jagatî, the Seventeenfold hymn and the Vairûpa Sâman, one on twelve potsherds; to Mitra-Varuna of the Anushtup, the Ekavimsa hymn, and the Vairâja Sâman, a mess of curdled milk; to Brihaspati of the Pankti metre, the Trinava hymn, and the Sâkvara Sâman, an oblation of rice boded in milk; to Savitar of the Ushnih, the Thirty-threefold hymn, and the Raivata Sâman, a rice-cake on eight potsherds; a mess of boiled rice is to be made for Prajâpati; the same for Vishnu’s Consort Aditi; to Agni Vaisvânara is to be offered a rice-cake on twelve potsherds, and to Anumati one on eight. 119
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देव सवितः प्र सुव यज्ञं प्र सुव यज्ञपतिं भगाय। दिव्यो गन्धर्वः केतपूः केतं नः पुनातु वाचस्पतिर्वाचं नः स्वदतु ॥१ ॥
translation: OUR sacrifice, God Savitar! speed onward: speed to his share the sacrifice’s patron. May the Celestial Gandharva, cleanser of thought and will, make clean our thoughts and wishes. The Lord of Speech sweeten the words we utter!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि। धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात् ॥२ ॥
translation: May we attain that excellent glory of Savitar the God: So may he stimulate our prayers.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: विश्वानि देव सवितर्दुरितानि परा सुव। यद्भद्रं तन्नऽआ सुव ॥३ ॥
translation: Savitar, God, send far away all troubles and calamities, And send us only what is good.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: विभक्तारꣳ हवामहे वसोश्चित्रस्य राधसः। सवितारं नृचक्षसम् ॥४ ॥
translation: We call on him distributer of wondrous bounty and of wealth, On Savitar who looks on men.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ब्रह्मणे ब्राह्मणं क्षत्राय राजन्यं मरुद्भ्यो वैश्यं तपसे शूद्रं तमसे तस्करं नारकाय वीरहणं पाप्मने क्लीबमाक्रयायाऽअयोगूं कामाय पुँश्चलूमतिक्रुष्टाय मागधम् ॥५ ॥
translation: For Brahman (Priesthood) he binds a Brahman to the stake; for Kshatra (Royalty) a Râjanya; for the Maruts a Vaisya; for Penance a Sûdra; for Darkness a robber; for Hell a homicide or a man who has lost his consecrated fire; for Misfortune a eunuch; for Venality an Ayogû; for Kâma a harlot; for Excessive Noise a Mâgadha;
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नृत्ताय सूतं गीताय शैलूषं धर्माय सभाचरं नरिष्ठायै भीमलं नर्माय रेभꣳ हसाय कारिमानन्दाय स्त्रीषखं प्रमदे कुमारीपुत्रं मेधायै रथकारं धैर्य्याय तक्षाणम् ॥६ ॥
translation: For Dance a stable-master; for Song a public dancer; for Duty one who attends court; for Pastime a timid man; for Sport a chatterer; for Laughter an artist; for Pleasure a woman- lover; for Desire a damsel’s son; for Dexterity a car-builder; for Firmness a carpenter;
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तपसे कौलालं मायायै कर्मारꣳ रूपाय मणिकारꣳ शुभे वपꣳ शरव्यायाऽइषुकारꣳ हेत्यै धनुष्कारं कर्मणे ज्याकारं दिष्टाय रज्जुसर्जं मृत्यवे मृगयुमन्तकाय श्वनिनम् ॥७ ॥
translation: For Trouble a potter’s son; for Device an artificer; for Beauty a jeweller; for Welfare a sower; for the Arrow-deity a maker of shafts; for Injury a bowyer; for Action a bowstring- maker; for Fate a rope-maker; for Death a hunter; for the Finisher a dog-leader;
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नदीभ्यः पौञ्जिष्ठमृक्षीकाभ्यो नैषादं पुरुषव्याघ्राय दुर्मदं गन्धर्वाप्सरोभ्यो व्रात्यं प्रयुग्भ्यऽ उन्मत्तꣳ सर्पदेवजनेभ्योऽप्रतिपदमयेभ्यः कितवमीर्यतायाऽअकितवं पिशाचेभ्यो विदलकारीं यातुधानेभ्यः कण्टकीकारीम् ॥८ ॥
translation: For Rivers a fisherman; for Rikshîkâs a Nishâda’s son; for the Man-tiger a madman; for the Gandharvas and Apsarases a Vrâtya; for Motives one demented; for Serpents and Genii an untrustworthy man; for Dice a gambler; for Excitement a non-gambler; for Pisâchas a woman who splits cane; for Yâtudhânas a woman who works in thorns;
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सन्धये जारं गेहायोपपतिमार्त्यै परिवित्तं निर्ऋत्यै परिविविदानमराद्ध्याऽ एदिधिषुः पतिं निष्कृत्यै पेशस्कारी संज्ञानाय स्मरकारीं प्रकामोद्यायोपसदं वर्णायानुरुधं बलायोपदाम् ॥९ ॥
translation: For Rendezvous a lover; for Homestead a paramour; for Trouble an unmarried elder brother; for Nirriti a younger brother who has married before his elder; for Misfortune the husband of a younger sister whose elder sister has not been married; for Representation a woman who embroiders; for Agreement a woman who deals in love-charms; for Garrulity a by-sitter; for Colour an obstinate man; for Strength a yielding man;
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उत्सादेभ्यः कुब्जं प्रमुदे वामनं द्वार्भ्यः स्राम स्वप्नायान्धमधर्माय बधिरं पवित्राय भिषजं प्रज्ञानाय नक्षत्रदर्शमाशिक्षायै प्रश्निनमुपशिक्षायाऽअभिप्रश्निनं मर्यादायै प्रश्नविवाकम् ॥१० ॥
translation: For Interruptions a hunch-back; for Delight a dwarf, for Doors a blear-eyed man; for Sleep a blind man; for Unrighteousness a deaf man; for Purifying Medium a physician; for Insight an astrologer; for Craving for Knowledge an inquisitive man; for Desire of extra Knowledge an extra-inquisitive man; for Moral Law a question solver;
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अर्मेभ्यो हस्तिपं जवायाश्वपं पुष्ट्यै गोपालं वीर्य्यायाविपालं तेजसेऽजपालमिरायै कीनाशं कीलालाय सुराकारं भद्राय गृहपꣳ श्रेयसे वित्तधमाध्यक्ष्यायानुक्षत्तारम् ॥११ ॥
translation: For Eye-diseases an elephant-keeper; for Speed a horse-keeper; for Nourishment a cowherd; for Manliness a shepherd; for Keenness a goatherd; for Refreshment a ploughman; for Sweet Beverage a preparer of Surâ; for Weal a house-guard; for Well-being a possessor of wealth; for Supervision a doorkeeper’s attendant;
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: भायै दार्वाहारं प्रभायाऽअग्न्येधं ब्रध्नस्य विष्टपायाभिषेक्तारं वर्षिष्ठाय नाकाय परिवेष्टारं देवलोकाय पेशितारं मनुष्यलोकाय प्रकरितारꣳ सर्वेभ्यो लोकेभ्यऽउपसेक्तारमवऽऋत्यै वधायोपमन्थितारं मेधाय वासः पल्पूलीं प्रकामाय रजयित्रीम् ॥१२ ॥
translation: For Light a wood-bringer; for Brightness a fire-kindler; for the Sun’s Station a besprinkler; for Highest Heaven a high steward; for the World of Gods a carver; for the World of Men a distributer; for All-Worlds a pourer-out: for Poverty, Affliction a stirrer-up of strife; for Sacrifice a washerwoman; for Delight a female dyer;
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ऋतये स्तेनहृदयं वैरहत्याय पिशुनं विविक्त्यै क्षत्तारमौपद्रष्ट्र्यायानुक्षत्तारं बलायानुचरं भूम्ने परिष्कन्दं प्रियाय प्रियवादिनमरिष्ट्याऽअश्वसादꣳ स्वर्गाय लोकाय भागदुघं वर्षिष्ठाय नाकाय परिवेष्टारम् ॥१३ ॥
translation: For Assault a thievish-hearted man; for Homicide a slanderer; for Discrimination a door- keeper; for Inspection a door-keeper’s attendant; for Strength a servant; for Plenty a running 120 footman; for the Beloved a sweet speaker; for Safety the rider of a horse; for the World of Svarga a dealer-out of portions; for Highest Heaven a high steward;
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मन्यवेऽयस्तापं क्रोधाय निसरं योगाय योक्तारꣳ शोकायाऽभिसर्त्तारं क्षेमाय विमोक्तारमुत्कूलनिकूलेभ्यत्रिष्ठिनं वपुषे मानस्कृतꣳ शीलायाञ्जनीकारीं निर्ऋत्यै कोशकारीं यमायासूम् ॥१४ ॥
translation: For Passion an iron-smelter; for Anger a remover; for Yoking a yoker; for Pain an assailant; for Quiet an unyoker; for Up-hill and Down-hill one who stands on three legs; for Form a conceited man; for Virtue a female ointment-maker; for Nirriti a female scabbard- maker; for Yama a barren woman;
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यमाय यमसूमथर्वभ्योऽवतोका संवत्सराय पर्य्यायिणीं परिवत्सरायाविजाता- मिदावत्सरायातीत्वरीमिद्वत्सरायातिष्कद्वरीं वत्सराय विजर्जरा संवत्सराय पलिक्नीमृभुभ्योऽ जिनसन्धꣳ साध्येभ्यश्चर्मम्नम् ॥१५ ॥
translation: For Yama a mother of twins; for the Atharvans a woman who has miscarried; for the First Year a gad-about; for the Parivatsara one who has not borne a child; for the Idâvatsara one who exceeds; for the Idvatsara one who transgresses; for the Vatsara one who is worn out; for the Samvatsara one with grey hair; for the Ribhus a hide-dresser; for the Sâdhyas a currier;
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सरोभ्यो धैवरमुपस्थावराभ्यो दाशं वैशन्ताभ्यो बैन्दं नड्वलाभ्यः शौष्कलं पाराय मार्गारमवाराय कैवर्त्तं तीर्थेभ्यऽआन्दं विषमेभ्यो मैनाल स्वनेभ्यः पर्णकं गुहाभ्यः किरातꣳ सानुभ्यो जम्भकं पर्वतेभ्यः किम्पूरुषम् ॥१६ ॥
translation: For Lakes a fisherman; for Standing Waters a fisher; for Tank-waters a Nishâda; for Reed- beds a fish-vender; for the Opposite Bank one who gropes for fish; for This Bank a fish- catcher; for Fords an Âuda; for shallows a Mainâla; for Sounds a Bhilla; for Caverns a Kirâta; for Mountain-heights a destructive savage; for Mountains a wild man;
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: बीभत्सायै पौल्कसं वर्णाय हिरण्यकारं तुलायै वाणिजं पश्चादोषाय ग्लाविनं विश्वेभ्यो भूतेभ्यः सिध्मलं भूत्यै जागरणमभूत्यै स्वपनमार्त्यै जनवादिनं व्यृद्ध्याऽअपगल्भꣳ सꣳशराय प्रच्छिदम् ॥१७ ॥
translation: For Abhorrence a Paulkasa; for Colour a goldsmith; for Balance a merchant; for Repentance a sluggard; for All Spirits a leper; for Prosperity a watchful man; for Failure a sleepy man; for Mischief a chatterer; for Misfortune a shameless man; for Undoing one who cuts up into small pieces;
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अक्षराजाय कितवं कृतायादिनवदर्शं त्रेतायै कल्पिनं द्वापरायाधिकल्पिनमास्कन्दाय सभास्थाणुं मृत्यवे गोव्यच्छमन्तकाय गोघातं क्षुधे यो गां विकृन्तन्तं भिक्षमाणऽउप तिष्ठति दुष्कृताय चरकाचार्यं पाप्मने सैलगम् ॥१८ ॥
translation: For the Dice-king a gambler; for the die Krita one who contemplates his adversary’s ill luck, for the Tretâ a gamble-manager; for the Dvâpara a chief manager; for Askanda one who will not leave the gambling-hall; for Mrityu one who approaches cows; for Antaka a Cow- killer; for Hunger one who goes begging to a man who is cutting up a cow; for Misdeed a leader of the Charakas; for Misery a robber;
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: प्रतिश्रुत्कायाऽअर्त्तनं घोषाय भषमन्ताय बहुवादिनमनन्ताय मूकꣳ शब्दायाडम्बराघातं महसे वीणावादं क्रोशाय तूणवध्ममवरस्पराय शङ्खध्मं वनाय वनपमन्यतोऽरण्याय दावपम् ॥१९ ॥
translation: For Echo a reviler; for Noise a snarler; for End a very talkative man; for Endless a mute; for Sound a drummer; for Might a lute-player; for Cry a flute-blower; for Confused Tone a Conch-blower; for the Wood a wood-ranger; for Partly-wooded Land a forest fire guard;
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नर्माय पुँश्चलू हसाय कारिं यादसे शाबल्यां ग्रामण्यं गणकमभिक्रोशकं तान्महसे वीणावादं पाणिघ्नं तूणवध्मं तान्नृत्तायानन्दाय तलवम् ॥२० ॥
translation: For Pastime a harlot; for Laughter a jester; for Lust a woman with spotty skin; for Might these, the head-man of a village, an astrologer, and a watchman; a lute-player; a hand- clapper, a flutist, these for Dance; for Pleasure a musician;
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्नये पीवानं पृथिव्यै पीठसर्पिणं वायवे चाण्डालमन्तरिक्षाय वꣳशनर्तिनं दिवे खलतिꣳ सूर्याय हर्यक्षं नक्षत्रेभ्यः किर्मिरं चन्द्रमसे किलासमह्ने शुक्लं पिङ्गाक्षꣳ रात्र्यै कृष्णं पिङ्गाक्षम् ॥२१ ॥
translation: For Fire a fat man; for Earth a cripple; for Wind a Chândâla; for Mid-Air a pole-dancer; for Sky a bald-head; for the Sun a green-eyed man; for Stars a spotty man; for the Moon a leper; for Day a white yellow-eyed man; for Night a black man with yellow eyes.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अथैतानष्टौ विरूपाना लभतेऽतिदीर्घं चातिह्रस्वं चातिस्थूलं चातिकृशं चातिशुक्लं चातिकृष्णं चातिकुल्वं चातिलोमशं च। अशूद्राऽअब्राह्मणास्ते प्राजापत्याः। मागधः पुँश्चली कितवः क्लीबोऽशूद्राऽअब्राह्मणास्ते प्राजापत्याः ॥२२ ॥
translation: Now he ties up the eight following variform men: one too tall, one too short, one too stout, one too thin, one too white, one too black, one too bald, one too airy. These must be neither Sûdras nor Brâhmans, and must be dedicated to Prajâpati. A minstrel, a harlot, a gambler, and a eunuch—neither of Sûdra nor Brâhman caste—are to be dedicated to Prajâpati. 121
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सहस्रशीर्षा पुरुषः सहस्राक्षः सहस्रपात्। स भूमिꣳ सर्वत स्पृत्वाऽत्यतिष्ठद्दशाङ्गुलम् ॥१ ॥
translation: PURUSHA hath a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet. Pervading earth on every side he fills a space ten fingers broad.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: पुरुषऽएवेदꣳ सर्वं यद्भूतं यच्च भाव्यम्। उतामृतत्वस्येशानो यदन्नेनातिरोहति ॥२ ॥
translation: Purusha is in truth this All, what hath been and what yet shall be; Lord, too, of immortality which waxes greater still by food.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: एतावानस्य महिमातो ज्यायाँश्च पूरुषः। पादोऽस्य विश्वा भूतानि त्रिपादस्यामृतं दिवि ॥३ ॥
translation: So mighty in his grandeur; yea, greater than this is Purusha. All creatures are one fourth of him, three fourths eternal life in heaven.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: त्रिपादूर्ध्व उदैत्पुरुषः पादोऽस्येहाभवत् पुनः। ततो विष्वङ् व्यक्रामत्साशनानशनेऽअभि ॥४ ॥
translation: With three fourths Purusha rose up: one fourth of him again was here. Thence he moved forth to every side over what eats not and what eats.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ततो विराडजायत विराजोऽअधि पूरुषः। स जातोऽअत्यरिच्यत पश्चाद् भूमिमथो पुरः ॥५ ॥
translation: From him Virâj was born; again Purusha from Virâj was born. When born, he spread to west and east beyond the boundaries of earth.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तस्माद्यज्ञात् सर्वहुतः सम्भृतं पृषदाज्यम्। पशूँस्ताँश्चक्रे वायव्यानारण्या ग्राम्याश्च ये ॥६ ॥
translation: From that great General Sacrifice the dripping fat was gathered up. He formed the creatures of the air and animals both wild and tame.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तस्माद्यज्ञात् सर्वहुतऽऋचः सामानि जज्ञिरे। छन्दासि जज्ञिरे तस्माद्यजुस्तस्मादजायत ॥७ ॥
translation: From that great General Sacrifice Richas and Sâma hymns were born: Therefrom were spells and charms produced; the Yajus had its birth from it.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तस्मादश्वाऽअजायन्त ये के चोभयादतः। गावो ह जज्ञिरे तस्मात् तस्माज्जाताऽअजावयः ॥८ ॥
translation: From it were horses born, from it all cattle with two rows of teeth From it were generated kine, from it were goats and sheep produced.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तं यज्ञं बर्हिषि प्रौक्षन् पुरुषं जातमग्रतः। तेन देवाऽअयजन्त साध्याऽऋषयश्च ये ॥९ ॥
translation: They balmed as victim on the grass Purusha born in earliest time. With him the Deities and all Sâdhyas and Rishis sacrificed.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यत्पुरुषं व्यदधुः कतिधा व्यकल्पयन्। मुखं किमस्यासीत् किं बाहू किमूरू पादाऽउच्येते ॥१० ॥
translation: When they divided Purusha how many portions did they make? What was his mouth? what were his arms? what are the names of thighs and feet?
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ब्राह्मणोऽस्य मुखमासीद् बाहू राजन्यः कृतः। ऊरू तदस्य यद्वैश्यः पद्भ्या शूद्रोऽअजायत ॥११ ॥
translation: The Brâhman was his mouth, of both his arms was the Râjanya made. His thighs became the Vaisya, from his feet the Sûdra was produced.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: चन्द्रमा मनसो जातश्चक्षोः सूर्योऽअजायत। श्रोत्राद्वायुश्च प्राणश्च मुखादग्निरजायत ॥१२ ॥
translation: The Moon was gendered from his mind, and from his eye the Sun had birth; Vâyu and Prâna from his ear, and from his mouth was Agni born.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नाभ्याऽआसीदन्तरिक्षꣳ शीर्ष्णो द्यौः समवर्त्तत। पद्भ्यां भूमिर्दिशः श्रोत्रात्तथा लोकाँ२ ॥ऽअकल्पयन् ॥१३ ॥
translation: Forth from his navel came mid-air; the sky was fashioned from his head; Earth from his feet, and from his ear the Quarters. Thus they formed the worlds.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यत्पुरुषेण हविषा देवा यज्ञमतन्वत। वसन्तोऽस्यासीदाज्यं ग्रीष्मऽइध्मः शरद्धविः ॥१४ ॥
translation: When Gods performed the sacrifice with Purusha as offering Spring was the butter, Autumn the oblation, Summer was the wood.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सप्तास्यासन् परिधयस्त्रिः सप्त समिधः कृताः। देवा यद्यज्ञं तन्वानाऽअबध्नन् पुरुषं पशुम् ॥१५ ॥
translation: Then seven were his enclosing-sticks, his kindling-brands were three times seven, When Gods, performing sacrifice, bound as their victim Purusha.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजन्त देवास्तानि धर्माणि प्रथमान्यासन्। ते ह नाकं महिमानः सचन्त यत्र पूर्वे साध्याः सन्ति देवाः ॥१६ ॥
translation: Gods, sacrificing, sacrificed the victim: these were the earliest holy ordinances. The Mighty Ones attained the height of heaven, there where the Sâdhyas, Gods of old, are dwelling.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अद्भ्यः सम्भृतः पृथिव्यै रसाच्च विश्वकर्मणः समवर्त्तताग्रे। तस्य त्वष्टा विदधद् रूपमेति तन्मर्त्यस्य देवत्वमाजानमग्रे ॥१७ ॥
translation: In the beginning he was formed, collected from waters, earth, and Visvakarman’s essence. Fixing the form thereof Tvashtar proceedeth. This was at first the mortal’s birth and godhead.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वेदाहमेतं पुरुषं महान्तमादित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात्। तमेव विदित्वाति मृत्युमेति नान्यः पन्था विद्यतेऽयनाय ॥१८ ॥
translation: I know this mighty Purusha whose colour is like the Sun, beyond the reach of darkness. He only who knows him leaves Death behind him. There is no path save this alone to travel. 122
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: प्रजापतिश्चरति गर्भेऽअन्तरजायमानो बहुधा वि जायते। तस्य योनिं परि पश्यन्ति धीरास्तस्मिन् ह तस्थुर्भुवनानि विश्वा ॥१९ ॥
translation: In the womb moves Prajâpati: he, never becoming born, is born in sundry figures. The wise discern the womb from which he springeth. In him alone stand all existing creatures.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यो देवेभ्यऽआतपति यो देवानां पुरोहितः। पूर्वो यो देवेभ्यो जातो नमो रुचाय ब्राह्मये ॥२० ॥
translation: He who gives light and heat to Gods, first, foremost Agent of the Gods, Born ere the Gods—to him the bright, the holy One, be reverence
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: रुचं ब्राह्मं जनयन्तो देवाऽअग्रे तदब्रुवन्। यस्त्वैवं ब्राह्मणो विद्यात् तस्य देवाऽअसन् वशे ॥२१ ॥
translation: Thus spake the Gods at first, as they begat the bright and holy One: The Brahman who may know thee thus shall have the Gods in his control.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: श्रीश्च ते लक्ष्मीश्च पत्न्यावहोरात्रे पार्श्वे नक्षत्राणि रूपमश्विनौ व्यात्तम्। इष्णन्निषाणामुं मऽइषाण सर्वलोकं मऽइषाण ॥२२ ॥
translation: Beauty and Fortune are thy wives: each side of thee are Day and Night. The constellations are thy form: the Asvins are thine open jaws. Wishing, wish yonder world for me, wish that the Universe be mine. 123
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तदेवाग्निस्तदादित्यस्तद्वायुस्तदु चन्द्रमाः। तदेव शुक्रं तद् ब्रह्म ताऽआपः स प्रजापतिः ॥१ ॥
translation: AGNI is That; the Sun is That; Vâyu and Chandramâs are That. The Bright is That; Brahma is That, those Waters, that Prajâpati.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सर्वे निमेषा जज्ञिरे विद्युतः पुरुषादधि। नैनमूर्द्ध्वं न तिर्य्यञ्चं न मध्ये परि जग्रभत् ॥२ ॥
translation: All twinklings of the eyelid sprang from Purusha, resplendent One. No one hath comprehended him above, across, or in the midst.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: न तस्य प्रतिमाऽअस्ति यस्य नाम महद्यशः। हिरण्यगर्भऽइत्येष मा मा हिꣳसीदित्येषा यस्मान्न जातऽइत्येषः ॥३ ॥
translation: There is no counterpart of him whose glory verily is great. In the beginning rose Hiranyagarbha, etc. Let not him harm me, etc. Than whom there is no other born, etc.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: एषो ह देवः प्रदिशोऽ नु सर्वाः पूर्वो ह जातः सऽ उ गर्भेऽ अन्तः। सऽ एव जातः स जनिष्यमाणः प्रत्यङ् जनास्तिष्ठति सर्वतोमुखः ॥४ ॥
translation: This very God pervadeth all the regions; yea, born aforetime, in the womb he dwelleth. He verily born and to be born hereafter meeteth his offspring, facing all directions.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यस्माज्जातं न पुरा किं चनैव य आबभूव भुवनानि विश्वा। प्रजापतिः प्रजया सꣳरराणस्त्रीणि ज्योतीषि सचते स षोडशी ॥५ ॥
translation: Before whom naught whatever sprang to being; who with his presence aids all living creatures, Prajâpati, rejoicing in his offspring, he, Shodasî, maintains the Three great Lustres.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: येन द्यौरुग्रा पृथिवी च दृढा येन स्व स्तभितं येन नाकः। योऽ अन्तरिक्षे रजसो विमानः कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥६ ॥
translation: By whom the heavens are strong and earth stands firmly, by whom light’s realm and sky- vault are supported; By whom the regions in mid-air were measured. What God shall we adore with our oblation?
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यं क्रन्दसीऽ अवसा तस्तभानेऽ अभ्यैक्षेतां मनसा रेजमाने। यत्राधि सूरऽ उदितो विभाति कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम। आपो ह यद् बृहतीर्यश्चिदापः ॥७ ॥
translation: To whom, supported by his help, two armies embattled look while trembling in their spirit, Where over them the risen Sun is shining. What God shall we adore with our oblation? What time the mighty waters, etc. He in his might surveyed, etc.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वेनस्तत्पश्यन्निहितं गुहा सद्यत्र विश्वं भवत्येकनीडम्। तस्मिन्निदꣳ सं च वि चैति सर्वꣳ सऽ ओतः प्रोतश्च विभूः प्रजासु ॥८ ॥
translation: The Sage beholdeth That mysterious Being wherein this All hath found one only dwelling. Therein unites the Whole, and thence it issues: far-spread it is the warp and woof in creatures.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: प्र तद्वोचेदमृतं नु विद्वान् गन्धर्वो धाम विभृतं गुहा सत्। त्रीणि पदानि निहिता गुहास्य यस्तानि वेद स पितुः पिताऽसत् ॥९ ॥
translation: Knowing Eternity, may the Gandharva declare that station, parted, kept in secret. Three steps thereof in mystery are hidden: he who knows these shall be the father’s father.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: स नो बन्धुर्जनिता स विधाता धामानि वेद भुवनानि विश्वा। यत्र देवाऽ अमृतमानशानास्तृतीये धामन्नध्यैरयन्त ॥१० ॥
translation: He is our kin, our Father and Begetter: he knows all beings and all Ordinances, In whom the Gods obtaining life eternal have risen upward to the third high station.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: परीत्य भूतानि परीत्य लोकान् परीत्य सर्वाः प्रदिशो दिशश्च। उपस्थाय प्रथमजामृतस्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानमभि सं विवेश ॥११ ॥
translation: Having encompassed round existing creatures, the world; and all the Quarters and Mid- quarters, Having approached the first-born Child of Order he with his Self into The Self hath entered.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: परि द्यावापृथिवी सद्यऽ इत्वा परि लोकान् परि दिशः परि स्वः। ऋतस्य तन्तुं विततं विचृत्य तदपश्यत् तदभवत् तदासीत् ॥१२ ॥
translation: Having gone swiftly round the earth and heaven, around the worlds, around the sky, the Quarters, Having spread out the lengthened thread of Order, he views, and he becomes and is That Being.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: सदसस्पतिमद्भुतं प्रियमिन्द्रस्य काम्यम्। सनिं मेधामयासिषꣳ स्वाहा ॥१३ ॥
translation: To the Assembly’s wondrous Lord, to Indra’s lovely Friend who gives Wisdom. have I drawn near in prayer.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यां मेधां देवगणाः पितरश्चोपासते। तया मामद्य मेधयाऽग्ने मेधाविनं कुरु स्वाहा ॥१४ ॥
translation: That wisdom which the Companies of Gods, and Fathers, recognize, Even with that intelligence, O Agni, make me wise to-day. All-hail!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मेधां मे वरुणो ददातु मेधामग्निः प्रजापतिः। मेधामिन्द्रश्च वायुश्च मेधां धाता ददातु मे स्वाहा ॥१५ ॥
translation: Varuna grant me wisdom! grant it Agni and Prajâpati! Wisdom may Indra, Vâyu grant. May the Creator grant it me. All-hail!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इदं मे ब्रह्म च क्षत्रं चोभे श्रियमश्नुताम्। मयि देवा दधतु श्रियमुत्तमां तस्यै ते स्वाहा ॥१६ ॥
translation: Let these the Priests and Nobles both enjoy the splendour that is mine. Best splendour may the Gods bestow on me. To thee, that splendour, hail! 124
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अस्याजरासो दमामरित्राऽअर्चद्धूमासोऽअग्नयः पावकाः। श्वितीचयः श्वात्रासो भुरण्यवो वनर्षदो वायवो न सोमाः ॥१ ॥
translation: His be the fires, eternal, purifying, protectors of our homes, whose smoke is shining, White, waxing in their strength, for ever stirring, and seated in the wood: like winds are Somas.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: हरयो धूमकेतवो वातजूताऽउप द्यवि। यतन्ते वृथगग्नयः ॥२ ॥
translation: Gold-coloured, bannered with the smoke, urged by the wind, aloft to heaven Rise, lightly borne, the flames of fire. Bring to us Mitra-Varuna, bring the Gods to the great sacrifice; Bring them, O Agni, to thine home.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: युक्ष्वा हि देवहूतमाँ२ऽअश्वाँ२ऽअग्ने रथीरिव। नि होता पूर्व्यः सदः ॥४ ॥
translation: Yoke, Agni, as a charioteer, thy steeds who best invoke the Gods: As ancient Hotar take thy seat.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: द्वे विरूपे चरतः स्वर्थेऽअन्यान्या वत्समुप धापयेते। हरिरन्यस्यां भवति स्वधावाञ्छुक्रोऽअन्यस्यां दद्य्शे सुवर्चाः ॥५ ॥
translation: To fair goals travel Two unlike in semblance: each in succession nourishes an infant. One bears a Godlike Babe of golden colour: bright and fair-shining is be with the other.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अयमिह प्रथमो धायि धातृभिर्होता यजिष्ठोऽअध्वरेष्वीड्यः। यमप्नवानो भृगवो विरुरुचुर्वनेषु चित्रं विभ्वं विशेविशे ॥६ ॥
translation: Here by ordainers was this God appointed first Invoker, best at worship, to be praised at rites, Whom Apnavâna and the Bhrigus caused to shine, bright-coloured in the wood, spreading to every house.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: त्रीणि शता त्री सहस्राण्यग्निं त्रिꣳशच्च देवा नव चासपर्यन्। औक्षन् घृतैरस्तृणन् बर्हिरस्माऽआदिद्धोतारं न्यसादयन्त ॥७ ॥
translation: Three times a hundred Gods, and thrice a thousand, and three times ten, and nine have worshipped Agni, For him spread sacred grass, balmed him with butter, and stablished him as Priest and Sacrificer.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मूर्द्धानं दिवोऽअरतिं पृथिव्या वैश्वानरमृतऽआ जातमग्निम्। कविꣳ सम्राजमतिथिं जनानामासन्ना पात्रं जनयन्त देवाः ॥८ ॥
translation: Him, messenger of earth and head of heaven, Agni Vaisvânara, born in holy Order, The Sage, the King, the Guest of men, a vessel fit for their mouths, the Gods have generated.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्निर्वृत्राणि जङ्घनद् द्रविणस्युर्विपन्यया। समिद्धः शुक्रऽआहुतः ॥९ ॥
translation: May Agni slay the foemen,—fain for riches, through the love of song Kindled, bright, served with sacrifice.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: विश्वेभिः सोम्यं मध्वग्नऽइन्द्रेण वायुना। पिबा मित्रस्य धामभिः ॥१० ॥
translation: With the All-Gods, with Indra and with Vâyu drink the Soma mead, O Agni, after Mitra’s laws.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आ यदिषे नृपतिं तेजऽआनट् शुचि रेतो निषिक्तं द्यौरभीके। अग्निः शर्द्धमनवद्यं युवानꣳस्वाध्यं जनयत्सूदयच्च ॥११ ॥
translation: When splendour reached the Lord of men to speed him, down from the heaven was shed the brilliant moisture. Agni brought forth to light and filled with spirit the youthful host benevolent and blameless.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्ने शर्द्ध महते सौभगाय तव द्युम्नान्युत्तमानि सन्तु। सं जास्पत्यꣳ सुयममा कृणुष्व शत्रूयतामभि तिष्ठा महासि ॥१२ ॥
translation: Show thyself strong for mighty bliss, O Agni; most excellent be thine effulgent splendours. Make easy to maintain our household lordship and trample down the might of those who hate us.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: त्वा हि मन्द्रतममर्कशोकैर्ववृमहे महि नः श्रोष्यग्ने। इन्द्रं न त्वा शवसा देवता वायुं पृणन्ति राधसा नृतमाः ॥१३ ॥
translation: We have elected thee as most delightful for thy beams’ glow: hear our great laud, O Agni. The best men praise thee as the peer of Indra in strength, mid Gods, like Vâyu in thy bounty.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: त्वेऽअग्ने स्वाहुत प्रियासः सन्तु सूरयः। यन्तारो ये मघवानो जनानामूर्वान् दयन्त गोनाम् ॥१४ ॥
translation: O Agni who art worshipped well, dear let our princes be to thee, Our wealthy patrons who are governors of men, who part in gifts their stalls of kine.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: श्रुधि श्रुत्कर्ण वह्निभिर्देवैरग्ने सयावभिः। आ सीदन्तु बर्हिषि मित्रोऽअर्य्यमा प्रातर्यावाणोऽअध्वरम् ॥१५ ॥
translation: Hear, Agni who hast ears to hear, with all thy train of escort Gods. Let Mitra, Aryaman, seeking betimes our rite, seat them upon the sacred grass.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: विश्वेषामदितिर्यज्ञियानां विश्वेषामतिथिर्मानुषाणाम्। अग्निर्देवानामवऽआवृणानः सुमृडीको भवतु जातवेदाः ॥१६ ॥
translation: The Freedom of all Gods who merit worship, freely received as Guest in all men’s houses, Agni who hath secured the Gods’ high favour, may he be gracious to us, Jâtavedas.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: महोऽअग्नेः समिधानस्य शर्मण्यनागा मित्रे वरुणे स्वस्तये। श्रेष्ठे स्याम सवितुः सवीमनि तद्देवानामवोऽअद्या वृणीमहे ॥१७ ॥
translation: In great enkindled Agni’s keeping and, for bliss, free from all sin before Mitra and Varuna, May we share Savitar’s best animating help. We crave this gracious favour of the Gods to-day. 125
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आपश्चित्पिप्यु स्तर्यो̫ न गावो नक्षन्नृतं जरितारस्तऽइन्द्र। याहि वायुर्न नियुतो नोऽअच्छा त्वꣳहि धीभिर्दयसे वि वाजान् ॥१८ ॥
translation: Like barren cows, moreover, swelled the waters: singers approached thy holy cult, O Indra. Come thou to us as to his team comes Vâyu. Thou through our solemn hymns bestowest bounty.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: गावऽउपावतावतं मही यज्ञस्य रप्सुदा। उभा कर्णा हिरण्यया ॥१९ ॥
translation: Ye Cows, protect the fount. The two mighty Ones bless the sacrifice. The handles twain are wrought of gold.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यदद्य सूरऽउदितेऽनागा मित्रोऽअर्य्यमा। सुवाति सविता भगः ॥२० ॥
translation: Now when the Sun hath risen to-day may sinless Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, and Savitar speed us forth.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आ सुते सिञ्चत श्रियꣳ रोदस्योरभिश्रियम्। रसा दधीत वृषभम्। तं प्रत्नथा। अयं वेनः ॥२१ ॥
translation: Pour on the juice the ornament which reaches both the heaven and earth; Supply the liquid to the Bull. Thou in the first old time. See, Vena.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आतिष्ठन्तं परि विश्वेऽअभूषञ्छ्रियो वसानश्चरति स्वरोचिः। महत्तद् वृष्णोऽअसुरस्य नामा विश्वरूपोऽअमृतानि तस्थौ ॥२२ ॥
translation: As he was rising up they all revered him: self-luminous he travels, clothed in splendour. That is the Bull’s, the Asura’s lofty nature: he, Omniform, hath reached the eternal waters.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: प्र वो महे मन्दमानायान्धसोऽर्चा विश्वानराय विश्वाभुवे। इन्द्रस्य यस्य सुमखꣳ सहो महि श्रवो नृम्णं च रोदसी सपर्य्यतः ॥२३ ॥
translation: I laud your Mighty One who joyeth in the juice, him who is good to all men, who pervadeth all; Indra whose conquering strength is powerful in war, whose fame and manly vigour Heaven and Earth revere.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: बृहन्निदिध्मऽएषां भूरि शस्तं पृथुः स्वरुः। येषामिन्द्रो युवा सखा ॥२४ ॥
translation: Great is their fuel, strung their laud, wide is their sacrificial post Whose Friend is Indra, ever young.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इन्द्रेहि मत्स्यन्धसो विश्वेभिः सोमपर्वभिः। महाँ२ऽअभिष्टिरोजसा ॥२५ ॥
translation: Come, Indra, and delight thee with the juice at all the Soma feasts, Conqueror, mighty in thy strength.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इन्द्रो वृत्रमवृणोच्छर्द्धनीतिः प्र मायिनाममिनाद्वर्पणीतिः। अहन् व्यꣳसमुशधग्वनेष्वाविर्धेनाऽअकृणोद्राम्याणाम् ॥२६ ॥
translation: Leading his band, Indra encompassed Vritra; weak grew the wily leader of enchanters. He who burns fierce in forests slaughtered Vyamsa, and made the milch-kine of the nights apparent.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: कुतस्त्वमिन्द्र माहिनः सन्नेको यासि सत्पते किं तऽइत्था। सं पृच्छसे समराणः शुभानैर्वोचेस्तन्नो हरिवो यत्तेऽअस्मे। महाँ२ऽ इन्द्रो यऽओजसा। कदा चन स्तरीरसि। कदा चन प्रयुच्छसि ॥२७ ॥
translation: Whence comest thou alone, thou who art mighty, Indra, Lord of the Brave? What is thy purpose? Thou greetest us, encountering us the Bright Ones. Lord of Bay Steeds, say what thou hast against us. Indra, great in his power and might. Ne’er art thou fruitless. Never art thou neglectful.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आ तत्तऽइन्द्रायवः पनन्ताभि यऽऊर्वं गोमन्तं तितृत्सान्। सकृत्स्वं ये पुरुपुत्रां मही सहस्रधारां बृहतीं दुदुक्षन् ॥२८ ॥
translation: Those men extolled that deed of thine, O Indra, those who would fain burst through the stall of cattle, Fain to milk her who bare but once, great, lofty, whose sons are many and her streams a thousand.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इमां ते धियं प्र भरे महो महीमस्य स्तोत्रे धिषणा यत्तऽआनजे। तमुत्सवे च प्रसवे च सासहिमिन्द्रं देवासः शवसामदन्ननु ॥२९ ॥
translation: To thee the Mighty One I bring this mighty hymn, for thy desire hath been gratified by my laud. In Indra, yea, in him victorious through his might, the Gods have joyed at feast and when the Soma flowed.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: विभ्राड् बृहत् पिबतु सोम्यं मध्वायुर्दधद् यज्ञपतावविह्रुतम्। वातजूतो योऽअभिरक्षति त्मना प्रजाः पुपोष पुरुधा वि राजति ॥३० ॥
translation: May the Bright God drink glorious Soma-mingled mead, giving the sacrifice’s lord uninjured life; He who, wind-urged, in person guard our offspring well, hath nourished them with food and shone o’er many a land.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उदु त्यं जातवेदसं देवं वहन्ति केतवः। दृशे विश्वाय सूर्य्यम् ॥३१ ॥
translation: His bright rays bear him up aloft, the God who knoweth all that lives, Sûrya, that all may look on him.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: येना पावक चक्षसा भुरण्यन्तं जनाँ२ऽअनु। त्वं वरुण पश्यसि ॥३२ ॥
translation: Pure Varuna, with that same eye wherewith thou lookest upon one Actively stirring mid the folk—
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: दैव्यावध्वर्यूऽआ गतꣳ रथेन सूर्यत्वचा। मध्वा यज्ञꣳ समञ्जाथे। तं प्रत्नथा। अयं वेनः। चित्रं देवानाम् ॥३३ ॥
translation: Ye two divine Adhvaryus, come hither upon a sun-bright car: Bedew our sacrifice with stead. Thou in the first old time. See, Vena. The brilliant presence.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आ नऽइडाभिर्विदथे सुशस्ति विश्वानरः सविता देवऽएतु। अपि यथा युवानो मत्सथा नो विश्वं जगदभिपित्वे मनीषा ॥३४ ॥
translation: Loved of all men, may Savitar through praises offered as sacred food come to our synod, That ye too, through our hymns, ye ever youthful, may gladden at your visit all our people.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: यदद्य कच्च वृत्रहन्नुदगाऽअभि सूर्य्य। सर्वं तदिन्द्र ते वशे ॥३५ ॥
translation: Whatever, Vritra-slayer! thou Surya hast risen on to-day, That, Indra, all is in thy power. 126
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तरणिर्विश्वदर्शतो ज्योतिष्कृदसि सूर्य्य। विश्वमा भासि रोचनम् ॥३६ ॥
translation: Swift, visible to all art thou, O Sûrya, maker of the light, Illuming all the radiant realm.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तत्सूर्य्यस्य देवत्वं तन्महित्वं मध्या कर्त्तोर्विततꣳ सं जभार। यदेदयुक्त हरितः सधस्थादाद्रात्री वासस्तनुते सिमस्मै ॥३७ ॥
translation: This is the Godhead, this the might of Sûrya: he hath withdrawn what spread o’er work unfinished. When he hath loosed his horses from their station, straight over all Night spreadeth out her garment.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: तन्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याभिचक्षे सूर्य्यो रूपं कृणुते द्योरुपस्थे। अनन्तमन्यद्रुशदस्य पाजः कृष्णमन्यद्धरितः सं भरन्ति ॥३८ ॥
translation: In the sky’s lap the Sun this form assumeth that Varuna and Mitra may behold it. His Bay Steeds well maintain their power eternal, at one time bright, and darksome at another.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: बण्महाँ२ऽअसि सूर्य्य बडादित्य महाँ२असि। महस्ते सतो महिमा पनस्यतेऽद्धा देव महाँ२ऽअसि ॥३९ ॥
translation: Verily, Sûrya, thou art great; truly, Âditya, thou art great. As thou art great indeed thy greatness is admired: yea, verily thou, God, art great.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: बट् सूर्य्य श्रवसा महाँ२ऽअसि सत्रा देव महाँ२ऽअसि। मह्ना देवानामसुर्य्यः पुरोहितो विभु ज्योतिरदाभ्यम् ॥४० ॥
translation: Yea, Sûrya, thou art great in fame: thou, evermore, O God, art great. Thou by thy greatness art the Gods’ Home-Priest, divine, far-spread, unconquerable light.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: श्रायन्तऽइव सूर्य्यं विश्वेदिन्द्रस्य भक्षत। वसूनि जाते जनमानऽओजसा प्रति भागं न दीधिम ॥४१ ॥
translation: Turning, as ‘twere, to meet the Sun, enjoy from Indra all good things. When he who will be horn is born with power we look to treasures as our heritage.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अद्या देवाऽउदिता सूर्य्यस्य निरꣳहसः पिपृता निरवद्यात्। तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहन्तामदितिः सिन्धुः पृथिवीऽउत द्यौः ॥४२ ॥
translation: To-day, ye Gods, when Sûrya hath ascended, deliver us front trouble and dishonour. This boon may Varuna and Mitra grant us, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आ कृष्णेन रजसा वर्त्तमानो निवेशयन्नमृतं मर्त्यं च। हिरण्ययेन सविता रथेना देवो याति भुवनानि पश्यन् ॥४३ ॥
translation: Throughout the dusky firmament advancing, laying to rest the immortal and the mortal, Borne on his golden chariot he cometh, Savitar, God, beholding living creatures.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: प्र वावृजे सुप्रया बर्हिरेषामा विश्पतीव बीरिटऽइयाते। विशामक्तोरुषसः पूर्वहूतौ वायुः पूषा स्वस्तये नियुत्वान् ॥४४ ॥
translation: Soft to the tread the sacred grass is scattered: these go like Kings amid the band around them, At the folk’s early call on Night and Morning,—Vâyu, and Pûshan with his team to bless us.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इन्द्रवायू बृहस्पतिं मित्राग्निं पूषणं भगम्। आदित्यान् मारुतं गणम् ॥४५ ॥
translation: Indra, Vâyu, Brihaspati, Mitra, Agni, Pûshan, Bhaga, Âdityas, and the Marut host.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: वरुणः प्राविता भुवन्मित्रो विश्वाभिरूतिभिः। करतां नः सुराधसः ॥४६ ॥
translation: Be Varuna our chief defence, let Mitra guard us with all aids: Both make us rich exceedingly!
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अधि नऽ इन्द्रैषां विष्णो सजात्यानाम्। इता मरुतोऽ अश्विना। तं प्रत्नथा। अयं वेनः। ये देवासः। आ नऽइडाभिः। विश्वेभिः सोम्यं मधु। ओमासश्चर्षणीधृतः ॥४७ ॥
translation: Regard us, Indra, Vishnu, here, ye Asvins, and the Marut host, us who are kith and kin to you. Thou in the first old time. See, Vena. O ye eleven Gods. Loved of all men, may Savitar. With the All-Gods. Ye Visvedevas who protect.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अग्नऽइन्द्र वरुण मित्र देवाः शर्द्धः प्र यन्त मारुतोत विष्णो। उभा नासत्या रुद्रोऽअध ग्नाः पूषा भगः सरस्वती जुषन्त ॥४८ ॥
translation: O Agni, Indra, Varuna, and Mitra, give, O ye Gods, and Marut host, and Vishnu. May both Nâsatyas, Rudra, heavenly Matrons, Pûshan, Sarasvatî, Bhaga accept us.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इन्द्राग्नी मित्रावरुणादितिꣳ स्वः पृथिवीं द्यां मरुतः पर्वताँ२ऽअपः। हुवे विष्णुं पूषणं ब्रह्मणस्पतिं भगं नु शꣳसꣳ सवितारमूतये ॥४९ ॥
translation: Indra, Agni, Mitra, Varuna, Aditi, the Waters, Mountains, Maruts, Sky, and Earth and Heaven, Vishnu I call, Pûshan and Brahmanaspati, and Bhaga, Samsa, Savitar that they may help.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अस्मे रुद्रा मेहना पर्वतासो वृत्रहत्ये भरहूतौ सजोषाः। यः शꣳसते स्तुवते धायि पज्रऽइन्द्रज्येष्ठाऽअस्माँ२ऽअवन्तु देवाः ॥५० ॥
translation: With us are raining Rudras, clouds accordant in call to battle at the death of Vritra, The strong, assigned to him who sings and praises. May Gods with Indra as their chief protect us.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: अर्वाञ्चोऽअद्या भवता यजत्राऽआ वो हार्दि भयमानो व्ययेयम्। त्राध्वं नो देवा निजुरो वृकस्य त्राध्वं कर्त्तादवपदो यजत्राः ॥५१ ॥
translation: Turn yourselves hitherward this day, ye Holy, that fearing in my heart I may approach you. Protect us, Gods, let not the wolf destroy us. Save us, ye Holy, from the pit and falling.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: विश्वेऽअद्य मरुतो विश्वऽऊती विश्वे भवन्त्वग्नयः समिद्धाः। विश्वे नो देवाऽअवसा गमन्तु विश्वमस्तु द्रविणं वाजोऽअस्मै ॥५२ ॥
translation: This day come all the Maruts, etc., as in XVIII. 31.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: विश्वे देवाः शृणुतेमꣳ हवं मे येऽअन्तरिक्षे यऽउप द्यवि ष्ठ। येऽअग्निजिह्वाऽउत वा यजत्राऽआसद्यास्मिन् बर्हिषि मादयध्वम् ॥५३ ॥
translation: Listen, All-Gods, to this mine invocation, ye who inhabit heaven and air’s mid-region. All ye; O Holy Ones, whose tongue is Agni, seated upon this sacred grass be joyful.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: देवेभ्यो हि प्रथमं यज्ञियेभ्योऽमृतत्वꣳ सुवसि भागमुत्तमम्। आदिद् दामानꣳ सवितर्व्यूर्णुषेऽनूचीना जीविता मानुषेभ्यः ॥५४ ॥
translation: For thou at first producest for the holy Gods the noblest of all portions, immortality. Thereafter as a gift to men, O Savitar, thou openest existence, life succeeding life.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: प्र वायुमच्छा बृहती मनीषा बृहद्रयिं विश्ववारꣳ रथप्राम्। द्युतद्यामा नियुतः पत्यमानः कविः कविमियक्षसि प्रयज्यो ॥५५ ॥
translation: I with a lofty song call hither Vâyu all-bounteous, filler of his car, most wealthy. Thou, Sage, with bright path, Lord of harnessed horses, impetuous, promptly honourest the prudent. 127
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: इन्द्रवायूऽइमे सुताऽउप प्रयोभिरा गतम्। इन्दवो वामुशन्ति हि ॥५६ ॥
translation: These, Indra-Vâyu, have been shed, etc., as in VII. 8.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: मित्रꣳ हुवे पूतदक्षं वरुणं च रिशादसम्। धियं घृताची साधन्ता ॥५७ ॥
translation: Mitra of holy strength I call, and foe-destroying Varuna, Who make the oil-fed rite complete.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: दस्रा युवाकवः सुता नासत्या वृक्तबर्हिषः। आ यातꣳ रुद्रवर्त्तनी ॥ तं प्रत्नथा। अयं वेनः ॥५८ ॥
translation: Nâsatyas, Wonder-workers, yours are these libations with clipt grass. Come ye whose paths are bright with glow.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: विदद्यदी सरमा रुग्णमद्रेर्महि पाथः पूर्व्यꣳ सध्र्यक्कः। अग्रं नयत्सुपद्यक्षराणामच्छा रवं प्रथमा जानती गात् ॥५९ ॥
translation: When Saramâ had, found the mountain’s fissure, that vast and ancient place she plundered thoroughly. In the floods’ van she led them forth, light-footed: she who well knew came first unto their lowing.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: नहि स्पशमविदन्नन्यमस्माद् वैश्वानरात् पुरऽएतारमग्नेः। एमेनमवृधन्नमृताऽअमर्त्यं वैश्वानरं क्षैत्रजित्याय देवाः६० ॥
translation: For nowhere did they find another envoy to lead the way than this Vaisvânara Agni. The Gods immortal strengthened the immortal Vaisvânara to win the land in battle.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उग्रा विघनिना मृधऽइन्द्राग्नी हवामहे। ता नो मृडातऽईदृशे ॥६१ ॥
translation: The strong, dispellers of the foe, Indra and Agni, we invoke: May they be kind to one like me.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: उपास्मै गायता नरः पवमानायेन्दवे। अभि देवाँ२ऽइयक्षते ॥६२ ॥
translation: Sing forth to Indu, O ye men, to him as he is purified, Fain to pay worship to the Gods.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: ये त्वाहिहत्ये मघवन्नवर्द्धन्ये शाम्बरे हरिवो ये गविष्ठौ। ये त्वा नूनमनुमदन्ति विप्राः पिबेन्द्र सोमꣳ सगणो मरुद्भिः ॥६३ ॥
translation: Drink Soma, Indra, handed with the Maruts who, Boon Lord! strengthened thee at Ahi’s slaughter, ‘Gainst Sambara, Lord of Bays! in winning cattle, and now rejoice in thee, the holy singers.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: जनिष्ठाऽउग्रः सहसे तुराय मन्द्रऽओजिष्ठो बहुलाभिमानः। अवर्द्धन्निन्द्रं मरुतश्चिदत्र माता यद्वीरं दधनद्धनिष्ठा ॥६४ ॥
translation: Thou vast born mighty for victorious valour, exulting, strongest, full of pride and courage. There, even there the Maruts strengthened Indra when his most rapid Mother stirred the Hero.
author: Ralph T.H. Griffith

sanskrit: आ तू नऽइन्द्र वृत्रहन्नस्माकमर्द्धमा गहि। महान् महीभिरूतिभिः ॥६५ ॥
